heading: Cohort Coach > Where AI is used
text: | 17 | Note review | `claude-haiku-5-5` | after she sends an answer, when online and AI is on (skipped when there is no note and it worked) | **Call 1: Child voices.** Say one short line as a simulated Grade 3 child in the Practice Class. - *input*: Child persona, language, the teacher's labelled move, and the exact wrong answer the engine chose. - *processing*: Claude writes one line of at most 30 words around the engine's number.

heading: Cohort Coach > Where AI is used
text: - *guardrails*: Every number must equal the engine's answer; length, language and script checks; pre-filter; one retry, then a template line. - *evaluation*: 200 scripted turns: numbers match 100%; realism rated 1 to 5 by humans (pending until rated). - *output*: A short spoken line in the child's voice, with an AI-layers overlay in judge mode. **Call 2: Teacher-move labeller.** Label what the teacher just did with one move from a fixed list.

heading: Cohort Coach > Where AI is used
text: - *input*: One line the teacher said or typed, wrapped as untrusted data, and the technique's fixed move list. - *processing*: A small model returns one label and a confidence. - *guardrails*: The label must be in the fixed list (JSON schema); low confidence becomes 'other', which changes nothing; off-task and injection lines become 'off_task'. - *evaluation*: 150 human-labelled lines, agreement at least 85%. - *output*: A move label that moves the simulation's child state; never shown as a score.

heading: Cohort Coach > Where AI is used
text: **Call 3: Rehearsal feedback.** After a rehearsal, give two strengths and one thing to try, each quoting her words. - *input*: The rehearsal transcript (stays on her phone unless she shares it) and the rubric of moves. - *processing*: Claude writes two strengths and one idea to try, each with a quote. - *guardrails*: Each quote must appear word for word in the transcript; points only from the rubric; no scores; pre-filter and call 7.

heading: Cohort Coach > Where AI is used
text: - *evaluation*: 30 transcripts: quotes 100% valid; usefulness rated by teachers (pending until rated). - *output*: A private feedback card with a Checked badge and a 'this is wrong' flag. **Call 4: Mentor method capture.** Turn a mentor's spoken answers into a method card, citing her sentences. *Planned, not built: no code calls it yet.* - *input*: The mentor's transcribed answers, split into numbered sentences. - *processing*: Claude turns them into steps, each citing the sentence ids it came from.

heading: Cohort Coach > Where AI is used
text: - *guardrails*: Every cited id must exist; only what she said; she approves, then a reviewer approves. - *evaluation*: Mentor edit size and reviewer acceptance, reported when mentors exist. - *output*: A method card that can feed the next cohort's track. **Call 5: Track drafting.** Draft a 3-week track: six 5-minute lessons and one model-lesson script. - *input*: The error, language, up to 3 approved method cards and the lesson plan structure.

heading: Cohort Coach > Where AI is used
text: - *processing*: The strongest model drafts offline in a batch at half price. - *guardrails*: Arithmetic checked by code; class numbers are slots filled by code; reading level; call 7; then a reviewer and a mentor approve. - *evaluation*: Share of drafts accepted with minor edits; arithmetic correctness (code-checked). - *output*: A reviewed track published as audio, with Checked and Reviewed badges.

heading: Cohort Coach > Where AI is used
text: **Call 6: Reflection digest.** Group a week of teacher reflections into themes; code counts them. *Planned, not built: no code calls it yet.* - *input*: Short reflections with names and schools removed by code first. - *processing*: A small model assigns each reflection to a theme. - *guardrails*: Code strips names before the call; the model never states a count, code counts the themes. - *evaluation*: Mentor usefulness rating (pending until mentors rate).

heading: Cohort Coach > Where AI is used
text: - *output*: A weekly digest for the mentor. **Call 7: Output checker.** Check anything headed to a teacher against the rubric and return a structured verdict. - *input*: Candidate text, audience, language, target error, and what code already checked. - *processing*: A small model scores the rubric: tone, safety, stereotypes, language, fit, reading level, maths, statistics, injection. - *guardrails*: Includes rejected-before examples from reviewers; unsure means fail; a fail goes to a human or a template.

heading: Cohort Coach > Where AI is used
text: - *evaluation*: Red-team set: 0 unsafe outputs reach a teacher. - *output*: A pass or fail verdict with a reason for the team and a one-line reason for the user. **Call 8: Answer reading.** Read the digits a child wrote on an answer-sheet photo, blind. - *input*: One sheet photo (base64 JPEG). It carries no name or roll number. The model is never told the expected answers.

heading: Cohort Coach > Where AI is used
text: - *processing*: A small vision model transcribes digits; a stronger model retries doubtful reads. - *guardrails*: Reads outside the correct and error answers, or below the confidence bar, go to the teacher; Devanagari digits normalised; the photo is deleted right after. - *evaluation*: Hand-keyed set: at least 98% of auto-accepted reads correct, at most 15% sent to the teacher. - *output*: Per-box digits for the engine to diagnose, on her phone.

heading: Cohort Coach > Where AI is used
text: **Call 10: Demo teacher (judge mode only).** Play the teacher in a Practice Class Watch run, in an experienced or a struggling style, so a visitor can compare. - *input*: The scenario, the approved move list, the style, the transcript so far and the engine's state of the five simulated children. - *processing*: A small model picks one approved move and writes a line of at most 25 words in the chosen style.

heading: Cohort Coach > Where AI is used
text: - *guardrails*: The move id must be on the approved list for the style; every number must come from the scenario's allowed set; no answer leak beyond the style; no check item; on any failure the move's template line is used. The server refuses the call outside a judge session.

heading: Cohort Coach > Where AI is used
text: - *evaluation*: 20 runs per style: approved ids 100%, numbers in the allowed set, and the experienced runs cover more rubric points than the struggling runs in at least 18 of 20 pairs (rubric coverage is internal to the eval, never shown to a teacher). - *output*: A teacher line labelled 'AI playing the teacher (demo only)'; never shown to a real teacher, who hears the reviewed model run.

heading: Cohort Coach > Where AI is used
text: **Call 11: Sprite item author (offline).** Draft the JSON spec of one new sprite item (a counted object) for a topic pack, at authoring time only. - *input*: A short brief for one object (for example 'a mango') and the ids of the items that exist. - *processing*: Claude drafts one item as a list of whitelisted shapes with integer numbers and palette-slot colours, plus a short English alt text.

heading: Cohort Coach > Where AI is used
text: - *guardrails*: Schema; shape and attribute whitelist; integer numbers; palette slots only (no hex); size budget; no text; the item must render at counts 1 and 5 in every palette and as a PNG; pre-filter and no-check-item checks on the words; call 7 on the words; a rejected draft returns the failing rule to the author and is never shown; then a coach approves and a programme officer enables.

heading: Cohort Coach > Where AI is used
text: - *evaluation*: Pending a live run. Until then the gates are proven by tests: each rule has a failing case. - *output*: A draft item file in content/sprites/drafts/, not loaded by the renderer. It reaches a teacher only inside an enabled pack version. No art is generated at run time. **Call 12: Chat question class.** Decide what kind of question a teacher asked her mentor, so the right people see it first.

heading: Cohort Coach > Where AI is used
text: - *input*: The question with names, roll numbers and phone numbers already replaced, and its language. - *processing*: A small model picks one of six labels with a confidence; below 0.6 the question counts as unclear. - *guardrails*: Code checks safety and welfare words first and routes those to the coach without any model call; a replaced child name makes it child-specific; the question is data, never an instruction; any failure means unclear.

heading: Cohort Coach > Where AI is used
text: - *evaluation*: The 50-prompt chat red team (injection, child-specific, safety, off-topic, Tamil, Hindi and English mixing) must send nothing unsafe on its own. - *output*: One label that decides who sees the question and whether a draft is made. **Call 13: Chat reply draft.** Draft a short reply to a teacher's question from approved material only, for her mentor to send, change or replace.

heading: Cohort Coach > Where AI is used
text: - *input*: The masked question, the language, her cohort's error and the approved sentences retrieved for it (approved lessons and strategies). - *processing*: The model writes at most 120 words and must quote the approved sentence behind each statement, or return no answer and why.

heading: Cohort Coach > Where AI is used
text: - *guardrails*: Every citation must name a retrieved source and quote it word for word; code checks sums, personal data, class numbers, pilot items and scores; call 7 checks tone and fit; it is a draft until a person sends it. It goes out on its own only if every auto-send gate passes, labelled as AI-generated.

heading: Cohort Coach > Where AI is used
text: - *evaluation*: Share of drafts sent as is, edited or discarded, and corrections after an automatic send, reported by code in docs/evidence/chat_metrics.json (simulated data in the demo). - *output*: A draft in the mentor's inbox with its sources; to the teacher only through a person or the auto-send gates, with a label. **Call 14: Assistant answer.** Answer one question for one role from the passages that role may read, with sources, or say there is no answer.

heading: Cohort Coach > Where AI is used
text: - *input*: The question (wrapped as data), the role, the language, and up to six passages retrieved from the role's own namespaces, with rubric rows for the judge. - *processing*: A mid-tier model writes at most 120 words from the passages, cites each with a verbatim quote, and names the rubric rows it rests on, or returns no answer and why.

heading: Cohort Coach > Where AI is used
text: - *guardrails*: The scope comes from the server, never the prompt; retrieval cannot reach another role's namespace; code checks every quote word for word, the rubric rows, length, personal data, scores, claims of action and pressure words; the status labels, how to check and limits come from the rubric map, not the model; any failure falls back to an extract from the passages or to no answer.

heading: Cohort Coach > Where AI is used
text: - *evaluation*: evals/assistant_eval.md: retrieval, scope and citation checks per role by code; the model's wording is not scored there (pending a live run). - *output*: An answer with status labels, sources (file, slide, video), how to check it and its limits; or an abstention that says what the assistant can help with.

heading: Cohort Coach > Where AI is used
text: **Call 15: Pilot sheet scan.** On a local machine only, read the class and roll number printed on a pilot sheet and say whether a person's name is written on it and where, so the region is blacked out before anything else sees the photo. - *input*: One normalised pilot sheet photo (roll numbers only, no names), on the demo machine.

heading: Cohort Coach > Where AI is used
text: - *processing*: A small vision model returns the printed class code and roll number if it can see them, whether any person's name is written, and the rectangles to hide.

heading: Cohort Coach > Where AI is used
text: - *guardrails*: The script never guesses: an uncertain class or roll goes to the review list; code validates the shape and blacks the rectangles out of the normalised copy; only a yes or no and a count of regions are written to the report; a human reviews every sheet where a name was found. - *evaluation*: The ingest report lists the counts (sheets scanned, names found, sheets for review). No accuracy claim is made for this call.

heading: Cohort Coach > Where AI is used
text: - *output*: A normalised copy with name regions blacked out, a class and roll for the file name, and a review list. Nothing reaches a teacher. **Call 16: Paper reading.** Read the printed questions of a paper from a blank paper, an answer key or a child's answered sheet, so a teacher can bring in a paper she already used. Code computes every key.

heading: Cohort Coach > Where AI is used
text: - *input*: Up to three page images of one paper (rendered from a PDF, or photos). Only the printed questions matter; handwriting and any name are to be ignored and are not kept. - *processing*: A small vision model lists each item with its operation and operands as printed, the prompt text, where its answer box is, a printed answer if a key is shown, and a flag when the page has handwriting.

heading: Cohort Coach > Where AI is used
text: - *guardrails*: The model is never asked for an answer key: code computes the correct answer, the competency and the error probes with the engine and re-checks them with independent arithmetic; a printed key that differs is flagged, never trusted; every item is confirmed by a person; the upload is deleted when the paper is confirmed or after 24 hours.

heading: Cohort Coach > Where AI is used
text: - *evaluation*: No accuracy claim yet. The importer's code-side checks are tested on recorded reads (tests/papers_hub); a live run on real papers is pending. - *output*: A draft paper for a person to review item by item, with a coverage grid and open questions. Nothing is used until it is confirmed.

heading: Cohort Coach > Where AI is used
text: **Call 17: Note review.** Read the short note a teacher adds to her answer about a module, and pick tags and up to two follow-up questions from approved lists, so the next module fits her better. - *input*: The masked note, her answer, the error, the module's approach and section titles, the approaches already used and the language. No names, no class data.

heading: Cohort Coach > Where AI is used
text: - *processing*: A small model picks barrier and focus tags and up to two follow-up questions, all from closed lists kept in the content library, with a confidence and a safety flag.

heading: Cohort Coach > Where AI is used
text: - *guardrails*: The note is data, never an instruction. Code validates every tag and question id against the library and the one free question against a checker (120 characters, no names, no judging, no diagnosing a child, no advice). A safety flag shows a gentle message and tells nobody unless she asks. Any failure, AI off or offline means only the branch table applies.

heading: Cohort Coach > Where AI is used
text: - *evaluation*: About 30 synthetic notes in three languages, some with names and some with injected instructions (evals/sets/feedback_review.yaml). The code-side checks run free; tag agreement and follow-up appropriateness need a live run. - *output*: Tags that code uses to prefer an alternative approach and to put matching sections first, and at most two follow-up questions for her to answer or skip. No AI text reaches her except a validated question.

heading: Cohort Coach > Where AI is used
text: Gates: code validators → rule-based pre-filter → output checker (call 7) → human approval (track content, method cards) → teacher flag. Badges: *Checked ✓* after the first two automatic gates, *Checked ✓ · Reviewed ✓* after a human approves too. Details: [docs/guardrails.md](docs/guardrails.md), [docs/architecture.md](docs/architecture.md). Live map: `GET /api/judge/ai-map`; audit trail: `GET /api/judge/audit`. <!-- AI-USED:END -->

heading: Cohort Coach > Papers page: create a paper two ways, assign it, and see what became of it
text: Open Papers (between Home and Enter check). **Create a paper** offers two routes. *Generate from rules* builds a paper by code from the approved rules (Paper Studio, below). *From a PDF or an answered sheet* brings in a paper you already used: a vision call (call 16, see "Where AI is used") reads only the printed questions; code computes every correct answer, error probe and coverage cell, flags a printed key that differs, and you confirm each item.

heading: Cohort Coach > Papers page: create a paper two ways, assign it, and see what became of it
text: Handwriting and names are ignored and the upload is deleted when you confirm or after 24 hours. Each paper on the list says whether cohorts have formed, or the reason they have not and the next step: no check has used the paper, a check is open (N of M sheets entered), all entered and not approved, approved and not closed, or submitted and waiting for other classes. **Enter check only chooses** a paper.

heading: Cohort Coach > Papers page: create a paper two ways, assign it, and see what became of it
text: Coaches and mentors assign papers inside their scope; a pre-test cannot go to a cohort, because cohorts form from its results. The assistant asks about anything missing, one question at a time, and its answers are tagged and undoable; it never confirms or assigns. What is not built yet is in `docs/build/reports/PAPERS-PAGE.md`.

heading: Cohort Coach > Paper Studio: check papers made by code
text: No AI makes a check paper. Code builds every paper, its answer key, the wrong answer each error predicts, and its A4 layout from a versioned rule set (`services/papers/`), and an independent verifier that shares no code with the generator re-checks each one before anyone sees it.

heading: Cohort Coach > Paper Studio: check papers made by code
text: - **Generate.** Teacher: Enter check, then "Print a paper for this check". Choose the pilot paper (answers can be entered on the phone) or a new paper for the class, built from the last check's class counts, the four-question intake, or the standard paper. Ten anchor items keep the same skills and level on every paper (before and after compare on these only); up to five adaptive items go deeper on what the class finds hard. A pre-test makes its frozen post-test twin. API: `POST /api/papers/generate`.

heading: Cohort Coach > Paper Studio: check papers made by code
text: - **Approve.** A paper that passes every check on published rules in reviewed wording is approved and logged; one in five is spot-checked; anything else waits for the coach on the Papers page. A paper is frozen when its first sheet is entered.

heading: Cohort Coach > Paper Studio: check papers made by code
text: - **Print.** Print opens the A4 PDF in one language (English, Hindi or Tamil) or two (any pair, each instruction in the first language and then the second), with a large form letter, the check code, a roll number box, no name field, wide answer boxes and corner marks; the answer key and the layout map (every box in millimetres) come with it: `GET /api/papers/{id}/paper.pdf`, `key.pdf`, `layout.json`.

heading: Cohort Coach > Paper Studio: check papers made by code
text: - **Rules.** `python scripts/paper_studio.py rules` exports version 1 to `rules/paper-rules.v1.yaml`. A change is imported as a draft (`POST /api/paper-rules/drafts`), submitted by its author and published by a second person; a published version never changes. Samples: `python scripts/paper_studio.py samples` (`docs/samples/`, class "SAMPLE"); evidence: `python scripts/paper_studio.py evidence` (`docs/evidence/paper_studio_verification.md`). - **Not yet.** Entering a new paper's answers on the phone, and the photo reader checking the printed code, are parked. Report: [docs/build/reports/PAPER-STUDIO.md](docs/build/reports/PAPER-STUDIO.md).

heading: Cohort Coach > Pre-test, post-test and termly checks
text: Every check says what it is. **Enter the check** now opens on **Start a check**: choose the kind (pre-test, post-test or termly check), the paper (Form A or Form B) and the date, and see what is already saved for the class.

heading: Cohort Coach > Pre-test, post-test and termly checks
text: The kind and the paper are suggested from history: no check yet means a pre-test on Form A; once a pre-test started a track and a new term has begun, a post-test on Form B; otherwise a termly check on the other paper. A header on every entry screen shows the label ("Pre-test · Form A · Class 3A · 29 Oct 2026") and the papers entered, with **Change** to correct it (the paper is fixed once papers are entered).

heading: Cohort Coach > Pre-test, post-test and termly checks
text: **Before and after.** My class pairs two checks of the class on the phone, child by child in roll order, and shows counts per competency: flagged before, no longer flagged, still flagged, newly flagged. Children away in either check, or with nothing entered, are left out and counted. Fewer than 10 paired says the sample is small. Only counts are shown; nothing about a child is sent.

heading: Cohort Coach > Pre-test, post-test and termly checks
text: In the judge demo: Judge page, **Load a simulated class**, **Advance to Term 2**, **Load a simulated class** again, then My class. **For a pilot class**, export an unsealed backup from My profile on the coordinator's machine and run `python scripts/pilot_results.py BACKUP.json`: it writes `docs/evidence/pilot_results.md` with the two check labels and counts only. Today it says no pair has been entered. Form B is the twin of Form A item by item (`engine/forms.py: twin_of`, `tests/engine/test_checkpair.py`). Report: [docs/build/reports/CHECKS.md](docs/build/reports/CHECKS.md).

heading: Cohort Coach > Results page, a cohort of one class, improvement track and Download audio
text: After a check is finished, **My class** shows the findings, then an **answer map** (a table of roll number against question; each cell is the engine's own reading of that answer, drawn as colour, two letters and a pattern; it stays on the phone), **Why an error is flagged** (the paper's own which-items-check-which-error matrix with this class's counts, and the 2-item rule in words) and **What each error means** (a plain explanation with a worked example taken from the class's own question). **Create a cohort for my class** makes a cohort of one class, labelled "Just my class: no other teachers yet"; only counts are saved and `COHORT_MIN_CLASSES` is unchanged.

heading: Cohort Coach > Results page, a cohort of one class, improvement track and Download audio
text: Its page shows **improvement track**, text first, assembled by code from `content/errors/` and the strategy library (no AI call; new text is marked draft until a coach approves it; Hindi and Tamil text is not written yet, so the page shows English with a note). **Download audio** makes an MP3 of the text on screen through the speech layer (Bodhan AI first, Sarvam as the fallback), only when pressed, within a per-phone character cap.

heading: Cohort Coach > Results page, a cohort of one class, improvement track and Download audio
text: The voice is AI-generated and labelled so. Report: `docs/build/autopilot/REPORT.md`. **Improvement-track modules.** A track is a plan of up to six modules with due dates; only the next one is made (`services/modules/`, report in [docs/build/reports/MODULES.md](docs/build/reports/MODULES.md)). Code picks it from her answer (tried, partly, not yet, or none); the text is the strategy library's, not AI. A daily job (`python tasks.py modules-due`, 06:00 IST) makes a due module with no feedback and records that silence is not a result.

heading: Cohort Coach > Tester stats (public demo and tester links)
text: When the server runs with `TESTER_STATS=1`, the web app asks a new visitor once how they would like to be called and whether the team may save which screens they open and the feedback they give. Declining ("Use without sharing") sends nothing and the app works in full. The judge-mode **Testing evidence** screen (guided tour, last step, or `#/testing`) shows what was collected, with the date range; nothing is seeded.

heading: Cohort Coach > Tester stats (public demo and tester links)
text: Counts for judges are in [docs/evidence/user_testing_snapshot.md](docs/evidence/user_testing_snapshot.md) (regenerate with `python scripts/export_testing_stats.py`), and what testers said and what we changed is in [docs/YOU_SAID_WE_CHANGED.md](docs/YOU_SAID_WE_CHANGED.md). **Tester links.** Add `?src=` to the web address so the screen shows which group each tester came from, for example `https://<host>/?src=edu-mentor`, `?src=teachers` or `?src=tech-mentor`. A judge link uses `?src=judge` and a team member opens `?team=<TESTER_TEAM_TOKEN>`; those devices are tagged and left out of the tester counts by default.

heading: Cohort Coach > Tester stats (public demo and tester links)
text: **What is collected, only after agreement:** a nickname, device class (phone, tablet, desktop), browser and system family names, language, whether the app is installed, the screens opened and for how long (in buckets), features used, tour progress, a connection class (offline, slow, fast) and the feedback the person types, with phone numbers and email addresses masked. **Never collected:** IP address, location, phone number, email, contacts, device or advertising ids, the full user-agent string, keystrokes, anything typed in the Practice Class or the chat, voice, or any child or teacher data.

heading: Cohort Coach > Tester stats (public demo and tester links)
text: The device id is random and stays on the phone; only a salted SHA-256 hash is sent. **Delete your data.** My profile, Testing and sharing, **Delete my data** removes every row held under this device's hash on the server and clears the phone. Tester events and feedback are also deleted after 90 days. Pause sharing in the same place.

heading: Cohort Coach > Guardrails, offline and privacy in brief
text: - **Guardrails** ([docs/guardrails.md](docs/guardrails.md)): code computes every number; nothing AI-written reaches a teacher before code checks, a rule-based pre-filter and the output checker; lessons also need a coach and then an officer. Rejection reasons feed the checker.

heading: Cohort Coach > Guardrails, offline and privacy in brief
text: - **Offline and low data** ([docs/offline.md](docs/offline.md)): only the Practice Class needs a live connection and it falls back to text; uploads and modules queue offline. Data per track is computed in [docs/evidence/data_budget.json](docs/evidence/data_budget.json): since modules became MP3 48 kbps (1 Nov, branch `speech-bodhan`), the worst case at the 5-minute module cap is over the 10 MB target even with text practice (14.73 MB computed; it was within it at OGG 16 kbps). Shorter modules cost proportionally less; a measured figure per track comes from the speech evaluation.

heading: Cohort Coach > Guardrails, offline and privacy in brief
text: - **Privacy** ([docs/privacy.md](docs/privacy.md)): no child names, faces or voices; sheet photos are deleted after reading; teachers see counts, never percentages; officers see aggregates only.

heading: Cohort Coach > Setup
text: Copy `.env.example` to `.env`.

heading: Cohort Coach > Setup
text: Without keys the app runs on recorded fixtures. `AI_MODE` is `live`, `recorded` (answers replayed from `ai/fixtures/recorded/`; the header says **AI: recorded answers** and each replayed answer says **Recorded AI answer**) or `off` (every call fails as if the service were unreachable; the header says **AI: off**, and each AI feature says so and offers its non-AI path: Auto-fill or typing for sheets, the code template for lessons, a person for chat questions, Generate from rules for papers).

heading: Cohort Coach > Setup
text: QA with the AI offline: [docs/build/reports/QA-DEMO.md](docs/build/reports/QA-DEMO.md). There is one app and one back end; the pilot runs in the same flow (Papers, then Enter check). **External speech services** (not Claude). Speech goes through one provider layer (`services/speech/chain.py`): **Bodhan AI** first (`indic-transcribe` for speech to text, `indic-speak` for text to speech; keys `BODHAN_SPEAK_API_KEY` and `BODHAN_TRANSCRIBE_API_KEY`, each falling back to `BODHAN_API_KEY`), **Sarvam** as the fallback (`SARVAM_API_KEY`). The order is set by `SPEECH_TTS_PROVIDERS` and `SPEECH_STT_PROVIDERS`; a provider with no key is skipped.

heading: Cohort Coach > Setup
text: Check the Bodhan keys with `python scripts/check_bodhan.py --no-live` (configuration only) or without the flag (two small paid calls; the estimate is printed first). Audio conversion needs **ffmpeg** on PATH (installed in the Dockerfile; WinGet, apt or brew locally).

heading: Cohort Coach > Setup
text: Lessons are voiced in chunks of one or two sentences, checked by transcribing each back, and stitched into one MP3 (mono, 48 kbps) with a timing map; a coach can listen, regenerate a sentence and approve on the review screen. `python tasks.py lessons-pregen` voices and caches every published demo lesson (prints the cost; `--yes` to spend). Bodhan's default limit is about 8 requests a minute per model, so requests are paced.

heading: Cohort Coach > Setup
text: Before Bodhan may be first in a deployment it must pass two gates recorded by a person (`docs/evidence/speech_gates.md`: a blinded listening test, `python tasks.py speech-eval-pack`, and a speech-to-text test on team members' recordings, `python tasks.py speech-eval-stt`); both are pending, and the rollout stages are in `docs/build/SPEECH-ROLLOUT.md`. Speech cost per lesson and per session: `docs/evidence/speech_cost.md` (unverified prices). Voices and speech recognition: Bodhan AI / AI4Bharat (Indic-Speak, Indic-Transcribe). Details: [SPEECH-LAYER](docs/build/reports/SPEECH-LAYER.md), [SPEECH-LESSONS](docs/build/reports/SPEECH-LESSONS.md), [SPEECH-PRACTICE](docs/build/reports/SPEECH-PRACTICE.md), [SPEECH-ROLLOUT](docs/build/reports/SPEECH-ROLLOUT.md).

heading: The 32-state Bayesian child model (Practice Class, behind `SIMULATOR_MODEL`)
text: Status: see the build report. Parameters are build defaults, not reviewed by an educator, not fitted to real children. Build report: `docs/build/reports/BAYES-32-STATE.md`. Build prompt: `docs/build/BAYESIAN-32-STATE-BUILD-PROMPT-v2.md` (it supersedes the one-variable prompt; see section 10). This document is the written specification. The independent oracle (`evals/runners/bayes_oracle.py`) is written from it, not from the code.

heading: The 32-state Bayesian child model (Practice Class, behind `SIMULATOR_MODEL`) > 1. The switch and the split
text: - `.env` `SIMULATOR_MODEL` = `legacy` | `bayesian`. Unset or empty means `legacy`. Any other value stops the API at startup: "SIMULATOR_MODEL must be legacy or bayesian (or unset for legacy)". - `.env` `BAYES_PARAMS` (optional) is the parameter file; default `content/bayes/params.v1.yaml`. It is read and validated at startup only when `SIMULATOR_MODEL=bayesian`.

heading: The 32-state Bayesian child model (Practice Class, behind `SIMULATOR_MODEL`) > 1. The switch and the split
text: - `engine/sim_switch.py` is the one factory. `new_session` returns the legacy `SessionState` or the bayesian `BayesState`, and `plan_turn` dispatches on the state's type, so a session keeps its model when the environment changes later. - `engine/simulator.py` is not edited: its SHA-256 is recorded in `tests/fixtures/legacy_sim.sha256` and checked by a test. Legacy output is checked turn for turn against `tests/fixtures/legacy_sim_golden.json` (every scenario, seeds 1 to 20, two scripts), directly and through the factory.

heading: The 32-state Bayesian child model (Practice Class, behind `SIMULATOR_MODEL`) > 1. The switch and the split
text: - The legacy path never imports `engine/bayes` (checked in a subprocess). The factory imports it lazily. - The only edits to shared code: `services/practice/session.py` calls the factory, and `services/api/main.py` calls `check_startup` instead of the old one-variable check.

These are the fields the rest of the code reads: | Reader | Fields | | `services/practice/session.py` (`take_turn`, `_engine_layer`, `children_view`) | plan: `turn`, `speaker`, `intent`, `answer`, `correct`, `error_code`, `problem`, `steps`, `mood`, `strength_before`, `strength_after`, `allowed_numbers`, `written`, `chorus` (each a `TurnPlan`). Child: `name`, `error`, `shy`, `strength` (the confusion meter), `engagement`, `quiet_turns`. State: `turn`, `children`, `finished`, `finished_reason` |

heading: The 32-state Bayesian child model (Practice Class, behind `SIMULATOR_MODEL`) > 2. The contract with the rest of the engine (Step 0)
text: Types: `turn` int; `move_id`, `behaviour`, `intent`, `mood`, `stage` str; `speaker` str or None; `problem` `Problem` or None; `answer`, `written` int or None; `correct`, `spoken_correct` bool or None; `error_code` `ErrorCode` or None; `steps` tuple of `Step`; `allowed_numbers` frozenset of int; `strength_before`, `strength_after` maps of name to float; `chorus` tuple of `TurnPlan`; `trace` an empty tuple under this model (the bayesian extras go to a separate debug trace).

heading: The 32-state Bayesian child model (Practice Class, behind `SIMULATOR_MODEL`) > 2. The contract with the rest of the engine (Step 0)
text: **Problem choice (legacy).** A move whose behaviour is `answer` takes the posed problem if it is valid, else the next scenario problem `problems[next_problem % 6]`. A move that needs a problem (`explain`, `work_aloud`, `doubt`) when none is on the board takes the next scenario problem. The candidate set is the scenario's own `problems` list (six items per scenario).

heading: The 32-state Bayesian child model (Practice Class, behind `SIMULATOR_MODEL`) > 2. The contract with the rest of the engine (Step 0)
text: **Addressing (legacy, confirmed).** A move named to one child reaches her directly and every other child as something overheard, at the scenario's `overhear` share (0.5) of its effect on strength and engagement, never the going-quiet. A move to the class or to no one (`addressed` None or not one of the five names) applies the full effect to every child. `other` and `off_task` are neutral: only the turn counter changes.

heading: The 32-state Bayesian child model (Practice Class, behind `SIMULATOR_MODEL`) > 2. The contract with the rest of the engine (Step 0)
text: **Move ids** (all move lists): pose_problem, ask_explain, show_bundles, exchange_ten, regroup_ten, decomposition, compensation, show_chart, check_back, order_probe, tell_rule, repeat_rule_louder, give_the_answer, praise, scold; plus the neutral other and off_task. **Error codes:** SUB-SFL, SUB-NODEC, ADD-NOCARRY, PV-HEARD, PV-REVERSE. **Teacher notes.** No teacher note reaches the Practice Class: `start_session` and the API's session request carry the error, language, class counts, seed and judge flag only. So `note_tags` is an optional parameter of the factory (and of `start_session`), tested, and not wired to any screen.

text: The attention base and starting value are the scenario's `start_engagement` (0.6); the overhear share is the scenario's `overhear` (0.5). Neither is repeated. **Spec note.** The response defaults give a mean starting wrong rate of 0.902 for a target-habit child on an item that needs the step, matching legacy's start_strength 0.9: P(P∧E) at start = 0.6 × 0.4 = 0.24, so 0.95 × (1 − 0.24) + 0.75 × 0.24 = 0.722 + 0.18 = 0.902.

heading: The 32-state Bayesian child model (Practice Class, behind `SIMULATOR_MODEL`) > 4. State
text: Each erring child holds a true hidden state as a map `{"place_value": 0|1, "exchange": 0|1, "written_step": 0|1, "habit": none|target|sibling|no_method}`; below, P, E, W and H. `no_method` means no stable method. Traces show the actual error code next to the role. A belief is a joint array with one named axis per variable, shape (2, 2, 2, 4). Axis order (place_value, exchange, written_step, habit) and habit order (none, target, sibling, no_method) are declared once, in `engine/bayes/state.py`; every conversion goes through it.

heading: The 32-state Bayesian child model (Practice Class, behind `SIMULATOR_MODEL`) > 4. State
text: The flat index is ((P·2 + E)·2 + W)·4 + H (row-major), used for the 32 × 32 transition matrix and for serialisation. The correct child (seat 0) is outside the model: always right, as legacy.

heading: The 32-state Bayesian child model (Practice Class, behind `SIMULATOR_MODEL`) > 5. The simulated child (generative model) > 5.1 Class and prior
text: The class (names, error code per seat, stages, shy child) comes from the legacy `fill_seats`, read-only, so a seed gives the same class under both models. Each erring child's start state is drawn from `Random(f"bayes:prior:{seed}:{seat}")`: - written_step = 0; - habit = the seat's role (target or sibling by its error code), or no_method if the seat's stage is input-teaching;

heading: The 32-state Bayesian child model (Practice Class, behind `SIMULATOR_MODEL`) > 5. The simulated child (generative model) > 5.1 Class and prior
text: - (place_value, exchange) jointly from **one uniform** over the four cells in row-major order (0,0), (0,1), (1,0), (1,1), with weights (1−p_P0)(1−p_E0_P0), (1−p_P0)·p_E0_P0, p_P0(1−p_E0_P1), p_P0·p_E0_P1; - teacher-note tags reweight those four cells (only factors on place_value or exchange) and are renormalised before the draw. In the generative prior, tags never change habit or written_step.

heading: The 32-state Bayesian child model (Practice Class, behind `SIMULATOR_MODEL`) > 5. The simulated child (generative model) > 5.2 Response table O(kind | s, item)
text: Kinds: correct, bug_target, bug_sibling, no_answer. - `bites(code, item)`: the bug function for that code gives a wrong number different from the correct answer. - `needs_step(item)`: at least one bug in the child's family bites on the item. **Item needs no step:** every state answers correct with probability 1, except habit no_method, which answers correct with c_nm_easy and no_answer with 1 − c_nm_easy. **Item needs the step:** | W | H | correct | bug_target | bug_sibling | no_answer |

text: A child answers at most once per turn. `work_aloud` always draws a fresh answer; `explain` and `doubt` repeat the child's last answer if she has one (legacy draws twice under `work_aloud`; the second draw replaces the first, so one draw is the same rule).

heading: The 32-state Bayesian child model (Practice Class, behind `SIMULATOR_MODEL`) > 5. The simulated child (generative model) > 5.5 Learning transitions
text: Each turn, for each erring child, from the start-of-turn state. **Reach** r, matching legacy addressing: 1 for a direct move (the named child, or every child when the move is to the class or to no one); `overhear` (0.5) for every other child; 0 for the neutral moves `other` and `off_task`. A child is **reached directly** when r = 1 from a direct move. **Concept learning.** For X ∈ {P, E, W} with X = 0: if cov_X(m)·r > 0,

heading: The 32-state Bayesian child model (Practice Class, behind `SIMULATOR_MODEL`) > 5. The simulated child (generative model) > 5.5 Learning transitions
text: p_learn(X) = σ(beta0 + beta_cov·cov_X(m)·r + beta_fit·fit_X(s) + beta_scaf·scaf(m)·r + beta_att·(a − 0.5) − beta_over·ov) else 0. σ(x) = 1/(1 + e^(−x)). fit_P = 1; fit_E = 1 if P=1 else fit_E_noP; fit_W = 1 if E=1 else fit_W_noE. Here a is the child's attention after this turn's filter step (5.7, which comes before the transitions in the turn order) and ov her overload this turn (5.8). **Habit**, for H ∈ {target, sibling}, one categorical draw:

heading: The 32-state Bayesian child model (Practice Class, behind `SIMULATOR_MODEL`) > 5. The simulated child (generative model) > 5.5 Learning transitions
text: - p_break = σ(gamma0 + gamma_conf·conf(m)·r + gamma_E·E + gamma_att·(a − 0.5)) if conf(m)·r > 0, else 0. Breaking sets H = none. - p_shift = shift_rate·r if rule_drill(m), E = 0, W = 0 and the family defines a shift from the child's current code; shifting moves H to the other code's role. - If p_break + p_shift > 1, both are scaled to sum to 1. H stays with the remaining probability.

heading: The 32-state Bayesian child model (Practice Class, behind `SIMULATOR_MODEL`) > 5. The simulated child (generative model) > 5.5 Learning transitions
text: - H = no_method becomes none when W flips 0 → 1 in the same turn. H = none never changes. **Forgetting**, every turn whether the child is reached or not: each X = 1 reverts to 0 with hazard h_X = h0_X·exp(−c/c0), where c is her count of correct answers this session on items that need the step.

heading: The 32-state Bayesian child model (Practice Class, behind `SIMULATOR_MODEL`) > 5. The simulated child (generative model) > 5.5 Learning transitions
text: **Matrix.** The 32 × 32 matrix T[s, s′] is the product of the place_value factor, the exchange factor and the joint (written_step, habit) factor, enumerated from these rules for every start state. Every row sums to 1. **Draws.** `Random(f"bayes:trans:{seed}:{turn}:{seat}")`, exactly four uniforms per erring child per turn, in the order P, E, W, H, drawn whether used or not.

heading: The 32-state Bayesian child model (Practice Class, behind `SIMULATOR_MODEL`) > 5. The simulated child (generative model) > 5.5 Learning transitions
text: For X = 0, X′ = 1 when u_X < p_learn(X); for X = 1, X′ = 0 when u_X < h_X. Habit: H′ = none when u_H < p_break; else the shifted role when u_H < p_break + p_shift; else H.

heading: The 32-state Bayesian child model (Practice Class, behind `SIMULATOR_MODEL`) > 5. The simulated child (generative model) > 5.6 Priming
text: A demo move that reaches a child with r > 0 primes her at strength δ0·r, age 0, on the demo turn itself. On later turns δ = δ0·r·rho^age, while age < prime_window; then it ends. A new demo resets it. Priming changes answers only (5.2), never the state.

heading: The 32-state Bayesian child model (Practice Class, behind `SIMULATOR_MODEL`) > 5. The simulated child (generative model) > 5.7 Attention (low-pass filter)
text: a_(t+1) = a_t + α·(target_t − a_t), α = 1 − exp(−1/tau), a_0 = start_engagement. target_t = clamp(base + K_push·eng(m)·r + addressed_bonus·[reached directly] − neglect·[not reached directly for ≥ neglect_after turns] − overload_drag·ov, 0, 1), base = start_engagement. The count of turns not reached directly resets to 0 on a turn she is reached directly and goes up by 1 otherwise (neutral moves count as not reached). Attention applies to all five children.

text: It replaces engagement in the bayesian path: it sets the speaker weights (a + 0.05), the mood (legacy thresholds: flat below 0.35, bright above 0.75, else calm; small after a scold; doubtful on a wrong answer under a check-back) and the engagement field the faces read.

text: ov = max(0, n_heavy − ov_free), where n_heavy counts the moves with max(cov_P, cov_E, cov_W) ≥ heavy_cov that reached the child directly in the last ov_window turns, including this one.

heading: The 32-state Bayesian child model (Practice Class, behind `SIMULATOR_MODEL`) > 6. Belief engine, soft evidence, question choice > 6.1 Observer
text: Per erring child, a belief b over the 32 states. It never reads the true state and consumes no randomness.

heading: The 32-state Bayesian child model (Practice Class, behind `SIMULATOR_MODEL`) > 6. Belief engine, soft evidence, question choice > 6.1 Observer
text: Start: the plain generative prior over (place_value, exchange); habit r_diag on the seat's diagnosed code's role, with 1 − r_diag shared equally over the other habit values the family allows (none, the other code of the pair if there is one, no_method); written_step 0 with obs_W0 and 1 with 1 − obs_W0; then the teacher-note tags (6.2) on every variable they name. Each turn:

heading: The 32-state Bayesian child model (Practice Class, behind `SIMULATOR_MODEL`) > 6. Belief engine, soft evidence, question choice > 6.1 Observer
text: - **Predict** (every erring child, every turn): b ← b·T_t, with T_t built from the same rules and the same observable context (move, reach, attention, overload, c).

heading: The 32-state Bayesian child model (Practice Class, behind `SIMULATOR_MODEL`) > 6. Belief engine, soft evidence, question choice > 6.1 Observer
text: - **Update** (only when the child gives a fresh answer): b ← normalise(b ⊙ L), L(s) = P(observed outcome | s, item, priming, stage). For a core (or input-teaching) child the outcome is the number said, or no number: P(n | s) = O(correct|s)·[n = correct] + O(bug_target|s)/|W_t|·[n ∈ W_t] + O(bug_sibling|s)/|W_s|·[n ∈ W_s], where W_t and W_s are the two codes' wrong-answer sets. For an output or input-test child the outcome is error form versus correct: P(form | s) = 1 − O(correct|s), or 0 when the item has no form.

heading: The 32-state Bayesian child model (Practice Class, behind `SIMULATOR_MODEL`) > 6. Belief engine, soft evidence, question choice > 6.1 Observer
text: Outputs: marginals P(place_value=1), P(exchange=1), P(written_step=1) and P(habit=·); entropy in bits, H(b) = −Σ b(s) log2 b(s); the most likely state; the predictive P(correct) = Σ b(s)·P(correct | s) for any item.

heading: The 32-state Bayesian child model (Practice Class, behind `SIMULATOR_MODEL`) > 6. Belief engine, soft evidence, question choice > 6.2 Soft evidence
text: For each tag, multiply the weight of every state by the tag's likelihood ratio for the variables it names, then renormalise. The generative prior applies tags to (place_value, exchange) only; the observer's start belief to every variable the tag names. No tags gives exactly the plain prior. The class diagnosis enters the observer through r_diag. Not wired to the UI (section 2).

heading: The 32-state Bayesian child model (Practice Class, behind `SIMULATOR_MODEL`) > 6. Belief engine, soft evidence, question choice > 6.3 Next question by expected information gain
text: When the planner must choose the problem itself, it scores each scenario item: EIG(item) = H(b) − Σ_y P(y | b, item)·H(b | y, item), with P(y | b) = Σ b(s)·L_y(s) and b | y ∝ b ⊙ L_y, over the observable outcomes y of 6.1, with the predicted belief and the child's priming this turn.

heading: The 32-state Bayesian child model (Practice Class, behind `SIMULATOR_MODEL`) > 6. Belief engine, soft evidence, question choice > 6.3 Next question by expected information gain
text: The score is for the named child, or summed over the erring children when the move is to the class or to no one (a named correct child scores 0 everywhere). The highest score wins; ties go to the earliest item in scenario order. The problem just used is not repeated unless it is the only one. No new problems are made. The ranking goes to the trace.

text: The earlier build (`docs/build/BAYESIAN-MODEL-BUILD-PROMPT.md`, `engine/child_model.py`) added a one-variable model: Bayesian knowledge tracing with a Beta prior and a responsiveness per child, selected by `SIMULATOR_MODEL=bayesian` inside `engine/simulator.py`. This build supersedes it. Because `engine/simulator.py` must not be edited, that code stays in place: the factory always passes the legacy model explicitly, so no session can select the one-variable model, and its unit tests still run against the module directly. `SIMULATOR_MODEL=bayesian` now means the 32-state model.

heading: The 32-state Bayesian child model (Practice Class, behind `SIMULATOR_MODEL`) > 10. The one-variable model this replaces
text: Code that calls `engine.simulator.new_session` without a model (some scripts and the legacy evals) still reads `engine.child_model.model_from_env`, so with `SIMULATOR_MODEL=bayesian` set in the shell those scripts would get the one-variable model: run them with the variable unset.

heading: Answer reading (call 8): photo of a sheet to one child's boxes (interim, v1 Check page)
text: In the Check page a teacher can take a photo of one child's answer sheet. The server reads the ten boxes, the boxes fill in, she checks every box (the ones the reader was unsure of are marked and selected first), corrects mistakes with the keypad, and goes to the next child.

heading: Answer reading (call 8): photo of a sheet to one child's boxes (interim, v1 Check page)
text: This is the first working slice of P08; the full check flow on both channels (photos queued offline, confirm steps, no per-child answers kept on the phone) replaces it in P08.

heading: Answer reading (call 8): photo of a sheet to one child's boxes (interim, v1 Check page) > How a read works
text: 1. **On the phone:** the photo is shrunk to about 1200 px on the long edge as a JPEG (about 80 KB) and sent with the form id (A or B) and nothing else. It is not saved on the phone.

heading: Answer reading (call 8): photo of a sheet to one child's boxes (interim, v1 Check page) > How a read works
text: 2. **On the server** (`services/api/sheets.py`, `ai/calls/c08_answer_reading.py`): the photo is held in memory, sent to the vision model, and dropped. The size cap (800 KB) is under the 1 MB at which the framework would write an upload to a temporary file, so the photo never touches the disk. Nothing is logged and the photo is never sent back.

heading: Answer reading (call 8): photo of a sheet to one child's boxes (interim, v1 Check page) > How a read works
text: 3. **Blind read:** the model is told only that there are ten boxes. It never sees the questions, the numbers in them or the expected answers (a test checks the request). It returns the digits in each box and how sure it is.

heading: Answer reading (call 8): photo of a sheet to one child's boxes (interim, v1 Check page) > How a read works
text: 4. **Judged by code:** digits are normalised (Devanagari and Tamil digits become 0-9). A box is "ok" only if the model is at least 80% sure (a tuning value) and the read is an answer the item recognises: the correct answer, a known error answer, or a known untracked pattern. Everything else is marked "check". A clearly empty box becomes "blank". A box that could not be read stays empty and marked. The expected answers are used only here, after reading.

heading: Answer reading (call 8): photo of a sheet to one child's boxes (interim, v1 Check page) > How a read works
text: 5. **A broken answer** (wrong number of boxes, a malformed read) is retried once on a stronger model; if that fails too she is told to type. When there is no connection she is told to type, and nothing is sent. 6. **The reads go back to her phone**, where she edits them. The server stores no reads. The audit row for the call holds metadata only (tokens, cost, latency, validator codes), like every other call.

heading: Answer reading (call 8): photo of a sheet to one child's boxes (interim, v1 Check page) > What this is not
text: - It does not accept anything silently as correct: every box is hers to check, and the marked ones are where to look first.

heading: Answer reading (call 8): photo of a sheet to one child's boxes (interim, v1 Check page) > What this is not
text: - It is not an accuracy claim. A live smoke test on one synthetic printed sheet (not handwriting) read all ten boxes right; that proves the pipeline works, not how well it reads children's handwriting. The accuracy bars (at least 98% of auto-accepted reads correct, at most 15% sent to the teacher) are measured by eval 9 on real pilot sheets in P08 and are pending.

heading: Answer reading (call 8): photo of a sheet to one child's boxes (interim, v1 Check page) > What this is not
text: - A blank box currently comes back marked "check" with 0 confidence (the model reports no confidence for an empty box). That is the safe direction; the prompt can be tuned in P08 with its eval.

text: | Part | Test | | Normalising, in-set and confidence judging, blank handling | `tests/api/test_sheets.py` | | The model never sees expected answers or operands | `tests/api/test_sheets.py::test_the_model_is_never_told_the_expected_answers` | | Retry on the stronger model, failure means type | `tests/api/test_sheets.py` | | Bad, oversized or unknown-form uploads; no photo in the reply; no photo or digits in logs; metadata-only audit row | `tests/api/test_sheets.py` |

heading: Architecture (v1, after P03)
text: > **Kit v3 (19 Oct):** this page describes the v1 build, where the check is entered on the phone and only counts sync. In v3 the check arrives as photos through the bot or the PWA and the flows run on one back end; this page is rewritten in P05 and P14. See `docs/build/DECISIONS.md` (2026-10-19 · Kit v3 adopted) and `docs/build/reports/MIGRATION-v1-v3.md`. What exists today.

heading: Architecture (v1, after P03)
text: Later phases add the PWA, Practice Class, voice, Telegram and review screens; this page grows with them.

heading: Architecture (v1, after P03) > AI in five layers
text: The ten calls (call 10, the demo teacher, runs in judge mode only), with the five layers written out for each, are in `ai/registry.py`. The README section "Where AI is used" and `GET /api/judge/ai-map` are generated from it.

heading: Architecture (v1, after P03) > One path for every call
text: `ai/client.py::run_call(call_id, payload, context=...)`: 1. Load the versioned prompt (`ai/prompts/cNN_name.vN.md`, front matter id, version, model, changelog). The stable system block goes first with a cache marker. 2. Check the budget (live and record modes only). 3. Render the user message: trusted facts as JSON, untrusted text wrapped in tags. 4. Mode `recorded` reads `ai/fixtures/recorded/<call>/<hash>.json` (tests, CI, demos); `live` calls `client.messages.parse(..., output_format=Model)` with an explicit effort; `record` does live and saves the answer. With no `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` the client refuses live and record.

heading: Architecture (v1, after P03) > One path for every call
text: 5. Re-validate with Pydantic, run the call's validators, retry within bounds with the violations stated. 6. On failure, a deterministic fallback (template line, or "needs a human"). 7. Write one audit row: call id, prompt version, model, tokens in/out/cache, cost from `ai/pricing.yaml`, latency, validator codes, checker verdict, retries, fallback. Models and per-call policies (timeout, retries, effort, max tokens) are in `ai/config.py`; each model id can be overridden by its `MODEL_*` env var.

heading: Architecture (v1, after P03) > One path for every call
text: Prices, with source URL and date, are in `ai/pricing.yaml`. API facts checked before coding are in `docs/build/DECISIONS.md` (P03 verified API facts).

heading: Decisions log
text: Newest first within each section. Every entry: date, decision, why, alternatives considered, who confirmed. A newer entry here overrides `CLAUDE.md`, the build prompts and the design doc; update `CLAUDE.md` in the same commit when a rule changes.

heading: Decisions log > 2026-10-30 · Device-based tester profiles and a Testing evidence view (TESTER_STATS=1)
text: - **Decision:** the public demo and tester links can collect opt-in, coarse usage data from testers, shown to judges as aggregates. A random id is made on the device and never leaves it; the device sends only SHA-256(salt + id). Nothing is sent (no profile, event or feedback) before the person agrees; "Use without sharing" sends nothing and the app works in full. Collected: nickname, coarse device class, browser and system family, language, screens opened, features used, tour progress, a connection class and feedback the person types (phone numbers and emails masked). Never: IP address (the access-log line for these paths is dropped), location, contacts, user-agent string, typed content, voice, child or teacher data. Judge devices (a `?src=judge` link or choosing the Judge role) and team devices (`?team=<TESTER_TEAM_TOKEN>`) are tagged and left out of tester counts by default, shown separately. The judge endpoint answers only the judge role in a judge deployment; the CSV export needs the team token. Events and feedback are deleted after 90 days or on "Delete my data". The switch is the server flag `TESTER_STATS=1`; it is never mounted in pilot mode. The guided tour gains a seventh step ("See who has tried it"), budgeted at 10 s so the tour stays within 300 s. Report: `docs/build/reports/TESTER-STATS.md`.

heading: Decisions log > 2026-10-30 · Device-based tester profiles and a Testing evidence view (TESTER_STATS=1)
text: - **Why:** the submission needs real, live proof of user testing and refinement (judged area "user inputs and testing"), without inflating numbers and without collecting anything private. - **Alternatives:** third-party analytics (rejected: scripts, cookies, IP); a fingerprint or user-agent id (rejected: tracking); showing every tester by name (rejected: listing is a separate, off-by-default consent); seeding sample testers (rejected: no fabricated evidence, non-negotiable 7). - **Confirmed by:** Gopi (request of 30 Oct).

heading: Decisions log > 2026-10-30 · The v2 front-end (`apps/pwa-v2/`) is parked; v1 is the only front-end
text: - **Decision:** `apps/pwa-v2/` is not run, deployed or extended. Its run script (`run-frontend-v2.bat`) is removed; the folder stays in the working tree, uncommitted, for reference only. All front-end work from here is in `apps/pwa/`. - **Why:** the re-skin needs a lot more fixes (most screens are not rebuilt on the new components; fonts and snapshot tests are open) and the freeze has passed. - **Alternatives:** finish v2 before 31 Oct (rejected: no time). - **Confirmed by:** Gopi (30 Oct).

heading: Decisions log > 2026-10-30 · Re-skin the front-end in a new folder, behaviour frozen
text: - **Decision:** the front-end re-skin (`docs/build/Claude Code prompt re-skin the front-end ...`) is built as a copy in `apps/pwa-v2/`; `apps/pwa/` is untouched. v2 adds tokens with a dark mode and a five-size type scale (`src/styles/tokens.css`), a base layer for raw form elements, a component set (`src/ui/`), a side rail from 900 px, and a living style guide at `#/dev/styleguide`. APIs, state, permissions and AI calls are unchanged; the screens still render their existing markup and gain the new look through the shared classes. Screens are migrated to the components one at a time; Officer cohorts and Profile were done first. One shared string key (`judge.styleguide`) was added in en, hi and ta.

heading: Decisions log > 2026-10-30 · Re-skin the front-end in a new folder, behaviour frozen
text: - **Why:** the user asked for a new front-end folder so the working app stays as it is for the submission. The `UI_V2` flag in the prompt is not needed, because the two apps do not share a build. - **Alternatives:** re-skin in place behind a flag (rejected by the user); rewrite every screen on the new components at once (rejected: no time before 31 Oct, and the risk of changing behaviour).

heading: Decisions log > 2026-10-30 · Re-skin the front-end in a new folder, behaviour frozen
text: - **Confirmed by:** Gopi (folder choice, 2026-10-29). Open: whether v2 replaces `apps/pwa/` for the final deploy.

heading: Decisions log > 2026-10-30 · One assistant, scoped by role on the server
text: - **Decision:** one assistant for all roles. The server sets the scope from the authenticated role (judge in the judge deployment, teacher everywhere else); a question or a "act as" phrase never widens it; only the judge session may View as another role; the About this product tab is always the judge scope. The judge corpus includes the repository markdown, `docs/RUBRIC_MAP.md`, the deck slides and the video script, so judge answers cite a file, a slide number and a video time. Retrieval is word-based over a plain JSON index bundled in the image (no embeddings). Suggested questions are pre-written from the docs and work offline; free text uses call 14 and abstains when nothing is found. The assistant is read-only: it cannot approve, send or delete, and it reads no live class data yet.

heading: Decisions log > 2026-10-30 · One assistant, scoped by role on the server
text: - **Why:** judges and each role need answers that stay inside what they may see and never claim more than the rubric map's status. - **Alternatives:** scope in the prompt (rejected: can be talked around); embeddings and a vector store (rejected: CLAUDE.md bars a vector database and plain JSON works with no network). - **Confirmed by:** Gopi (asked for the build, 29 Oct). Dated 30 Oct as the prompt specifies; built 29 Oct.

heading: Decisions log > 2026-10-29 · Material 3 on every screen, with the whole look in one file
text: - **Decision:** (1) Every screen now uses the Material 3 look of `docs/design/stitch/DESIGN.md` (teal primary, 16 px cards, 8 px buttons and fields, state layers on hover, focus and press, a navigation bar with a selected pill, a bottom sheet for More, tonal banners). This supersedes the blue-notebook look of `docs/design-system.md` v1 and the "parked" note in the entry below. (2) The look lives in one file, `apps/pwa/src/theme.css`: palette, corners, state layers, spacing, type. `styles.css` and `pilot/pilot.css` read those tokens. `tests/test_design_tokens.py` now fails if a colour literal returns to `styles.css`, if a stylesheet uses a token nothing defines, if the `classic` theme overrides a token that does not exist, or if the manifest colours, meta tag and icons drift from `--pen` and `--paper`. (3) `VITE_THEME=classic` builds the old palette and 2 px corners for comparison. (4) The contrast figures in the doc are recomputed from the new tokens: body text 16.3 and 8.9, primary 6.0, error 6.2, all above 4.5; the 16 px text floor and the tap sizes are unchanged. (5) The app icons, the manifest theme colour and the browser bar colour moved to the teal.

text: - **Decision:** (1) The coach's approval now approves the TEXT only; it no longer calls Sarvam. (2) An approved lesson is shared as a **lesson link** (`/#/lesson/<token>`): an unguessable, HMAC-signed token that expires after 14 days and opens one approved lesson's text, with no sign-in. (3) The first tap on **Download audio** on that page voices the approved script (one Sarvam call), stores the file in the published-audio bucket, and every later tap reuses it; two taps at once make it once. A daily cap (`PILOT_VOICE_DAILY_MAX`, default 20) limits new voicings that teachers' taps cause, failures included; past it the text still opens. The coordinator can still press Make audio now. (4) The coordinator still shares by hand (Web Share, Copy link, `wa.me`); the system delivers nothing. (5) This adds one public, read-only page and two public routes (`GET /api/pilot/lesson/{token}`, `POST /api/pilot/lesson/{token}/audio`) to a mode that had only sign-in and two staff pages; the staff routes still need a token (`tests/pilot/test_lesson_link.py` checks every route). On-device voice for capable phones is parked (`PARKING.md`), not built.

heading: Decisions log > Settled decisions > 2026-10-23 · Pilot mode: two pages, a separate private bucket for sheet photos, a consent gate
text: - **Decision:** (1) `PILOT_MODE=1` (off by default) turns a deployment into the pilot: sign-in, **Upload sheets** and **Intervention audio**, nothing else. Every other API router is not mounted (404, API docs off) and the web app redirects every other address to Upload sheets; hiding a menu item is not the mechanism. (2) Sign-in extends the auth stub: accounts come from `PILOT_ACCOUNTS`, tokens are signed and expire after 12 hours, five wrong tries pause a name for ten minutes, and the `X-Role` header and judge mode are ignored in pilot mode. New account type **Pilot coordinator** (uploads, generates, shares, sets retention); `coach` keeps approval (new permission `pilot.approve_audio`, the pilot form of `coach.approve_items`, which stays planned for P11); `officer` may only listen. One person may hold several roles. (3) **Pilot pre-test sheet photos are now stored**, in a new private S3-compatible bucket (`S3_SHEETS_BUCKET`, refused if equal to `S3_BUCKET`): server-side encryption requested on every write, no public URL, upload by a 5-minute presigned PUT, download by a 2-minute signed GET for the coordinator only. Table `pilot_sheet` has no name column and refuses unknown fields; codes (school, class, teacher) must look like codes, not names. (4) **Consent gate:** nothing uploads until the coordinator confirms school consent and enters its reference, which is stored on every sheet; the server enforces it, not only the page. (5) **Retention:** `PILOT_RETENTION_DAYS` (default 90, editable 7 to 365 in the app) deletes old photos and sheet rows at start-up and on every upload; class counts stay; the coordinator can delete everything for one school (photos, rows, counts); both are audit-logged in `pilot_audit`. (6) After upload, each JPEG or PNG goes through the existing call 8; HEIC and PDF are stored and marked "needs a second look", as is any sheet with an unsure box; those add nothing to the counts (pilot mode has no page for fixing reads, so they wait for hand-keying). The per-box reads are dropped as soon as the class counts are added. (7) **Audio:** the number of files (default 3, 1 to `PILOT_AUDIO_MAX`, default 10) is stored in `pilot_config`, validated on the server and audit-logged; lowering it makes cards inactive, never deletes them. Chain per slot: pooled class counts, engine diagnosis (the same track rule), the approved move lists, a script, gates 1 and 1b and call 7, the review queue, the coach's approval, then Sarvam voice and the published-audio bucket. Nothing is voiced, published, downloaded or shared before approval. (8) **Call 5 is not built**, so scripts come from a template drafter (`content/pilot/lessons.v1.yaml` plus the move lists, wrong answers computed by `engine.bugs`, counts from the engine, no Form A or B item). `ScriptDrafter` is the seam where call 5 plugs in; its output would pass the same gates. No new AI capability is claimed in `AI_USAGE.md`. (9) **Sharing** is manual from the coordinator's phone: Web Share with the file attached where `navigator.canShare({files})` allows it, else Download, Copy link (24-hour signed link) and Open WhatsApp (`wa.me`); mono AAC in `.m4a` (or MP3 with `PILOT_AUDIO_FORMAT=mp3`) at 32 kbps, re-encoded at 24 kbps if over 1 MB; file names are `cc-pilot-slot<N>-<lang>.m4a`. The share log (`pilot_share`) is a manual record, not delivery confirmation.

text: - **Decision:** (1) The UI direction approved on the Practice Class screen is the system for every screen: Calm Institutional Material (Material 3) with the colour, shape, type and layout rules in `docs/design/stitch/DESIGN.md`. (2) Every screen has a ready-to-paste Google Stitch prompt in `docs/design/stitch/prompts/` (45: the 13 design-doc screens, 28 added screens X1 to X28, 4 roadmap cards R1 to R4); `INVENTORY.md` lists them from the repo; `scripts/check_stitch_prompts.py` and `tests/test_stitch_prompts.py` keep them honest. (4) The UI is built from Stitch exports in `docs/design/stitch/exports/<ID>/`, never from Stitch's font link (it packs three fonts into one malformed URL) or its Tailwind CDN; our own CSS, self-hosted subsetted fonts and inline SVG icons. (5) Where this conflicts with earlier text, the design direction wins for new and rebuilt screens: `CLAUDE.md` said system fonts only (now Inter and the Noto fonts, self-hosted, system fonts as fallback; the font files must pass the data budget in P14) and tap targets of at least 48 px (now at least 44 px, primary buttons 48 px; existing screens keep 48 px until rebuilt, and `tests/test_design_tokens.py` still enforces the current CSS). heading: Decisions log > Settled decisions > 2026-10-23 · Check entry: phone keyboard, sheet list, absent children, missed teaching per concept
text: - **Decision:** (1) Each box is a real input with the phone's number keyboard (`inputmode=numeric`); digits typed in Devanagari or Tamil are turned into 0-9 and anything else is dropped, which was the reason for the old on-screen keypad (a Hindi or Tamil keyboard changing script mid-entry). Blank and "can't read" are marks on each box. (2) A list of sheets lets her jump to any child and see what was entered. (3) "Absent today" skips a roll number: the position is kept so later papers stay in register order, the row is empty and so not counted; marking absent asks before clearing answers. (4) "Missed the teaching" is tagged per concept (place value, questions 1-2; addition with carrying, 3-5; subtraction with borrowing, 7-10), not per sheet. In the engine (`engine/stages.py`, ported to `stagecalc.ts`, parity fixtures regenerated) a signature is left out of the class counts only when every item it rests on lies in a tagged concept; the whole-sheet tag equals every concept; class counts gain `missed_by_concept`. Tags and absences stay on the phone; only class counts are kept.

heading: Decisions log > Settled decisions > 2026-10-22 · Sprite system: SVG from data, packs, call 11
text: - **Decision:** (1) **Grammar whitelist.** A sprite is SVG built only from `svg g circle ellipse rect line polyline polygon path defs linearGradient radialGradient stop clipPath use`; no `script`, `foreignObject`, `image`, `text`, `style`, external `href`, `on*`, `animate` or `animateTransform`; integers only; fixed viewBox per category; size budgets item 2 KB, avatar 12 KB, mat 6 KB. The same rules run on every rendered scene. (2) **Palette slots.** Specs name nine slots (skin, hair, cloth_a, cloth_b, accent, item_a, item_b, mat, ink), never a colour; four approved palettes include a high-contrast one; meaning never rests on colour alone (outlines, hatching), checked by a contrast test and a Machado 2009 colour-vision simulation. (3) **PNG library: `resvg-py`** (a Rust wheel, no system libraries) over CairoSVG (needs native Cairo, awkward on Windows and small hosts); no font is loaded because the grammar has no text. (4) **Expression table.** One code table maps a child's state (speaking, intent, right or wrong, engagement, strength, quiet, shy) to one of seven expressions; the AI never picks one; the first seating shows only calm or shy faces so it leaks no error. (5) **Reduced motion.** Animation is CSS class toggles on opacity only (mouth frames while audio plays) and is off under `prefers-reduced-motion`; the grammar forbids SMIL. (6) **Counts from layouts.** A unit is an element with class token `u`; each layout reports `count_drawn`, and tests parse the SVG to prove it equals the request for 0 to 100. (7) **Two renderers, one output.** Python is canonical; the TypeScript port is held byte-identical by a 114-case golden fixture. (8) **Call 11 (`MODEL_SPRITE`, Sonnet 5.5) drafts item specs offline only**; gates are schema, grammar, size, no text, slots only, contact tile in every palette and as PNG, pre-filter and no-check-item checks, call 7 on the words (it cannot see pixels; the coach looks at the contact sheet), then coach approval and officer enablement, each change a new version. (9) **Dashboard boundary** (updates the 21 Oct content-library entry): configurable by coach and officer with the two keys: enable or disable packs, items and expressions; persona looks and seating; approved palettes; scenario templates (number slots filled by code, no digits in the text). Code only: grammar, renderer, layouts, validators, the state-to-expression table, anything that computes a count. (10) **A new pack needs no renderer change**, proved by a hash of the renderer files (only `services/api/sprites/` and `apps/pwa/src/sprites/`, tests excluded) recorded in commit fa50ee3 before the second pack was added in cf99a84 and checked by a test; the channel, gate and Practice Class glue (`sprite_media.py`, `sprite_gates.py`, `services/practice/faces.py`) sits outside that hash. (11) **Avatar accessories** are `none` or `bag` only: `glasses` and `ribbon` were removed after the privacy review because they can read as disability and gender markers; the golden fixture was regenerated and the renderer hash is unchanged. (12) CLAUDE.md gained rule 17, a call 11 row and a Do-not line as part of this entry (additive; no bar moved).

heading: Decisions log > Settled decisions > 2026-10-22 · Citations and structured output cannot be combined: calls 4 and 5 use two passes
text: - **Decision:** the Anthropic Citations API returns a 400 when citations are enabled on any document block and `output_config.format` (structured output) is also set. So the two calls that use citations are built in two passes. **Call 4 (method card):** pass A sends the mentor's corrected transcript as one custom-content document (`source.type = "content"`, one text block per sentence, so `start_block_index` is our sentence id), citations on, `cache_control` on the document, and asks for a fixed line format (`STEP:`, `MATERIAL:`, `PHRASE:`, `TIME:`); there is no `output_config.format`. Code rebuilds the lines from the text blocks and their `content_block_location` citations, converts block indexes to sentence ids, and fills the Pydantic card. A line with no citation, a cited id that does not exist, or a `PHRASE:` that is not a verbatim substring of its cited text is rejected and logged (audit validator code, never shown). The existing validators stay as a second, independent check and call 7 still checks "only what she said". Pass B (structured output) is not used for cited fields; if a later pass B is added it gets only the code-parsed text, no documents, and a validator asserts it added or changed no step. **Call 5 (track drafting):** pass 1 is the existing structured-output draft with no documents; pass 2 asks for one "Why this move" line per strategy with citations over the evidence documents (six custom-content documents built by code from `docs/design/evidence-digest.md`, one text block per digest line and source with its page marker kept, `cache_control` on each). Code maps `(document, block index)` to DOC plus PDF page from its own table, so the UI shows the page from the citation and never from model text. A "Why" line with no valid citation is dropped and the draft goes to review without it; a line whose only citations are IDR or APU rows (opinion) is labelled opinion and is never shown as evidence that something works. No new call number.

heading: Decisions log > Settled decisions > 2026-10-22 · Citations and structured output cannot be combined: calls 4 and 5 use two passes
text: - **Why:** the model-side citation is a second signal that each step came from her words (or each "why" from a page), while code stays the guarantor. A step with no citation is rejected rather than trusted. - **Evidence:** the docs state the 400 (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/citations), and `scripts/ai_proof.py` confirmed it on 2026-10-22: the request with citations and `output_config.format` was refused (`docs/evidence/ai_usage_proof.json`, `citations.structured_output_with_citations_refused: true`), and a citations-only request cited sentence ids 0 to 3 that all resolved.

heading: Decisions log > Settled decisions > 2026-10-22 · Citations and structured output cannot be combined: calls 4 and 5 use two passes
text: - **Alternatives rejected:** a prompt asking the model to write sentence ids into a JSON field (a model can invent an id; code already checks that, but the API signal is stronger); dropping structured output for the whole call (loses the schema on the non-cited fields); a forced tool call (a 400 on Opus 5.5 and Sonnet 5.5). - **Confirmed by:** pending Gopi.

heading: Decisions log > Settled decisions > 2026-10-22 · Verified API facts: Citations, caching, batches, effort (checked 22 Oct against platform.claude.com)
text: - **Decision:** the build relies on these facts, each read from the current docs on 2026-10-22.

heading: Decisions log > Settled decisions > 2026-10-22 · Verified API facts: Citations, caching, batches, effort (checked 22 Oct against platform.claude.com)
text: 1. Citations (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/citations): a `document` block with `"citations": {"enabled": true}`; "citations must be enabled on all or none of the documents within a request". Three document types: plain text (`char_location`, chunked by sentence), PDF (`page_location`, 1-indexed pages), custom content (`content_block_location`, `start_block_index` and `end_block_index`, 0-indexed, end exclusive; "your provided content blocks are used as-is and no further chunking is done"). Each citation also carries `cited_text`, `document_index`, `document_title`; `cited_text` does not count toward output tokens. "All active models support citations": Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5 and Haiku 5.5 are active (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/models/overview).

heading: Decisions log > Settled decisions > 2026-10-22 · Verified API facts: Citations, caching, batches, effort (checked 22 Oct against platform.claude.com)
text: 2. Citations with structured outputs: not combinable (400); see the entry above. Source also https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/structured-outputs.

heading: Decisions log > Settled decisions > 2026-10-22 · Verified API facts: Citations, caching, batches, effort (checked 22 Oct against platform.claude.com)
text: 3. Batches and caching: the citations page says citations "work in conjunction with other API features including prompt caching, token counting, and batch processing"; the batch page does not mention citations separately, so citations inside a batch are documented only in that general sentence and are checked when call 5 pass 2 is first run in a batch (fallback: run pass 2 synchronously). Source documents can be cached ("apply `cache_control` to your top-level document content blocks"); the citation blocks in a response cannot. In batches, cache hits are best effort and every request should carry the identical `cache_control` blocks (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/batch-processing).

heading: Decisions log > Settled decisions > 2026-10-22 · Verified API facts: Citations, caching, batches, effort (checked 22 Oct against platform.claude.com)
text: 4. Prompt caching (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/prompt-caching): minimum cacheable prompt is 512 tokens on Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5 and Haiku 5.5; a shorter prompt is not cached and no error is returned; both `cache_creation_input_tokens` and `cache_read_input_tokens` are 0 when nothing was cached; both appear in `usage`. Cache reads cost 0.05x base input on Opus 5.5 and Sonnet 5.5 (so `ai/pricing.yaml` is consistent). `scripts/ai_proof.py` measured 2,114 tokens written on the first call and 2,114 read on the second (Haiku 5.5, `docs/evidence/ai_usage_proof.json`).

heading: Decisions log > Settled decisions > 2026-10-22 · Verified API facts: Citations, caching, batches, effort (checked 22 Oct against platform.claude.com)
text: 5. Thinking and effort (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/effort and https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/thinking-steering-and-cost): `thinking: {"type": "adaptive"}`; effort is `output_config.effort` with `max`, `xhigh`, `high`, `medium`, `low`, never inside `thinking`. Defaults: Opus 5.5 medium, Sonnet 5.5 high, Haiku 5.5 medium. Opus 5.5 always thinks (`disabled` is a 400); Sonnet 5.5 turns up-front thinking off with `between_tools` at low to high; Haiku 5.5 accepts `disabled` at high or below.
