heading: Decisions log > Settled decisions > 2026-10-22 · Addendum v3.1: how the first build differs from the spec
text: - **Decision:** (1) Stage of breakdown is computed **on the phone** from signature answers the engine writes into the answer keys, with a parity test against `engine/stages.py`; the per-child rows never leave the phone. `POST /api/stages` also exists (stateless, no storage, no logging, 300-child cap) for the bot's check flow in P08/P10 and is not called by the PWA. (2) The simulator's mishearing kinds (other operation, swapped digits, one digit off) are code in `engine/simulator.py`, not `content/personas/mishear.yaml` (the addendum lists simulator behaviour as not configurable). (3) The default seating of three core, one input-test and one output child applies to the two subtraction scenarios first (`stage_mix` in their scenario files); PV-HEARD and ADD-NOCARRY seat every child as core until Seema reviews the stage routines. (4) Sample sheets are made-up Form A rows in `content/demo/sample_sheets.v1.yaml`; they are the one file the no-check-items scan exempts. (5) Watch runs are played back on the client from a run the server returns whole; the live cap is `WATCH_LIVE_PER_HOUR` (default 6), measured at about USD 0.02 to 0.04 a run (OD-19 still open for Gopi to set). (6) Call 1 prompt v3 and the call 10 prompt are new versions; eval 2 and the labeller eval are re-run in P13. (7) Conflicts with the addendum text resolved here: the judge flag is server-side (JUDGE_MODE), the missed-teaching count is a class-level count, and the stage routines and officer stage view wait for P09 and P12.

heading: Decisions log > Settled decisions > 2026-10-21 · Stage of breakdown
text: - **Decision:** error cards add a stage of breakdown in teacher language, always "most likely": Input (teaching), Input (test), Core, Output. New signatures (CORE-OFF1, IN-OP, IN-OPND, IN-NEAR, OUT-REV, OUT-REC, NO-METHOD) are generated by code from each form's items and are disjoint from each other and from the correct answer (the designed PV-HEARD and PV-REVERSE overlap is the only exception). Confirm-step tags stay in memory with the per-sheet reads; only class counts per (error, stage) are stored. A stage reaching 25% of children checked (≥ 10 checked) adds a routine of ≤ 60 s to each lesson. The simulator gains persona stages and `spoken` and `written` answers. Spec: `docs/design/addendum-v3.1.md` §F; sheets: `docs/build/synthetic-sheets-stage-addendum.md`.

heading: Decisions log > Settled decisions > 2026-10-21 · Stage of breakdown
text: - **Why:** a count of one wrong method does not tell a teacher whether to reteach, re-read the question aloud or check the writing; a stage with a one-minute probe is the smallest next step. The wording stays honest about what final answers can show.

heading: Decisions log > Settled decisions > 2026-10-21 · Stage of breakdown
text: - **Alternatives rejected:** naming a cause as fact; showing a stage to a child; storing per-child stage or tags (breaks rule 2); an AI call to assign stages (it must be code, rule 1); a per-stage significance test in the officer view without adequate n. - **Confirmed by:** Gopi.

heading: Decisions log > Settled decisions > 2026-10-21 · Teaching strategies and the no-check-items validator
text: - **Decision:** decomposition and compensation become approved moves for SUB-SFL and SUB-NODEC; "check by adding back" is the Output routine (ADD-NOCARRY children check with bundles); an order probe "Is 2 − 6 the same as 6 − 2?" for SUB-SFL; two practice levels per track (without, then with regrouping). A validator blocks any lesson, practice set, script, model run, hint option or worked example that contains a Form A or Form B item (either order, either operation, plus the dictation numbers), at the content gate and in CI. We use the strategies, never the source worksheets' wording or items.

heading: Decisions log > Settled decisions > 2026-10-21 · Teaching strategies and the no-check-items validator
text: - **Why:** the strategies come from the team's own subtraction materials and give teachers alternatives to try; teaching with the check items would invalidate the next check. - **Alternatives rejected:** copying the worksheets' items; trusting reviewers to spot a check item by eye; a one-off list of forbidden numbers (it is derived from the golden file instead, so it cannot drift). - **Confirmed by:** Gopi.

heading: Decisions log > Settled decisions > 2026-10-21 · Content library and its configuration boundary
text: - **Decision:** coach and officer get a content library. Configurable (versioned data): approved strategies and their order, scenario descriptions, persona seating mix, stage routines on or off, practice levels, and thresholds marked `configurable` with a safe range in code. Not configurable (code and files, changed by review): error functions, item generator, scoring, the two-item rule, signature and stage rules, simulator behaviour, validators, prompts, guardrails, and anything that computes a number users see. Two keys: the coach approves (gate 3), the officer switches it on for the block; every change makes a new track version and results stay per version. New topics are not created there.

heading: Decisions log > Settled decisions > 2026-10-21 · Content library and its configuration boundary
text: - **Why:** coaches and officers need to see and steer content without being able to change anything that computes a number; the boundary is what makes the guardrails credible. - **Alternatives rejected:** a free editor for prompts or rules; one key (approval and activation by the same person); creating new topic packs in the library now (parked, `docs/build/PARKING.md`). - **Confirmed by:** Gopi.

heading: Decisions log > Settled decisions > 2026-10-21 · Guided tour and Practice Class demo modes, with call 10
text: - **Decision:** a six-step, five-minute guided tour in judge mode (check, cohort, content, Practice Class, Term 2, under the hood) that switches roles as it goes. The Practice Class gains scenario picker, Watch (an AI teacher in an experienced or a struggling style, ending in the normal feedback card), Try with hints, Free, always-on subtitles (call 1 returns the scenario-language line and the English line), move tags, a confusion meter, a "Show the machinery" panel, speed controls and "Try to break it" chips. New **call 10, Demo teacher** (`MODEL_DEMO_TEACHER` → `claude-haiku-5-5`), judge mode only, labelled "AI playing the teacher (demo only)", with code validators and a template-line fallback; recorded runs (labelled, with date, model versions and seed) take over on a failed call or a turn over 8 s; live runs are capped per hour with a visible cost meter. New **eval 11**: 20 runs per style, 100% approved move ids, 0 numbers outside the allowed set, experienced beats struggling on the rubric in ≥ 18 of 20 pairs. Call 1 gets prompt v2; eval 2 re-runs.

heading: Decisions log > Settled decisions > 2026-10-21 · Guided tour and Practice Class demo modes, with call 10
text: - **Why:** a judge who does not teach cannot tell a strong rehearsal from a weak one by trying it; watching both, with the machinery visible, shows the AI layers and the guardrails in five minutes. Recorded runs keep the demo inside the budget and up during the judging window.

heading: Decisions log > Settled decisions > 2026-10-21 · Guided tour and Practice Class demo modes, with call 10

heading: Decisions log > Settled decisions > 2026-10-21 · Landing page and roles
text: - **Decision:** the web app opens on a landing page with four role cards (Teacher, Mentor, Coach, Programme officer) and a "Guided tour (5 min)" card. Picking a role opens a scope dialog (You can, You can't, Data you'll see, Also on, weekly time cap) with Enter dashboard, 60-second walk-through and Back. The dialog is generated from `services/api/roles/permissions.yaml`, the same config the server enforces through one `require()` guard; a test asserts every "can" and "can't" line maps to an enforced permission, and the reverse. In demo and judge mode every role is selectable with a header switcher; in production only the roles recorded for her pseudonymous id appear (assigned by the officer with consent, no passwords). Teacher and mentor render in a phone frame on wide screens. Spec: `docs/design/addendum-v3.1.md` §A.

heading: Decisions log > Settled decisions > 2026-10-21 · Landing page and roles
text: - **Why:** judges should see who holds each role in the field and what each role cannot do before they see any data; one config avoids a dialog that promises more or less than the server allows. - **Alternatives rejected:** a hand-written dialog (it drifts); a separate demo UI per role; passwords or accounts (rule in section 14); a role cap for the officer invented now (OD-25). - **Confirmed by:** Gopi.

heading: Decisions log > Settled decisions > 2026-10-20 · P05 flow engine: re-entry, erasure, replay
text: - **Decision:** the home menu re-shows its status line whenever the flow is re-opened (`Node.reentry`). A replayed answer key returns the current step only, not the earlier auto messages. Deleting a teacher also deletes her consent history (keyed by her device ids), not just her record; `/stop` in Telegram asks first. Webhook send errors are swallowed so the bot token in the URL never reaches a log.

heading: Decisions log > Settled decisions > 2026-10-20 · P05 flow engine: re-entry, erasure, replay
text: - **Why:** privacy review of P05 (erasure must be complete; token must not leak). Replay returns the current step because the earlier auto messages are not state. - **Alternatives:** keep consent history as an audit record (rejected: erasure means erasure). - **Confirmed by:** pending Gopi.

heading: Decisions log > Settled decisions > 2026-10-20 · Cohort space, mentor pages, coach pages
text: - **Decision:** each cohort gets a small thread (a code-chosen weekly prompt, and replies from teachers, the mentor, the coach and the system), a mentor page set and a coach page set. The thread is relayed by the bot in Telegram and shown at `/cohort` in the PWA, so teachers on either channel see one conversation. Display names are chosen by the teacher; handles and phone numbers are never shown. Every post passes the PII validator (child names, roll numbers) and the call 7 pre-filter; moderation is after the fact with a Report button; a flagged post is held until the coach decides. AI never writes a post. Mentor recordings and method-card steps move draft → submitted → awaiting_coach → approved (or changes requested, or rejected) and are "in use" only once a published track version includes them; nothing a mentor records reaches a teacher before the coach approves it. Cohorts move proposed → active → closing → closed, each transition audited. The **coach** is the reviewer extended (assigned per cohort by the programme officer, 30-minute weekly cap; one person may be coach and officer). Thread text is deleted 30 days after the cohort closes (and in every case within 90 days of the last post or cancellation). The filter is best-effort and local; no thread text goes to Claude; joining is a separate consent; coaches and mentors see pseudonyms and cohort medians only. Built as P11 steps 7–16; P12 renames the reviewer role to coach and adds "Posts and replies" to the funnel as a system-labelled engagement count, never as adoption.

heading: Decisions log > Settled decisions > 2026-10-20 · Cohort space, mentor pages, coach pages
text: - **Why:** peers matter to how teachers pick up tools (36% of EdTech-using teachers find tools through peers: BaSE 57, EdTech users only; BaSE 67 is not in `docs/design/evidence-digest.md`, so it is not used); support posts are overloaded or vacant (FLN 58 for one State, FLN 59, 110; NITI 145, 147: see the digest for scope); and the institution cannot see what reaches teachers (G4): the approval queue and cohort status make it visible. These support the design; they do not show a moderated thread works, which the pilot tests.

text: - **Alternatives rejected:** a Telegram group per cohort (exposes handles and phone numbers); an unmoderated chat; AI answering in the thread (rule 1, rule 15).

heading: Decisions log > Settled decisions > 2026-10-20 · Cohort space, mentor pages, coach pages
text: - **Confirmed by:** Gopi for the design. Raising this role's weekly cap from 15 minutes (reviewer) to 30 (coach) is a cap change under rule 12: Gopi confirmed it in this entry; OD-15 stays with Seema for the pilot. This entry supersedes the wording in the "Roles, profile, backup" entry that the "officer" label is replaced by coach: the programme officer remains a separate role, and the coach is the reviewer extended.

heading: Decisions log > Settled decisions > 2026-10-20 · Roles, profile, backup, multiple classes, consent, feedback and admin
text: - **Decision:** at Gopi's request: (1) roles are now **teacher, coach, mentor, admin** (plus **judge** for the demo); the old "officer" label is replaced by **coach** (a DIET-like person who holds the reviewer and programme-officer duties of `CLAUDE.md` section 5; one person may still hold both); the mentor is one of the teachers and sees the teacher screens as well. Each role has its own home and menu; the role switcher is a demo mechanism until real sign-in exists. (2) **My profile** holds classes (add, rename, switch, delete: several classes per teacher), storage (the app asks the browser for persistent storage and shows the answer), backup (export and restore a file, optionally sealed with a passphrase: AES-GCM, PBKDF2 200,000 iterations), **data used** (bytes of the app's own calls counted on the phone, a cost from a price per GB she types, and a Clear button), privacy and feedback. (3) **DPDP**: a notice in three languages, four consent switches all off by default (counts, AI in the Practice Class, sharing rehearsals, feedback), versioned consent records on the phone and on the server under a random device id, withdrawal in one tap, erase-everything (phone plus `DELETE /api/classes/{id}`), class counts and feedback sent only with consent. (4) **Feedback**: anonymous app, content, simulation and card-flag feedback stored in the `feedback` table (text up to 500 characters, refused if it holds a phone number, email or ID number); the **admin** page lists feedback and the teachers' simulation observations, filters them and marks them reviewed with a note. Admin endpoints need `ADMIN_KEY` when it is set; with it unset they are open (judge demo and local dev) and the page says so. (5) **UI**: an icon set, toasts, tiles and panels (`docs/ui-guidelines.md`); the card's speaker icon answers with a toast. Flags now go to the admin instead of staying on the phone.

heading: Decisions log > Settled decisions > 2026-10-20 · Roles, profile, backup, multiple classes, consent, feedback and admin
text: - **Why:** teachers could not carry their work to a new phone, keep two sections, see what the app costs them, control what is shared, or tell the team what they think; the admin had nowhere to read it. - **Constraints kept:** no per-child data or photo on the server; feedback and observations are anonymous; nothing is sent before the matching consent; counts only, no percentages; simulated data labelled.

heading: Decisions log > Settled decisions > 2026-10-20 · Responsive layout, "What I entered", "My programme", classroom observation
text: - **Decision:** at Gopi's request: (1) the phone frame is gone on wide screens; the app is a fluid column from 320 px up to a centred 1000 px, with a scrolling bottom menu, tested at 320, 360, 768 and 1280 px for sideways scrolling; (2) **What I entered** lists every check on the phone (children, how many came from a photo, class counts sent or waiting) and shows the answers on request; photos stay unstored, answers stay on the phone; (3) **My programme** (`GET /api/programme/{class_id}`) shows check, track, cohort, mentor and lessons status in counts only; a real class not yet placed is told "waiting"; a simulated class sees a labelled example placement from the simulated block; lessons and the model-lesson script show "none published yet" until the content pipeline (P09/P10) exists; a mentor invitation is said to follow the next check; (4) **Class observation**: after trying it in class she answers "were the children like the pretend ones" and picks what differed from six fixed choices; stored on the phone and sent as choices only (no free text, no class id) to `sim_observations`; the summary endpoint hides anything under 5 reports. The Practice Class sub-tabs were renamed so they no longer overwrite the bottom menu styles.

heading: Decisions log > Settled decisions > 2026-10-20 · Responsive layout, "What I entered", "My programme", classroom observation

heading: Decisions log > Settled decisions > 2026-10-19 · Practice Class: review tab, her own impact tag, cue card, language follow-through
text: - **Decision:** at Gopi's request the Practice Class screen gained (1) a **Review** tab: every rehearsal is recorded in IndexedDB on the phone (turns with the move she used, language, seed, feedback card), listed newest first, replayed turn by turn, with the moves she used counted, and deletable one by one or all at once; (2) an **impact tag** she sets herself on a rehearsal (It helped, No difference, It did not help), shown as counts in the Review summary: it is her own private note on the phone, it is not a score, it is not sent anywhere, and nothing in the product reads it as a judgement of her (rules 3, 11); (3) a **cue card** ("What can I say?"): the move list's example lines in her language, with the example child's name swapped for one of her five children, plus four generic delivery tips (a move that silences children is never cued); (4) **language follow-through**: the session is created in the app's current language, the goal, tips, cues and feedback arrive in it, and if she changes language mid-rehearsal a banner offers a restart in the new language with the same children.

heading: Decisions log > Settled decisions > 2026-10-19 · Photo reading in the v1 Check page (first slice of P08)
text: - **Decision:** Gopi asked for a photo option in the Check page: the teacher photographs one child's sheet, call 8 reads it blind on the server, the boxes fill in, she checks and corrects them and goes to the next child. Built now in the v1 PWA as an interim slice of P08 (`POST /api/sheets/read`, `ai/calls/c08_answer_reading.py`, `docs/answer-reading.md`). The photo is held in server memory for the call only (never on disk or in logs, capped at 800 KB), is not stored on the phone, and the reads go back to the phone; nothing about them is stored on the server. Code judges the reads (confidence at least 0.8 and an answer the item recognises, else "check"); every box is still the teacher's to confirm. P08 replaces this with the two-channel check flow (queued photos, confirm steps, in-memory reads with a 30-minute TTL, Telegram message deletion) and the eval 9 accuracy run; until then no accuracy is claimed.

heading: Decisions log > Settled decisions > 2026-10-19 · Two channels, one back end
text: - **Decision:** teacher and mentor flows run on both Telegram and the PWA. Each flow is defined once in a channel-neutral flow engine as steps (message, choice, photo batch, number grid, voice, media, link), and thin adapters render them per channel. A teacher has one pseudonymous id across channels and can use either or both. The Practice Class and the officer and reviewer screens stay web only. WhatsApp will be a third adapter. Privacy is the same on every channel: per-sheet reads in server memory only, photos deleted after reading, class counts stored.

heading: Decisions log > Settled decisions > 2026-10-19 · Two channels, one back end

If behind, cut-list item 11 trims PWA web push and PWA voice reflections first.

heading: Decisions log > Settled decisions > 2026-10-19 · Changes from the Challenge 3 evidence review
text: - **Decision:** (1) reviewer and programme officer are roles that a BRC, CRC, DIET faculty member or head teacher can hold, each working from one weekly batch; nothing auto-approves. (2) A model run (audio of the move done well with the same simulated class, built from approved content and reviewed) plays before rehearsal. (3) An officer funnel, Delivered → Tried → Practised → Changed, with source labels; no completion figure alone. (4) Call 9, the reflection pointer: one approved next step after a voice reflection. (5) An optional CRC visit brief, opt-in, with no numbers. (6) Time caps. (7) A mixed-level persona flag.

heading: Decisions log > Settled decisions > 2026-10-19 · Changes from the Challenge 3 evidence review
text: - **Why:** support posts are overloaded or vacant (FLN 58, 59, 110; NITI 145, 147); training rarely demonstrates or lets teachers practise (FLN 56; NITI 147); monitoring tracks inputs (FLN 54, 72, 73); classroom feedback is rare (AIC 74; NITI 147, 148); teacher time is scarce (FLN 25, 27; NITI 146, 185); most schools are multigrade (FLN 35; NITI 139, 150). Sources: `docs/design/evidence-digest.md`.

heading: Decisions log > Settled decisions > 2026-10-19 · Changes from the Challenge 3 evidence review
text: - **Rejected:** recording real lessons for AI feedback (one 50-teacher pilot where 68% were comfortable recording, AIC 75; children's voices would enter the data); video exemplars (data cost); grouping by teacher age or experience (the BaSE splits are about EdTech adoption; IDR 3 is anecdote); teacher-chosen courses or credits (opinion only, IDR 4–6); CRCs as coaches; admin automation (off-challenge).

heading: Decisions log > Settled decisions > 2026-10-19 · Changes from the Challenge 3 evidence review
text: - **Bets where sources disagree:** training alone doesn't change practice (FLN 136, 140), but practice plus feedback plus follow-through might (FLN 64; AIC 39, 75), and the next check decides. The problem is too much of the wrong training, so tracks are targeted and capped. We attack quality and sidestep access with teachers' own phones (BaSE 53, 56). Simulated practice is untested in every source and is presented as a hypothesis. - **Confirmed by:** Gopi.

heading: Decisions log > Settled decisions > 2026-10-17 · P07 verified Sarvam facts
text: - **Decision:** the speech layer is built on these facts, read from Sarvam's docs on 2026-10-17 (nothing here was confirmed with a live call: the key in `.env` is rejected, see the next entry). 1. **Auth:** header `api-subscription-key`. Errors have the shape `{"error": {"request_id", "message", "code"}}`; codes include `invalid_api_key_error`, `rate_limit_exceeded_error`, `insufficient_quota_error`. 429 and 503 are retried with backoff. Source: https://docs.sarvam.ai/api-reference/authentication and https://docs.sarvam.ai/api/getting-started/ratelimits

heading: Decisions log > Settled decisions > 2026-10-17 · P07 verified Sarvam facts
text: 2. **Speech-to-text:** `POST https://api.sarvam.ai/speech-to-text`, multipart `file`, `model` (`saaras:v4` default and recommended, `saaras:v3` available; `saaras:v2.5` is deprecated and uses a different endpoint), `language_code` (BCP-47: `hi-IN`, `ta-IN`, `en-IN`, or `unknown` to detect), `input_audio_codec` (only for raw PCM, 16 kHz), `with_timestamps`, `keyterms` (up to 50, v4 only). **Real-time limit 30 seconds**; the batch API takes up to 2 hours. Accepted formats include WAV, MP3, AAC, OGG, OPUS, FLAC, MP4, AMR, WMA and **WebM**, so the phone's Opus-in-WebM could be sent as is; we still transcode to 16 kHz mono WAV so chunking at silences is exact. Response: `request_id`, `transcript`, `language_code`, `language_probability` (only when the language is detected), `timestamps` (only with `with_timestamps`). Source: https://docs.sarvam.ai/api-reference/speech-to-text/transcribe

heading: Decisions log > Settled decisions > 2026-10-17 · P07 verified Sarvam facts
text: 3. **Text-to-speech:** `POST https://api.sarvam.ai/text-to-speech`, JSON `text` (2,500 characters on v3 and v4-flash, 1,500 on v2; use commas in numbers over 4 digits), `language_code` (the field is `language_code`, not `target_language_code`), `speaker` (case-sensitive, must match the model), `model` (`bulbul:v3` is the default if omitted; `bulbul:v4-flash` is the new recommended model with the same contract; `bulbul:v2` is legacy), `pace`, `speech_sample_rate`, `output_audio_codec`, `temperature`, `dict_id`. **`pitch` and `loudness` exist on `bulbul:v2` only.** **`opus` is a validation error on v3 and v4-flash**: use `mp3` or `wav`, then encode to OGG/Opus ourselves. Response: `{"request_id", "audios": [base64]}`. Source: https://docs.sarvam.ai/api-reference/text-to-speech/convert and https://docs.sarvam.ai/api/getting-started/models/bulbul

heading: Decisions log > Settled decisions > 2026-10-17 · P07 verified Sarvam facts
text: 4. **Voices:** v3 has 30+ named speakers (Shubh default; Aditya, Ritu, Priya, Neha, Rahul, Pooja, Rohan, Simran, Kavya, Amit, Dev, Ishita, Shreya, Ratan, Varun, Manan, Sumit, Roopa, Kabir, Aayan, Ashutosh, Advait, Anand, Tanya, Tarun, Sunny, Mani, Gokul, Vijay, Shruti, Suhani, Mohit, Kavitha, Rehan, Soham, Rupali). v4-flash has 200+ persona voices named like `simran_en_customer`; v3 names are not valid on it. The v2 speaker list is not published.

heading: Decisions log > Settled decisions > 2026-10-17 · P07 verified Sarvam facts
text: 5. **Voice cloning (beta):** `POST /voices/create` (multipart: `file` 10 to 15 s recommended and up to 50 MB, `name`, `language`; returns `data.voice_id`) then `POST /voices/clone` with the `voice_id` (its request fields are not documented). Voice count is capped by plan tier. No licence terms are published on the page. Source: https://docs.sarvam.ai/api-reference/voice-cloning

heading: Decisions log > Settled decisions > 2026-10-17 · P07 verified Sarvam facts
text: 6. **Pronunciation dictionary:** `POST /text-to-speech/pronunciation-dictionary` (multipart `file`, a `.json` with a `pronunciations` object keyed by language code; the entry shape is in the guide, not the reference), returns `dictionary_id`, passed as `dict_id` in TTS. Only v3 and v4-flash. Limits: 10 dictionaries, 100 words each, 1 MB. Source: https://docs.sarvam.ai/api-reference/pronunciation-dictionary 7. **Rate limits (Starter):** speech-to-text REST 60 requests a minute; text-to-speech REST 60 (30 on v3); voice cloning 10 sustained. 429 body `{"error": {"message": "Rate limit exceeded", "code": "rate_limit_exceeded_error"}}`.

heading: Decisions log > Settled decisions > 2026-10-17 · P07 verified Sarvam facts
text: 8. **Prices (INR):** speech-to-text 30 per hour of audio (billed per second); Bulbul v3 30 per 10,000 characters; instant voice cloning 30 per 10,000 characters; new accounts get 100 in credits. Stored in `services/speech/pricing.yaml`. Source: https://docs.sarvam.ai/api/getting-started/pricing

Three of these differ from CLAUDE.md or the design: the TTS field is `language_code`; Opus output is refused on v3, so OGG/Opus is made with ffmpeg; and `bulbul:v4-flash` now exists (Voice Agents on v3 end on 10 Nov 2026, per Sarvam's landing page; the REST API is not said to end). - **Alternatives:** the finguru voice server (decided against on 2026-10-16). - **Confirmed by:** pending Gopi (facts only).

heading: Decisions log > Settled decisions > 2026-10-17 · P07 the Sarvam key in `.env` is rejected

heading: Decisions log > Settled decisions > 2026-10-17 · P07 voice design
text: - **Decision:** (1) Child voices use stock Bulbul v3 speakers whose pitch is raised with ffmpeg (`asetrate`, `aresample`, `atempo`: pitch up, speed unchanged), because v3 has no pitch control and v2's speaker list is unpublished; each of the 12 personas has a fixed speaker and pitch ratio in `content/voices/children.v1.yaml`, so a child sounds the same every session and five children in a session sound different. Cloned voices are built behind `SARVAM_CLONES=1`, off by default and untested live. Licence policy: licence-cleared AI-designed voices or a consenting adult; never a real child. (2) Speech goes out as OGG/Opus mono at 24 kbps (about 3 KB a second), returned inline as base64 in the voice-turn response. (3) Speech-to-text gets 16 kHz mono WAV chunks of at most 28 seconds, cut at silences. (4) Text-to-speech runs in parallel with call 7; audio is released only if the check passes, otherwise the template line is synthesised. (5) A circuit breaker opens after 3 consecutive speech failures for 30 seconds; the client also falls back to text after 2 failures or on a 2g connection. (6) `SPEECH_MODE=stub` makes speech-to-text return scripted lines and text-to-speech a generated tone, for tests and demos; it is not speech recognition and says so. (7) Speech calls are logged in a `speech_calls` table (stage, latency, bytes, characters, seconds, cost in INR, error kind), never the audio or text.

heading: Decisions log > Settled decisions > 2026-10-17 · P06 Practice Class UI decisions
text: - **Decision:** (1) The API creates a session with the class's counts (class-level only) and returns the seed, so "try again with the same children" reuses it; `?seed=` in the deep link makes a demo repeatable (the Playwright tests use seed 5 to replay the recorded rehearsal). (2) The AI-layers overlay, AI map and audit pages are judge-role only; they show metadata and the trace, and the audit page never shows what anyone typed. (3) When the day's budget is spent the screen says "Practice is paused for today" and offers a recorded sample rehearsal (`apps/pwa/public/sample-practice.json`, made by `scripts/make_sample_practice.py` from the committed live session); a slow or failed model call shows a template line with a "slow connection" notice; offline shows "Practice needs a connection". (4) "Share this session" is a stored choice only, off by default; no sharing endpoint exists yet. (5) Thumbs up or down per feedback point are saved on the phone with the transcript. (6) CORS: the API answers browsers from `PWA_ORIGIN` only (no wildcard, no credentials); the PWA reads `VITE_API_BASE` for a separately hosted API. (7) Playwright starts the API on port 8011 in recorded mode with its log in `e2e-api.log`, so tests never meet a dev server on 8000 and can check the server log holds no transcript text. (8) The staging deploy is a written recipe (`docs/deploy.md`, `Dockerfile`), not yet run: it needs hosting accounts and secrets from Gopi.

heading: Decisions log > Settled decisions > 2026-10-17 · P06 Practice Class UI decisions
text: - **Why:** the smallest build that meets P06 and keeps what a teacher says on her phone. - **Alternatives:** a server-side transcript store for sharing (rejected for now: needs the opt-in flow of P11); a service-worker cache for practice replies (rejected: the Practice Class is the one live feature). - **Confirmed by:** pending Gopi.

heading: Decisions log > Settled decisions > 2026-10-17 · P05 PWA decisions
text: - **Decision:** (1) No router or state library: a 40-line hash router (deep links work on a static host and offline) and React context. (2) Judge mode is the default role and its strip (role and language) is always on screen; a real teacher build will hide it in P15. (3) Answer keys now carry each item's operands (`a`, `b`), so the app can show a class's own example ("52 − 29 → 37"); still lookups only, regenerated by `python tasks.py export-keys`. (4) The profile that syncs is counts only and the server schema forbids every other field (`extra=forbid`); the class id is a random id made on the phone. (5) The untracked pattern is counted per answer, not per child, so its card says "answers" not "children". (6) Autosave writes one after another, so the last key typed is the last thing saved. (7) The simulated class is generated on the phone from the answer keys (28 children, term 1 and term 2 counts set in `src/lib/demo.ts`) and is labelled simulated wherever it shows. (8) A teacher's "this is wrong" tap on a T3 card is kept in the phone's queue for now; no server endpoint stores flags yet (T3 cards are made by code, not AI). (9) Lighthouse 12 and later have no PWA category, so installability and offline behaviour are asserted by Playwright and Lighthouse supplies performance, accessibility and best-practices. (10) `fake-indexeddb` is a dev dependency, for Vitest only.

heading: Decisions log > Settled decisions > 2026-10-17 · P04 Practice Class decisions
text: - **Decision:** (1) The simulator is `engine/simulator.py`, pure and seeded per turn from (session seed, turn number), so a session replays exactly. (2) Move ids are shared across the four tracked errors (`pose_problem`, `ask_explain`, `show_bundles`, `exchange_ten`, `check_back`, `tell_rule`, `praise`, `scold`, plus `show_chart` and `regroup_ten` where they fit); effect values follow CLAUDE.md section 5, and the two not listed there (`exchange_ten` -0.3, `regroup_ten` -0.3, `show_chart` -0.3) are placeholders for Seema. (3) The PV-HEARD scenario uses the design's 2-digit dictations (forty-three, 403) although the check items are 3-digit; both are valid for the bug functions. (4) If she names no child, the child she was talking to continues; a line to the class lets the engine choose the speaker by engagement. (5) A tap on the materials tray is a move without a labeller call and counts as evidence for the rubric ("[tapped bundles]"). (6) A scolded child is quiet for 2 turns; scolding changes engagement, never strength. (7) The Tamil number-word list leaves out ஒன்று, பத்து and நூறு, because they are also the Tamil place-value words a child's working must say. (8) Child-line readability allows 20 words per sentence (was 12), because a child's step-by-step working is one sentence; the 30-word cap is unchanged. (9) `AI_MODE=stub` and `CallContext(mode="stub")` run a rule-based stand-in for the model with no spend; audit rows say `stub`. (10) Live result files are separate from code-only ones (`redteam_live.json`, `sim_fidelity_live.json`). (11) The red-team seed set grew from 12 to 22 (10 injection lines typed to the Practice Class); the bar (0 unsafe reach a teacher) is unchanged.

heading: Decisions log > Settled decisions > 2026-10-16 · P03 design choices
text: - **Decision:** (1) The audit trail stores metadata only for every call: ids, hashes, token counts, cost, validator codes. It never stores prompt or output text; reviewed content lives in `review_items`. (2) Judge-mode traffic ignores `AI_BUDGET_USD_TOTAL` and `AI_BUDGET_USD_DAILY` (the judging reserve) but stops at a new hard ceiling `AI_BUDGET_USD_HARD` (default 500). (3) Recorded mode with no recording counts as a failed call and goes to the deterministic fallback, so tests show the fallback path rather than crash. (4) Schemas for calls 1 to 8 are minimal and may grow in P04 to P09; prompts for calls 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8 are v1 drafts until their phase. (5) Hindi and Tamil number-word lists and profanity lists are first drafts for native review (`TODO-HUMAN(Shivani, Gopi)`).

heading: Decisions log > Settled decisions > 2026-10-16 · P02 clarifications and deviations
text: - **Decision:** (1) Same-term candidate mentors need at least 10 children checked (the check's own floor); the spec gave none. (2) The comparison-group improver drops the "beats the comparison group's average" rule: she is in the comparison group. (3) A pilot with no untrained error at p of at least 10% at pre-test has no baseline, so extra fall is undefined and the verdict is inconclusive. (4) Bootstrap estimate and interval are rounded to 9 places before comparing with a threshold, so float noise cannot flip a verdict at exactly -10. (5) Cohorts follow the spec literally (15 to 20, at most 2 per school); where the pool cannot fill a cohort of 15, it is flagged undersized rather than padded, and teachers who do not fit are returned as unplaced. (6) The simulated block uses 3 Grade 3 sections per school and one block, so demo cohorts are small. (7) Planted effects are set as `extra_fix` (extra chance a child's error is fixed): SUB-SFL v1 0.36 for about 20 points, SUB-NODEC v1 0.00. The value was chosen to match the design's "about 20 points", not to reach a verdict. (8) Eval 8 simulates classes with binomial child counts rather than the full answer-sheet model, for speed; effects vary class to class (sd 5 points). (9) Tables are created with `create_all`; the first Alembic migration waits for a stable API schema (P03 or P09). (10) Hypothesis deadlines are off (timing flake on a loaded machine; logic unchanged).

heading: Decisions log > Settled decisions > 2026-10-16 · P01 spec clarifications
text: - **Decision:** (1) The eligibility boundary "p = 0.25 with 10 checked" cannot occur (2.5 children); the engine compares `count × 4 ≥ checked` with integers and tests 3 of 12 and 4 of 16 (eligible) and 3 of 13 (not). The 10-children minimum is tested separately. (2) `class_profile(children)` takes no `form` argument (it was unused). (3) Numbers with a zero digit have no heard or reversed answer. (4) Normaliser keeps a leading-zero string as its number ("034" → 34); more than 9 digits or any non-digit is unreadable. (5) Children checked counts every diagnosed child, including ones with blank or unreadable boxes. (6) Answer sheets crossed out and rewritten ("use the last answer") is a reading-step rule (P08), not an engine rule.

heading: Decisions log > 2026-10-31 · Practice Class: a chorus of one to three children, overheard moves, and a switch for call 7 and for call 1
text: - **Decision (Gopi, 2026-10-31).** (1) Each teacher turn now has one to three speaking children, chosen by the engine (the named child first, then others weighted by engagement; the shy child only when named; a child who went quiet stays out). (2) The class shares one room: a move aimed at one child reaches every other child as something overheard, at `overhear` (0.5) of its effect on strength and engagement; going quiet applies only to the child it was aimed at. Both are tuning parameters in the scenario files (`overhear`, `chorus_max`); the engine's defaults (0 and 1) keep the old one-child behaviour. (3) `.env` `PRACTICE_SKIP_CHECKER=1` leaves out call 7 on a child's line; the code validators (numbers, length, script, subtitle) and the pre-filter still run on every AI line, and a line that fails them is still replaced by the template. (4) `.env` `PRACTICE_AI_INTENTS=explain,work_aloud` sends only those kinds of line to call 1; every other line (an answer, an agree, a thanks) is the engine's template. The children who join in as the chorus always speak in template words: they give their own answer, which a template carries whole.

heading: Decisions log > 2026-10-31 · Practice Class: a chorus of one to three children, overheard moves, and a switch for call 7 and for call 1
text: - **Why.** A live turn took a median of 5.1 s and 7.7% of turns passed 12 s (the label, child-line and check calls run one after another). A child's line is made from numbers the engine chose, so most of it is mechanical; only a child explaining her working needs a model. And the children sit in one room.

heading: Decisions log > 2026-11-01 · Edit and delete a paper (Gopi, by request)
text: - **Edit.** An imported paper is edited in place (`POST /api/paper-hub/papers/{id}/items`): numbers or include only, code recomputes every key and probe, and the paper goes back to "confirmed" and, if a reviewer had approved it, back into the review queue. A generated paper is never changed in place: Edit saves a **new paper** through the existing custom-paper path (always reviewed, constraints checked, the original untouched). A paper that is in use cannot change; saving then makes a new version.

heading: Decisions log > 2026-11-01 · Edit and delete a paper (Gopi, by request)
text: - **Delete.** `DELETE /api/paper-hub/papers/{id}` removes the paper, its items, its review rows and its assignments (only withdrawn ones can exist), after a confirmation step in the screen. It is refused while a sheet of a check is entered on it or an assignment is live; deleting a pre-test also deletes its post-test twin if that is unused, and is refused if the twin is in use. The events stay as the audit trail ("deleted"). Who: a coach, the class's own teacher or mentor, or the person who imported it.

heading: Decisions log > 2026-11-01 · Edit and delete a paper (Gopi, by request)
text: - **Change to `store.freeze`.** A post-test twin is frozen when made, so `freeze` did nothing when its first sheet was entered. It now records the "first sheet entered" event in that case too (no column changes), so use of a twin is known.

heading: Decisions log > 2026-11-01 · Edit and delete a paper (Gopi, by request)

heading: Decisions log > 2026-11-01 · Edit changes the paper itself, with no copy (Gopi: "Don't create a copy"; supersedes the Edit part above)

heading: Decisions log > 2026-10-31 · A check is entered on the chosen paper's own key; no Form A / Form B for a teacher
text: **Decision.** Enter check asks for a paper that exists (made on Papers, with its answer key) and nothing else. text: **Decision.** The answers are `worked`, `partly`, `not_yet` and `not_tried` (the old `tried` is now `worked`; rows made earlier are rewritten by `services/modules/migrate.py` at start). `not_tried` is a HOLD, never a result: the module stays open (not `feedback_given`), the planned dates and the end date move by `MODULE_DEFER_DAYS` (7) at most `MODULE_MAX_DEFERRALS` (2) times, the second deferral records a `coach_notified` event, and after it the daily job makes the planned module as `no_feedback` with the reason "you had not tried it yet".

heading: Decisions log > 2026-11-02 · Four answers on a module, and the not-tried hold (Part A)
text: "Get the next module" always works while held. Why-not-yet chips (no time, materials, not sure how, absent, other) are kept as private events; coaches see only counts, with "not tried" in its own column. **Defaults I chose.** (1) The first deferral happens when she answers; the second is made by the daily job when the moved date arrives (a repeated "not tried" press does not defer twice).

heading: Channels: one back end, thin adapters > Identity
text: A teacher has one random id (`t-` plus 16 hex). A device id (web) or chat id (Telegram) is linked to it. To use the second channel she asks for an 8-character code (15 minutes, one use) and sends it to the bot (`/start CODE`) or types it in the web app.

heading: Channels: one back end, thin adapters > Identity
text: Her other record on that channel is erased on linking. `/stop` in Telegram, and "Delete my data" in either channel, ask once and then erase the teacher, links, flow state, her consent history and her class counts everywhere.

heading: Channels: one back end, thin adapters > Adding a channel
text: 1. Write `channels/<name>/` with a function that turns its incoming event into `(step_id, option_id)` and a sender that shows `Message` objects from `base.render_turn`. 2. Import nothing from `engine/` or `ai/` (`tests/channels/test_import_rule.py` fails otherwise). 3. Add the channel to `tests/channels/test_golden.py`: the same scripted answers must show the same words and choices and leave the same stored state as the web adapter.

text: | Step | Telegram | Web app | | Lesson (`media`) | A voice note (OGG/Opus) fetched from a signed lesson link, the words as its caption, or as a following message when long; the badge line is part of the words | A lesson card with the words and an audio player on the same link | | Taps (`choice`) | Inline buttons, callback data `step:option` | Buttons |

heading: Channels: one back end, thin adapters > T4 and T6: lessons, two taps, my result (P10)
text: | Model lesson | A message with the script and the badge line | A card | | Rehearse (`link`) | A button that opens the Practice Class with a signed link | A link | | My result | Messages, counts only | Cards, counts only | Lessons come only from a published manifest (a track version both keys switched on). Taps are self-report, stored per lesson per pseudonymous teacher id, and shown to officers as counts.

heading: Channels: one back end, thin adapters > T4 and T6: lessons, two taps, my result (P10)
text: Not built (cut in P10): the call 9 reflection pointer, voice reflections and the biweekly "Still using it?" prompts. Offline replay of a downloaded lesson in the web app is not built either; a lesson is fetched when it is opened.

heading: Channels: one back end, thin adapters > Known gaps
text: Photo, voice and number-grid steps have no adapter rendering yet (P08 and P10). The webhook sender does not retry; a failed send is dropped. Telegram's Bot API cannot confirm a message was read.

heading: Cohort space (P11, reduced scope)
text: A small, moderated, pseudonymous thread for the teachers of one cohort, with a lifecycle a coach runs and an approval step for what a mentor offers. Built in `services/api/cohorts/`; screens at `#/cohort` (teacher and coach). Tests: `tests/cohorts/`.

heading: Cohort space (P11, reduced scope) > Lifecycle
text: Every transition leaves an audit row (role, a pseudonymous id, the action; never post text). The thread is **open** only while the cohort is active and has at least 5 members; otherwise it is read-only and the prompts still show. Figures over fewer than 5 teachers (members, schools) are hidden.

heading: Cohort space (P11, reduced scope) > Mentor items
text: Editing an item in use makes a new draft version; the old one stays in use until the new one is approved. A coach decides only items in her own cohorts. **Nothing reaches a teacher unless approved.**

heading: Cohort space (P11, reduced scope) > Who sees what
text: | Person | Sees | Never sees | | Teacher | The visible posts of a cohort she joined, under labels like "Teacher 3" | Who is behind a label; held or hidden posts | | Mentor | Her own cohorts: status and cohort-level figures; her own items; the thread she mentors | A member list, a teacher id, a school or class |

heading: Cohort space (P11, reduced scope) > Who sees what
text: | Coach | Her assigned cohorts, the thread with held and reported posts, her cohort's mentor items | Cohorts she is not assigned to. **She can map a label to a teacher** (the coach and admin can; peers cannot) | | Officer | All cohorts: status and figures under the same under-5 rule | Post text | No handle, phone number or teacher id is in any response (a test checks every route).

heading: Cohort space (P11, reduced scope) > Posting checks (best effort, rule based, never sent to a model)
text: Every post is checked in code (`ai/validators/thread.py`): a first name from a list in three scripts, a roll-number phrase (the words "roll no" or "no." followed by a number), a name with a relationship word ("Rahul's sister"), a phone number, an email or an ID-like number, and the pre-filter (harsh words, markup). A failed check stores nothing and asks her to rewrite.

heading: Cohort space (P11, reduced scope) > Posting checks (best effort, rule based, never sent to a model)
text: If the check cannot run, the post is held. **This is a filter, not a guarantee**: a teacher can still describe a child without a name. Compensating controls: a notice at the compose step in three languages, a 500-character cap, a Report button (a reported post is held and invisible to others until the coach decides) and a fast hide. If the coach marks a post as identifying a child, its text is erased at once.

heading: Cohort space (P11, reduced scope) > Posting checks (best effort, rule based, never sent to a model)
text: A teacher can delete her own posts.

heading: Cohort space (P11, reduced scope) > Retention (`thread.purge`, run by the officer route; schedule it daily in production)
text: | What | When the text goes | | Reported, hidden or held post | 7 days after the decision (at once for an identifier) | | Thread text of a closed cohort | 30 days after it closed | | Any post | 90 days after it was written (stricter than "90 days after the last post") | | A deleted post | at once | Audit rows keep ids, rule codes and counts only.

heading: Cohort space (P11, reduced scope) > Not built (cut, see DECISIONS 2026-10-27 and PARKING)
text: The Telegram relay of the thread, voice replies and notifications, the mentor recording flow (M1), call 4 (method cards) and call 6 (the weekly digest), the mentor pages in the PWA (the routes exist: `/api/cohorts/mentor/*`), real role assignment (P12; until then a person is a pseudonymous id the judge deployment lets a request name). A mentor's name is never shown in the thread: a mentor posts as "Mentor".

heading: Cohort space (P11, reduced scope) > Officer cohort screen and the review wait (27 Oct)
text: The officer page now has a Cohorts panel (`apps/pwa/src/components/OfficerCohorts.tsx`): propose a cohort for one tracked error with a coach id and a school count, then Activate, Start closing, Close (post-test received, or without it with a written reason) or Cancel. The buttons shown are the ones the current status allows; the server enforces the same lifecycle and writes an audit row for every change (`services/api/cohorts/lifecycle.py`). Member counts under 5 show as "fewer than 5".

heading: Cohort space (P11, reduced scope) > Officer cohort screen and the review wait (27 Oct)
text: Mentors are not assigned here yet (parked), and the coach id is a pseudonymous id typed in, not a role assignment with consent. The funnel also shows content waiting for review: how many items are pending or awaiting the mentor, how many for more than 7 days, and the age of the oldest (`review_waiting` in `/api/officer/funnel`, source "system: review queue ages"). Gates never auto-approve, so this is the queue's age made visible, not a deadline.

heading: Content pipeline: from a draft to a lesson a teacher hears
text: Built in P09 (26 to 27 Oct). It carries the SUB-SFL track (six lessons and one model-lesson script) from the model to a published manifest, and nothing in it removes a gate. The pilot's three template lessons use the same gates and the same review tables (`docs/build/reports/PILOT-MODE.md`).

heading: Content pipeline: from a draft to a lesson a teacher hears > What is code and what is the model
text: | Step | Who | Why | | Which parts exist, which strategies, which languages | Data: `content/tracks/sub-sfl.v1/track.yaml`, `content/strategies/`, `content/templates/` | Seema owns it; code never hard-codes it | | The words of a lesson | Call 5 (Claude Opus), one part per request | The only free-writing step | | Every class number | Code, as a slot filled at delivery from the cohort's pooled counts | Rule 1: Claude never states a number about a class |

heading: Content pipeline: from a draft to a lesson a teacher hears > What is code and what is the model
text: | Every sum | Code (arithmetic validator). A child's intended mistake carries a `[child: 37]` tag the validator accepts | A wrong sum is blocked before the queue | | A check item (Form A or B) in an example | Code (check-items validator) | The forms stay a clean measure | | "Is this fit for a teacher" | Call 7, then a person | Gate 2 and gate 3 |

heading: Content pipeline: from a draft to a lesson a teacher hears > What is code and what is the model
text: | Approval, activation | People: coach, then officer | Neither key alone publishes |

heading: Content pipeline: from a draft to a lesson a teacher hears > The two keys and versions
text: A track version moves draft, in review, approved (the coach's key), active (the officer's key), retired. An edit makes a new version while the old one stays in use until the new one is active. Every step writes an audit row with the role and the actor; the audit row of an activation holds both keys. Settings the programme may tune (for example the stage-routine threshold) have fixed ranges and go through the same two keys (`services/content/configurable.py`).

heading: Content pipeline: from a draft to a lesson a teacher hears > Rejections feed the checker
text: A return needs one structured reason. The rejection waits in `content/rejections/pending/`; the coach may promote it to `approved/`, and only then does the next call 7 prompt include it as "rejected before, and why". The audit row records which example set the checker saw.

heading: Content pipeline: from a draft to a lesson a teacher hears > Publish
text: Only a version that both keys switched on is published. Each lesson is voiced once per language (reused by content hash), kept to about 0.6 MB per 5 minutes, and the manifest lists lesson ids, audio keys, sizes, script text, badge state, reviewer and activation roles and times. Class numbers are the pooled counts of the cohort's classes, computed by code, and a sum that is only wrong with the real numbers is caught before voicing.

heading: Content pipeline: from a draft to a lesson a teacher hears > What was drafted and what came of it
text: The first live run drafted SUB-SFL v1 in Hindi and English (14 parts). All 14 passed the code gates; call 7 passed 2 and held 12 (`docs/evidence/p09_live_draft_run.txt`). **Finding, fixed:** most of those holds said the draft stated a class count.

heading: Content pipeline: from a draft to a lesson a teacher hears > What was drafted and what came of it
text: The cause was in our gate, not the drafts: in slot mode the text is shown to call 7 with sample numbers in place of the `{class.*}` slots, and call 7's own rule is that it states no statistic, so it read the samples as claims. The checker is now told in its trusted input (`slots_note`) that the numbers stand in for slots that code fills at delivery.

heading: Content pipeline: from a draft to a lesson a teacher hears > What was drafted and what came of it
text: A second run in a clean database (`docs/evidence/p09_live_draft_run_after_slots_note.txt`): 12 of 14 reached the coach, 2 held with reasons. The call 7 prompt file did not change; its eval is still P13's job and should include this case. Cost: the script's estimate was USD 0.60 for 14 parts and each full run cost about twice that, so read the estimate as a rough guide.

heading: Content pipeline: from a draft to a lesson a teacher hears > What was drafted and what came of it
text: The local development database also held drafts of some parts from earlier work, so the first run's "queued" marks show only the parts that were new; the cumulative spend is `python tasks.py budget`. Held drafts are not lost: they sit in the queue as `held_by_checker`, and a coach can read, edit (the edit is checked again) and approve them.

heading: Content pipeline: from a draft to a lesson a teacher hears > Not built (cut up front)
text: Tamil lessons (the track file declares `ta` but nothing is drafted), the citations pass 2 ("why this move" lines with citations), stage routines, and a live Message Batches run (the request builder is built and tested on recorded data). The model run (T12) was built on 29 Oct; see "The model run" below.

heading: Content pipeline: from a draft to a lesson a teacher hears > The model run
text: `services/content/model_run.py`. About three minutes of the track's move done well, with the same five simulated children, for a teacher to hear before she rehearses.

heading: Content pipeline: from a draft to a lesson a teacher hears > The model run
text: 1. **Render.** From an *approved* model-lesson script only. The teacher's lines are the script's teacher lines (slots filled with the engine's worked example, tags stripped), nothing else. The move for each line is assigned by code from the track's strategy order (pose the problem, the strategies, praise), and the Practice Class engine and call 1 answer as the children, so every number a child says is the engine's. A fixed seed freezes it.

heading: Content pipeline: from a draft to a lesson a teacher hears > The model run
text: 2. **Review.** It becomes a review item of type `model_run`; the coach approves or returns it (gate 3, audited). The same script version is never rendered twice: a new render needs a new approved script version.

heading: Content pipeline: from a draft to a lesson a teacher hears > The model run
text: 3. **Voice.** Only after approval, once: an adult voice (`ritu`) for the teacher and each child's own stock voice, joined as OGG/Opus mono at 16 kbps (12 kbps if it would pass 0.35 MB per three minutes). The file is named by a hash of its words and voices. 4. **Publish.** The track manifest lists it as a `model_run` part with a caption that says simulated. Routes (coach renders, approves and returns; officer voices): `/api/review/model-runs`.

heading: Content pipeline: from a draft to a lesson a teacher hears > The model run
text: Not built: a screen for it in the review queue (the routes and tests exist), and a live render with call 1 (the tests use the offline stub client).

heading: Deploying staging (and later production)
text: The defaults follow OD-3 in `docs/build/DECISIONS.md`: an always-on small API instance, managed Postgres, S3-compatible storage for published audio, and static hosting for the PWA. No plan that sleeps during 1–10 Nov.

Leave it unset anywhere real teachers are stored: it fails closed |

The API answers browsers from this origin only | | `PUBLIC_BASE_URL` | the API's https URL | | `SARVAM_API_KEY`, `TELEGRAM_*`, `S3_*` | needed from P07, P10 and P09 |

heading: Deploying staging (and later production) > Secrets and settings
text: On the PWA host, set one build variable: `VITE_API_BASE` = the API's https URL (no trailing slash). It is public by nature; it holds no secret.

heading: Deploying staging (and later production) > Steps
text: 0. **Before any deploy: the assistant's reference.** Run the prompt `docs/build/Claude Code prompt refresh the assistant reference before deploy.md` in Claude Code (it brings the help pages and each role's suggested questions up to date for every page), then `python tasks.py predeploy`, which must print `predeploy ok`. The index it rebuilds (`services/assistant/index/`) is copied into the API image, so a deploy without this step ships the old questions and answers.

heading: Deploying staging (and later production) > Steps
text: 1. **Database.** Create a Postgres database; copy the connection string and change the scheme to `postgresql+psycopg://`. Tables are created on first start (Alembic comes with the stable schema; see DECISIONS). 2. **API.** Create a web service from this repo using the `Dockerfile` (it installs `.[prod]` and runs uvicorn on `$PORT`). Choose an always-on plan, set the variables above, deploy. Health check path: `/api/health`.

heading: Deploying staging (and later production) > Steps
text: 3. **PWA.** Create a static site from this repo: root directory `apps/pwa`, build command `npm ci && npm run build`, output directory `dist`, build variable `VITE_API_BASE`. Make sure the host serves `index.html` for the app and `sw.js`, `manifest.webmanifest` and `workbox-*.js` as files. 4. **Link them.** Put the PWA's URL in the API's `PWA_ORIGIN` and redeploy the API. Put the API's URL in the PWA's `VITE_API_BASE` and rebuild the PWA. 5. **Record the URLs** in `docs/build/PROGRESS.md` under Environments.

heading: Deploying staging (and later production) > Verify (run these once it is live)
text: - `curl https://<api>/api/health` returns `{"status":"ok", …}`. - `curl -i -X OPTIONS https://<api>/api/practice/sessions -H "Origin: https://<pwa>" -H "Access-Control-Request-Method: POST"` shows `access-control-allow-origin: https://<pwa>`; the same with another origin shows none. - Open the PWA URL on a phone: it opens straight into judge mode; Load a simulated class; My class shows counts; Practice runs a turn and the child answers (this is the human check for the P06 acceptance on a real phone over mobile data).

heading: Deploying staging (and later production) > Verify (run these once it is live)
text: - `https://<pwa>/#/audit` lists the AI calls just made, with no text anyone typed. - Server logs contain request lines only: search them for a phrase you typed in Practice (there must be no match). - Spend: `python tasks.py budget` against the production database (set `DATABASE_URL`) shows cost per call.

heading: Deploying staging (and later production) > Cold starts and keep-alive
text: A plan that sleeps makes the first judge wait. Use an always-on instance. As a belt and braces, from 1 to 10 Nov an uptime monitor can request `/api/health` every 5 minutes (free tiers of most monitors allow this). The health route never calls an AI model, so keep-alive costs nothing.

heading: Deploying staging (and later production) > Rollback
text: Redeploy the previous image or commit on the API host; on the PWA host, promote the previous deployment. Data in the database is class-level counts and audit metadata only, so a rollback loses nothing a teacher typed.

heading: Design system (v2, 29 Oct 2026: Material 3)
text: A compact token plan for a phone-first app used by primary teachers in sunlight, on cheap Android phones, in Tamil, Hindi and English. v1 (20 Oct) was a blue-ink notebook look; v2 follows the Stitch design file, `docs/design/stitch/DESIGN.md` ("Calm Institutional Material", which is Material 3), on every screen. The decision is logged in `docs/build/DECISIONS.md` (2026-10-29).

heading: Design system (v2, 29 Oct 2026: Material 3) > How to change the look (quick changes)
text: Everything lives in one file, `apps/pwa/src/theme.css`. `styles.css` and `pilot/pilot.css` hold layout and read the tokens; `tests/test_design_tokens.py` fails if a hex colour or an rgba() creeps back into `styles.css`, if a stylesheet uses a token that nothing defines, or if the manifest or icons drift from the primary colour. | To change | Edit | Notes |

heading: Design system (v2, 29 Oct 2026: Material 3) > Colour tokens
text: Containers carry meaning with an icon and a word as well, never colour alone: primary container for the focus (the guided tour, the scenario), tonal (secondary container) for neutral chips and the selected navigation item, tertiary (`warn`) container for what to watch and for offline, success container for what went well, error container for what failed. Buttons and fields that must be seen use `outline` (`#6F7979`, 4.3 on paper, above the 3:1 needed for non-text).

heading: Design system (v2, 29 Oct 2026: Material 3) > Type
text: System fonts only, so nothing is downloaded and Android's Noto Devanagari and Noto Tamil are used: `system-ui, "Noto Sans Devanagari", "Noto Sans Tamil", sans-serif`. Sentence case everywhere; no all-caps labels. | Role | Size and weight | Use | | Count numeral | 40 px, 700 | The "11" in "11 of 28 children" | | Headline | 28 px, 700 | Landing page title | | Title | 24 px, 700 | Screen title |

heading: Design system (v2, 29 Oct 2026: Material 3) > Spacing and shape
text: Scale in px: 4, 8, 12, 16, 24, 32. Tap targets are at least 44 px, and primary buttons and fields 48 px or more. Corners follow Material 3: cards and tiles 16 px, buttons and fields 8 px, chips and notes 12 px, sheets 28 px, the signal pill a soft 16 px. No shadows except the one floating toast.

heading: Design system (v2, 29 Oct 2026: Material 3) > Spacing and shape
text: Hover, focus and press show as a tint of the content colour over the control (a state layer), not a colour change. Screens use one column at 360 px wide.

heading: Design system (v2, 29 Oct 2026: Material 3) > The one memorable element: tally bundles
text: Counts are drawn as sticks: a row of short vertical strokes, grouped in tens and tied with a band, with the children who show the error filled in `stick` and the rest outlined. "11 of 28 children" is read in words and seen as 28 sticks, 11 of them filled. It is SVG, has a text alternative, and is the only decorative element in the app.

heading: Design system (v2, 29 Oct 2026: Material 3) > Components
text: - **Filled button:** `pen` fill, white text, 48 px high, 8 px corners, full width on phones; one per screen. - **Outlined button:** 1 px `outline` border, `pen` text, same size. **Tonal button** (`m-btn-tonal`): `tonal` fill, used for the quieter choice beside a filled one. - **Navigation bar:** four tabs and More on `chalk`; the selected tab shows a `tonal` pill behind its icon and its label in `ink`. More opens a bottom sheet with 28 px top corners.

heading: Design system (v2, 29 Oct 2026: Material 3) > Components
text: - **Chips and notes:** `tonal` or a container colour, 12 px corners, an icon and a word. - **Keypad:** a 3 × 4 grid of 56 px keys (digits, backspace, "blank", "can't read"), because Indian phones' system keyboards switch scripts in the middle of entry. - **Banner:** the "Simulated data" strip on `tonal`, always visible when synthetic data shows, with the word "simulated" in the teacher's language.

heading: Design system (v2, 29 Oct 2026: Material 3) > Components
text: - **Signal pill:** an icon plus a word for online, offline and "will send when connected". Offline uses the tertiary container with a cloud-off icon, and a note under the header says what still works. - **Focus ring:** 3 px `pen` outline with a 2 px offset on every interactive element.

heading: Design system (v2, 29 Oct 2026: Material 3) > Components
text: - **Answer map** (results page): a real table, one button per cell (44 px), roll column fixed while the table scrolls inside its own box. A mistake is colour **and** two letters **and** a pattern: PV-HEARD PH (sky, forward stripes), PV-REVERSE PR (purple, backward stripes), ADD-NOCARRY AC (orange, dots), SUB-SFL SF (green, horizontal stripes), SUB-NODEC SN (yellow, vertical stripes). A confirmed mistake has a solid edge, a "possible" one a dashed edge. The tokens `--heat-ph/pr/ac/sf/sn` are in `theme.css`; `tests/test_design_tokens.py` checks each against `ink` (at least 4.5:1) and that no two are closer than 15 CIE76 units under protan, deutan and tritan simulation.

heading: Design system (v2, 29 Oct 2026: Material 3) > Motion
text: None that carries meaning. State layers fade in 150 ms (`--motion`), and are removed under `prefers-reduced-motion`.

heading: Design system (v2, 29 Oct 2026: Material 3) > Accessibility
text: Body contrast 16.3:1, secondary 8.9:1. Every control has a visible label; audio and icon-only controls have text names. The page language attribute follows the chosen language. Layout is checked at 360 px in the screenshots under `docs/evidence/screenshots/`, and for sideways scrolling at 320, 360, 768 and 1280 px.

heading: Design system (v2, 29 Oct 2026: Material 3) > Larger screens (2026-10-20)

text: - **Who counts as a judge.** Whether a session is a judge session, and so whether every role is selectable, is decided by the server (a signed, expiring judge link or the deployment's judge setting), never by `localStorage`, the header switcher or a request body. heading: Addendum v3.1 (21 Oct 2026): roles, tour, demo modes, content library, strategies, stages > C. Practice Class demo modes (judge mode only) > Try with hints
text: Each turn the server builds three options by code, from `sample_lines` stored per move in the move list: - **strong**: the next unused rubric-aligned move that fits the engine state (for example, ask a child to explain after a wrong answer); - **common mistake**: a move tagged `common_mistake` (just tell the rule, repeat louder, give the answer); - **neutral**: a move tagged `neutral` (for example, "Let's all look at the sticks").

Hint lines are content: they pass the no-check-items validator (section E) and the language and reading-level checks. Free text stays available. Move lists gain, per move: `quality` (`strong`, `common_mistake`, `neutral`) and `sample_lines` per language.

heading: Cohort Coach — Build Stage prototype design > Making this stand out to judges
text: Three small, visible additions, chosen because judges can verify each in seconds by opening the repo or deck, rather than taking a claim on trust.

heading: Cohort Coach — Build Stage prototype design > Making this stand out to judges
text: - **A "verified" tag on every AI-drafted lesson and feedback card a teacher sees**, shown once it has passed the output checker and, where required, a human reviewer. Shows guardrails working, rather than only describing them in the deck. In practice this is one line added to the Telegram message itself — "checked for accuracy ✓" — so a teacher or a judge sees the check happened instead of trusting it occurred in the backend.

heading: Cohort Coach — Build Stage prototype design > Making this stand out to judges
text: - **Live guardrails from rejection feedback.** When Seema or Shivani reject a drafted lesson in the review queue, capture a structured reason — wrong maths, culturally off, too complex for the medium, tone issue, factually shaky — instead of a free-text note. After 20–30 rejections, feed the accumulated examples back into the output checker's prompt (call 7) as "content rejected before, and why": the checker gets stricter over the build, with no retraining.

heading: Cohort Coach — Build Stage prototype design > Making this stand out to judges
text: - **A confidence note on every number in the results deck** — "from 3 classes, read as directional" rather than presenting early numbers as proven. Judges notice false confidence faster than they notice a small sample. - **A cost-per-teacher-per-track figure for all eight Claude calls combined**, in cents. The single clearest signal that this survives past hackathon credits.

heading: Cohort Coach — Build Stage prototype design > Guardrails: further options worth adding
text: - From a look at current practice in LLM safety and child-directed AI, three additions are worth the build time, each cheap relative to what it closes off.

heading: Cohort Coach — Build Stage prototype design > Guardrails: further options worth adding
text: - **A fast rule-based pre-filter ahead of the LLM checker.** Simple keyword and pattern checks catch the obvious bad cases — profanity, off-topic content, malformed answers — before call 7's LLM judge runs at all. Cheaper, faster, and the LLM judge is then only needed for genuine judgment calls, not the easy ones.

heading: Cohort Coach — Build Stage prototype design > Guardrails: further options worth adding
text: - **A Grade-3 reading-level check**, separate from the correctness and safety checks already in call 7. Published research on LLMs and children finds models regularly generate content too complex for the target age, and struggle to tell a second-grader's level from a fourth-grader's. Worth a specific check: does this lesson's language actually fit Grade 3 listening and reading level, not only "is it correct and safe."

heading: Cohort Coach — Build Stage prototype design > Guardrails: further options worth adding
text: - **Explicit injection testing on the Practice Class child simulator.** A teacher can type anything into rehearsal, so the simulated child is exposed to classic "ignore your previous instructions" attempts. Add this as its own red-team category: can a determined teacher talk the simulator out of behaving like a child making her class's error.

heading: Cohort Coach — Build Stage prototype design > Guardrails: further options worth adding
text: - **One shared audit trail, used in two places.** Log every AI call: what triggered it, what it produced, what the checker said, and, if it went to the review queue, who decided and why and when. This single log is the evidence behind the "verified" tag and the rejection-feedback loop above, and it is also the proof behind the user-testing slide: not a separate logging feature, but the record both sections already depend on.

heading: Cohort Coach — Build Stage prototype design > Guardrails: further options worth adding
text: - **Explainability, as its own feature, not the same thing as the audit trail.** The audit trail answers what the system did; explainability answers why. Most of that "why" already exists inside the calls that make each decision — it just gets discarded instead of shown. Surface it as a one-line reason wherever a teacher or officer sees an AI decision: "grouped into this cohort because your class showed 40% SUB-SFL," or "this lesson was held back because the checker flagged a maths error." Cheap to add, because the reasoning is already computed; it only needs a place to be shown.

heading: Cohort Coach — Build Stage prototype design > Decisions at a glance
text: The prototype runs one complete termly loop for one narrow slice: Grade 3 numeracy with four specific errors, on a simulated block. heading: Cohort Coach — Build Stage prototype design > How the loop works
text: One termly check drives everything. Teachers are grouped by what their children get wrong. Teachers whose classes fixed an error supply the next group's track. *[Diagram in the original doc: termly loop · 7 steps, one reinforcing link]* Read it clockwise from the top left. Four kinds of user meet the loop: the Grade 3 teacher, the mentor, the programme officer (block or DIET), and judges through judge mode.
