heading: Cohort Coach — Build Stage prototype design > Deterministic engine
text: Everything a judge must be able to trust is plain, unit-tested code: diagnosis, grouping, comparison, mentor selection and evaluation. Claude never computes or states a number about a class.

heading: Cohort Coach — Build Stage prototype design > Deterministic engine > The four errors
text: Each error is a Python function that turns a problem into the wrong answer a child with that error would give. | Code | Error | Example | Correct | | PV-HEARD | Writes a number the way it is said | "forty-three" → 403 | 43 | | ADD-NOCARRY | Drops the carried ten | 47 + 25 → 62 | 72 |

heading: Cohort Coach — Build Stage prototype design > Deterministic engine > The four errors
text: | SUB-SFL | Takes the smaller digit from the larger in each column | 52 − 29 → 37 | 23 | | SUB-NODEC | Borrows a ten but does not reduce the tens digit | 52 − 29 → 33 | 23 | The item generator builds questions from templates and computes each error's answer with these functions. It rejects any item where two errors give the same wrong answer.

heading: Cohort Coach — Build Stage prototype design > Deterministic engine > The four errors
text: For example, 52 − 27 gives 35 under both SUB-SFL and SUB-NODEC, so that item can't tell them apart. The same generator produces parallel items with new numbers for the next term's check. **Hindi changes the errors.** Hindi number names say the ones first: 43 is *tentalis*, "three-forty". Tamil says the tens first. Hindi-medium classes may therefore show digit reversal (43 → 34) more than PV-HEARD.

heading: Cohort Coach — Build Stage prototype design > Deterministic engine > The four errors
text: Round 1 checks this, and reversal is added as a fifth error, PV-REVERSE, if it is common.

heading: Cohort Coach — Build Stage prototype design > Deterministic engine > Diagnosis
text: - Children write their answers in boxes on a printed sheet, so there are no options to guess from. Each number is read from a photo of the sheet, or tapped in by the teacher. The app already knows which wrong number belongs to which error, and anything else goes under "other". - Proposed 10 items: 2 number-writing, 3 addition with carrying, 4 subtraction with borrowing (each detects both subtraction errors), and 1 anchor subtraction without borrowing.

heading: Cohort Coach — Build Stage prototype design > Deterministic engine > Diagnosis
text: - A child counts as showing an error if her answer matches that error on at least 2 of the items that probe it. - Class prevalence p = children showing the error ÷ children checked. It is computed on the phone, and only the counts sync.

heading: Cohort Coach — Build Stage prototype design > Deterministic engine > Where the answers come from
text: Each class uses the best source it has. Manual entry stays, but only as the fallback. | Source | When it is used | What it saves | In the prototype | | 1. Past exams | The state assessment kept the answer each child wrote, item by item | Skips the check for those items | A CSV importer with a fixed schema, run on a simulated state file |

heading: Cohort Coach — Build Stage prototype design > Deterministic engine > Where the answers come from
text: | 2. Photo of the answer sheet | Default for every termly check | About 10 minutes per class | Built: printed sheet, Claude reads the numbers (call 8), the teacher confirms unsure reads | | 3. Manual taps | No camera, a damaged sheet, or confirming an unsure read | Nothing; this is the fallback | Built | **Why past exams can't replace the check.** Most exam records keep marks, not the answer a child wrote.

heading: Cohort Coach — Build Stage prototype design > Deterministic engine > Where the answers come from
text: A zero on 52 − 29 can't tell 37 from 33, and that difference decides the cohort. Where only marks exist, they rank which classes to check first. Some state tests on OMR sheets do keep the option each child marked. If those options were written as error distractors, they map straight onto the errors.

heading: Cohort Coach — Build Stage prototype design > Deterministic engine > Where the answers come from
text: **The answer sheet.** One sheet per child with 10 numbered answer boxes, rough-work space beside each, and four corner markers so the photo can be straightened. There is no name and no roll-number field. The teacher shoots sheets in roll-number order, so only her phone links a sheet to a child.

heading: Cohort Coach — Build Stage prototype design > Deterministic engine > Grouping
text: 1. A class is eligible for a track when p ≥ 25% and at least 10 children were checked. 2. Each class gets one track per term. PV-HEARD comes first because the others build on it. Otherwise the class gets its highest-p error. 3. Eligible teachers for a track (same grade and medium) are randomly assigned to this term or next term, stratified by baseline p.

heading: Cohort Coach — Build Stage prototype design > Deterministic engine > Grouping
text: 4. This term's teachers are split into cohorts of 15 to 20, with at most 2 from one school and one mentor per cohort. If a block has fewer than 15 eligible teachers, cohorts are formed across neighbouring blocks instead.

heading: Cohort Coach — Build Stage prototype design > Deterministic engine > Comparison group
text: The comparison group is the next-term teachers for the same track. If there is no waitlist, the fallback is a matched group: same grade, medium and school type, with baseline p within 5 points.

heading: Cohort Coach — Build Stage prototype design > Deterministic engine > Mentor selection
text: - **Proven mentor.** Last term her class's p was at least 25%. This term it fell by at least 15 points and by at least half, with at least 15 children checked both times. Her class's fall also beats the comparison group's average fall. She must consent.

heading: Cohort Coach — Build Stage prototype design > Deterministic engine > Mentor selection
text: - **Cold start, before any data exists.** Candidates are classes with the same grade and medium where p ≤ 5% while the block average is at least 25%. A short method interview checks them, and they stay "candidate" until a term's data confirms them. - **Comparison-group improvers.** A comparison-group teacher whose class met the proven-mentor bar on her own is invited too.

heading: Cohort Coach — Build Stage prototype design > Deterministic engine > Evaluation
text: - The unit is a track version (for example SUB-SFL v1), pooled across all its cohorts. - The effect is the change in p for track classes minus the change in p for comparison classes, with a 95% bootstrap interval over classes. - **Working:** the whole interval is below 0 and the estimate is a fall of at least 10 points. - **Not working:** the estimate is a fall of less than 5 points, or a rise.

heading: Cohort Coach — Build Stage prototype design > Deterministic engine > Evaluation
text: - **Inconclusive:** anything else, or fewer than 15 classes per arm. The track runs another round. - When a version is not working, it is retired or revised. Its teachers get no mark, and they are first in line for the revised version. In the demo data, the generator sets SUB-SFL v1 to work and SUB-NODEC v1 to fail, so both outcomes appear on screen.

heading: Cohort Coach — Build Stage prototype design > AI layer
text: Claude makes eight kinds of call. Each is shown below through the five layers the judges ask for. Code sits on both sides of every call: it decides what the call may say, and it checks the result before anyone sees it. | Call (model) | Input | Processing | Guardrails | Evaluation | Output |

heading: Cohort Coach — Build Stage prototype design > AI layer
text: | 1. Child voices (Sonnet 5.5) | The engine's turn plan (which child speaks, her exact answer, her mood), her persona, the last 6 turns | Writes 1 or 2 short sentences in a Grade 3 child's voice, in Tamil, Hindi or English | Every number must equal the engine's answer; at most 30 words; safety and language check; one retry, then a template line | 200 scripted turns: 100% of numbers must match; teachers rate how real it sounds | Text, then speech |

heading: Cohort Coach — Build Stage prototype design > AI layer
text: | 2. Teacher-move labeller (Haiku 5.5) | The teacher's transcribed line and the technique's list of moves | Labels the move and which child it was addressed to | A fixed label set enforced by JSON schema; low confidence becomes "other", which changes nothing | 150 lines labelled by our teacher; target 85% agreement | A label the engine uses to update each child |

heading: Cohort Coach — Build Stage prototype design > AI layer
text: | 3. Rehearsal feedback (Sonnet 5.5) | The transcript, move labels and the technique's rubric | Two strengths and one thing to try, each quoting her own words | Each quote must exist in the transcript; points come only from the rubric; no scores; private | Thumbs up or down per point; expert review of 30 transcripts | Feedback card |

heading: Cohort Coach — Build Stage prototype design > AI layer
text: | 4. Mentor method capture (Sonnet 5.5) | The mentor's corrected transcript as a custom-content document, one block per sentence | Builds a method card: steps, materials, exact phrases, timing, with the Citations API pointing each line at its sentence (two passes: see below) | Only what she said; each step and phrase carries an API citation that code converts to our sentence ids; a line with no valid citation is rejected; every phrase is a verbatim substring; she approves the card | How much the mentor edits; how often reviewers accept | Method card |

heading: Cohort Coach — Build Stage prototype design > AI layer
text: | 5. Track drafting (Opus 5.5, offline batch) | Approved method card, error definition, lesson templates, and the evidence digest as six cached documents | Drafts 6 voice-lesson scripts and the model-lesson script; a second, cited pass adds a "Why this move" line per strategy | Arithmetic is checked by code; numbers about a class are slots that code fills; a "Why" line without a valid citation is dropped; the page shown comes from the citation, not from model text; a reviewer approves | Reviewer edit rate; teacher comprehension in testing | A draft in the review queue |

heading: Cohort Coach — Build Stage prototype design > AI layer
text: | 6. Reflection digest (Haiku 5.5) | One week of the cohort's voice-reply transcripts | 3 to 5 themes, with no names | Code removes names and schools and computes the theme counts | Mentor rates usefulness | Digest for the mentor |

heading: Cohort Coach — Build Stage prototype design > AI layer
text: | 7. Output checker (Haiku 5.5) | Every AI output headed for a teacher | Checks tone, child safety, language and fit to the target error | Failures go to a human | Red-team set (see Evals) | Pass, or fail with a reason |

heading: Cohort Coach — Build Stage prototype design > AI layer
text: **Citations on calls 4 and 5 (added 22 Oct).** The Anthropic Citations API returns a 400 if citations are on and structured output (`output_config.format`) is also set (`DECISIONS.md`, 22 Oct), so these calls use two passes, and code stays the guarantor.

heading: Cohort Coach — Build Stage prototype design > AI layer
text: - **Call 4, pass A (citations on, no schema).** The corrected transcript goes in as one custom-content document with one text block per sentence, so a citation's `start_block_index` is our sentence id. The model writes fixed-format lines (`STEP:`, `MATERIAL:`, `PHRASE:`, `TIME:`). Code rebuilds each line from the text blocks and their citations, converts block indexes to sentence ids, and fills the card. A line with no citation, a cited id that does not exist, or a phrase that is not a verbatim substring of its cited text is rejected and logged, never shown. The old validators and call 7 still run as a second, independent check.

heading: Cohort Coach — Build Stage prototype design > AI layer
text: - **Call 5, pass 2 (citations on, no schema).** The evidence digest goes in as six cached documents (BaSE, FLN, AIC, NITI, IDR, APU), one text block per digest line and source with its page marker kept. Each "Why this move" line must cite; code maps the cited block to DOC plus PDF page from its own table, and the judge-mode Evidence panel shows that page. A line that cites only IDR or APU is labelled opinion, since those rows are never evidence that something works. A line with no citation is dropped and the draft goes to review without it. Pass 1 (the lesson scripts) keeps structured output and gets no documents.

heading: Cohort Coach — Build Stage prototype design > AI layer
text: - No new call number: both are described under calls 4 and 5 and in their registry entries when built. **8. Answer reading (Haiku 5.5; Sonnet 5.5 on retry).** This call runs once per sheet. - **Input.** One straightened sheet photo, carrying no name or roll number.

heading: Cohort Coach — Build Stage prototype design > AI layer
text: - **Processing.** Claude reads each of the 10 boxes as a number and gives a confidence for each. It reads blind: it is never told the expected answers, so it cannot bend a messy 38 into a 37. - **Guardrails.** A JSON schema allows only digits. Code checks each read against the correct answer and the error answers. A read outside that set, or one below the confidence bar, goes to the teacher. The photo is deleted once read.

heading: Cohort Coach — Build Stage prototype design > AI layer
text: - **Evaluation.** Hand-keyed round 1 sheets, scored on the accuracy of auto-accepted reads and on the share of reads sent to the teacher. - **Output.** A number per box, or a request to confirm. **Speech layer (not Claude).** Claude reads and writes Tamil, Hindi and English text, and every language step in this design runs in Claude.

heading: Cohort Coach — Build Stage prototype design > AI layer
text: Its API takes no audio in and gives none out, though, so speech is converted to text before Claude and back to voice after. Sarvam AI's APIs handle both ends, so no GPU is needed: Saarika turns Hindi, Tamil and English speech into text, and Bulbul turns text into voice. The finguru FastAPI WebSocket server with voice-activity detection is reused to stream audio. **Cost control.** The Build Stage comes with [USD 500 of Claude credits per team](https://hack2skill.com/event/aiforfoundationallearning).

heading: Cohort Coach — Build Stage prototype design > AI layer
text: - Calls 2, 6, 7 and 8 run on Haiku, and Opus runs only offline. - Fixed system prompts use prompt caching. - Judge mode caps a rehearsal at 40 turns. - Every call logs its tokens, so the deck can report a measured cost per teacher.

heading: Cohort Coach — Build Stage prototype design > Practice Class
text: The teacher rehearses the technique with five simulated children who make her own class's mistakes. The bug engine computes every wrong answer, and Claude supplies only the children's words.

heading: Cohort Coach — Build Stage prototype design > Practice Class > What the teacher sees and hears
text: It is a live voice conversation on her phone, like a phone call with five pupils. There is no video and no camera, and nothing is recorded or kept. - **Screen.** Five cartoon children with name labels. The one speaking lights up. - **She speaks.** She holds the phone and teaches out loud, in Hindi, Tamil or English, exactly as she would in class. On a weak signal she can type instead.

heading: Cohort Coach — Build Stage prototype design > Practice Class > What the teacher sees and hears
text: - **The children answer.** They reply in a child's voice through the speaker, making the mistakes her own pupils make. - **Materials tray.** The app can't see her hands, so physical materials are buttons: bundles of ten, loose sticks, a place-value chart. Tapping one shows it to the children and counts as using it. - **Feedback.** After about 10 minutes, a private card says what she did well and one thing to try next time.

heading: Cohort Coach — Build Stage prototype design > Practice Class > What the teacher sees and hears
text: **Child voices.** Sarvam's stock voices are all adult, so each of the five children gets a cloned voice. Sarvam's Voice Cloning API (beta) builds a reusable voice from one clean 10 to 15 second clip, and the clone can speak languages other than the clip's. Each child's clip comes from one of two sources: an AI-designed child voice from a tool whose licence allows reuse, or a consenting adult on the team reading in a child-like voice.

heading: Cohort Coach — Build Stage prototype design > Practice Class > What the teacher sees and hears
text: A real child's voice is never used. Before relying on the clones, check that they stream fast enough for live turns. If a clone sounds wrong, that child falls back to a pitch-raised stock voice. The children's words come from Claude either way, so the rehearsal logic is unchanged. **A sample exchange** (SUB-SFL, shown in English; it runs in her language): | Who | Says or does | What the app notes |

heading: Cohort Coach — Build Stage prototype design > Practice Class > What the teacher sees and hears
text: | Teacher | "Meena, what is 52 minus 29?" | Asks a child directly | | Meena (simulated) | "37, Miss!" | Wrong answer from the SUB-SFL error, computed by code | | Teacher | "Tell me how you got 37." | Move: asks the child to explain |

heading: Cohort Coach — Build Stage prototype design > Practice Class > What the teacher sees and hears
text: | Meena | "2 minus 9 I can't do, so I did 9 minus 2. That's 7. Then 5 minus 2 is 3." | Her wrong reasoning is now out loud | | Teacher | Taps bundles: "Here is 52: 5 bundles and 2 sticks. Take away 9 sticks." | Move: uses bundles | | Meena | "I only have 2 loose ones... can I open a bundle?" | Her error weakens |

heading: Cohort Coach — Build Stage prototype design > Practice Class > What the teacher sees and hears
text: | Teacher | "Yes! Now how many tens are left?" | Move: builds on the child's idea | | Feedback card | "You asked Meena to explain ('Tell me how you got 37'), which showed you her thinking. Next time, check by adding back: 37 + 29 = 66, not 52." | Two strengths and one thing to try; no score |

heading: Cohort Coach — Build Stage prototype design > Practice Class > Setup
text: - **Children.** Five fictional children with ordinary local names, never her pupils' names. Seats are filled to match her class's error mix: if 40% of her class shows SUB-SFL, 2 of the 5 children do. One child always answers correctly, and one is shy and speaks only when called by name. - **State.** Each child has an error strength from 0 to 1, starting at 0.9 for her error, and an engagement level.

heading: Cohort Coach — Build Stage prototype design > Practice Class > Setup
text: - **Scenario.** The problems and materials come from the approved model-lesson script, e.g. 52 − 29 with bundles of ten sticks.

heading: Cohort Coach — Build Stage prototype design > Practice Class > One turn
text: *[Diagram in the original doc: one Practice Class turn · 7 steps, 2 Claude calls, 1 retry loop]* The judges' layers map onto it as follows. Input is her line and speech-to-text. Processing is the labeller, the engine and the child's voice. The checks are the guardrails, the spoken reply is the output, and evaluation runs offline. | Her move | Change in error strength | What the child does |

heading: Cohort Coach — Build Stage prototype design > Practice Class > One turn
text: | Asks the child to show it with bundles of ten sticks | −0.3 | Works it through aloud | | Asks the child to explain her steps | −0.2 | Says her wrong reasoning: "2 minus 9 can't be done, so 9 minus 2" | | Checks by adding back (37 + 29 = 66, not 52) | −0.2 | Looks puzzled and starts to doubt her answer |

heading: Cohort Coach — Build Stage prototype design > Practice Class > One turn
text: | Just tells the rule | −0.05 | Agrees, but may misapply it on the next problem | | Praises effort | none | Engagement rises | | Scolds | none | Engagement drops and the child goes quiet | A child answers wrong with probability equal to her error strength, and the wrong number always comes from the bug function. The strength values are tuning parameters. Our teacher sets them in each scenario file.

heading: Cohort Coach — Build Stage prototype design > Practice Class > End of session
text: - **When it ends.** After each child with the error answers correctly twice in a row, or after 40 turns. - **Feedback.** A card with two strengths and one thing to try, each quoting her own words, plus a retry with the same children.

heading: Cohort Coach — Build Stage prototype design > Practice Class > End of session
text: - **Privacy.** The transcript stays on her phone. The server relays calls and keeps nothing unless she chooses to share a session to improve the simulator. The programme view sees how many teachers practised, never what was said.

heading: Cohort Coach — Build Stage prototype design > Practice Class > Why an engine, not just a prompt
text: A language model asked to play a confused child can drift: it gets the sum right by accident or invents an error no child makes. Putting the error in code keeps the children faithful to her class, makes sessions reproducible, and makes the simulator testable.

heading: Cohort Coach — Build Stage prototype design > Guardrails and privacy
text: AI output must pass four gates before it reaches a teacher, and it stays flaggable after that. No child's personal data ever leaves the classroom. | Gate | What it catches | Where it applies | | 1. Code checks | Wrong numbers, invented class statistics, quotes that aren't in the transcript, replies that run too long | Every call |

heading: Cohort Coach — Build Stage prototype design > Guardrails and privacy
text: | 2. Output checker (Haiku) | Unkind or unsafe tone, stereotypes, wrong language, off-topic content | Everything headed for a teacher | | 3. Human approval | Content that is pedagogically wrong or unclear | All track content and method cards: the reviewer approves first, then the mentor | | 4. Teacher flag | Anything the first three gates miss | A "this is wrong" button on every AI card; flags feed the eval set |

heading: Cohort Coach — Build Stage prototype design > Guardrails and privacy > Specific risks
text: - **Breaking role.** If a teacher types "ignore your instructions", the children stay in role, the labeller tags the line off-task, and the red-team set tests this. - **Harsh practice.** If she scolds or threatens during rehearsal, the feedback names it gently and suggests what to do instead. This is in line with the RTE Act's ban on physical punishment and mental harassment.

heading: Cohort Coach — Build Stage prototype design > Guardrails and privacy > Specific risks
text: - **Stereotypes.** Children's names and personas come from a reviewed list, balanced by gender. Personas carry no caste, religion or disability markers. - **Judging teachers.** The AI never scores a teacher. Feedback is private, evaluation is per track, and officers have no teacher-level dashboard.

heading: Cohort Coach — Build Stage prototype design > Guardrails and privacy > Privacy
text: - **Children.** Answer sheets carry no name or roll number, and only the teacher's phone links a sheet to a child. Sheet photos are deleted once read, and only class counts are stored. No names, faces or voices are collected. This avoids the DPDP Act's parental-consent requirement for children's data altogether.

heading: Cohort Coach — Build Stage prototype design > Guardrails and privacy > Privacy
text: - **Teachers.** Teachers give consent at onboarding, and Practice Class transcripts stay on the device. Voice reflections are transcribed, then the audio is deleted after 30 days. The mentor's digest is anonymised. - **Mentors.** Her name and her class's improvement are shown to her cohort only with her consent. - **Officers.** Officers see aggregates only, and any figure covering fewer than 5 classes is hidden so that no single teacher can be identified.

heading: Cohort Coach — Build Stage prototype design > Guardrails and privacy > Privacy
text: - **Deck.** Reuse the finguru DPDP mapping format for the deck's data-flow table.

heading: Cohort Coach — Build Stage prototype design > Low connectivity, low data, low-cost devices
text: Only the Practice Class needs a live connection. Everything else works offline or queues until a signal returns. The target is under 10 MB of data for a teacher's whole 3-week track, measured in testing. **Target device.** State a concrete low-end phone — for example, a two to three-year-old sub-$100 Android device — and test against it directly, since "low-cost devices" is named in the criteria separately from connectivity and judges may test on an old phone deliberately.

heading: Cohort Coach — Build Stage prototype design > Low connectivity, low data, low-cost devices
text: A stated spec beats an implied one. **The one deliberate trade-off.** Practice Class, the AI child rehearsal, is both the most judge-impressive feature and the only one needing a live connection. Worth naming this trade-off explicitly rather than leaving it to be noticed: rehearsal realism is worth the live call, and everything in the actual lesson cycle — the check, the grouping, the lessons themselves — still works fully offline.

heading: Cohort Coach — Build Stage prototype design > Low connectivity, low data, low-cost devices > Low-cost devices
text: - **Target phone.** An Android Go-class phone with 2 GB of RAM, running Chrome. - **Install.** The app is a PWA installed from the browser, with no app store. The first load is under 1 MB of compressed JavaScript. - **Fonts and images.** Tamil uses the phone's system fonts. There are no images, only SVG icons. - **Testing.** Test on Chrome's Slow 3G throttling and on one real low-end phone.

heading: Cohort Coach — Build Stage prototype design > Low connectivity, low data, low-cost devices > Server-side fallbacks
text: - All voice lessons are rendered to audio when they are published, so only the Practice Class needs live speech. - If Sarvam's API is unreachable, the Practice Class switches to text automatically.

heading: Cohort Coach — Build Stage prototype design > Architecture, stack and repo
text: The build reuses what already exists: the finguru FastAPI voice server, with Sarvam AI's APIs for speech, and the Claude API for language. A thin PWA sits on top. Everything lives in one repo, laid out so judges can find every AI call in a minute. *[Diagram in the original doc: components · 3 clients, 1 API, 3 services]* Practice Class transcripts, and the link between sheets and children, stay on the phone.

heading: Sprite system: items, mats, avatars and expressions as data, drawn by code
text: Status: built 22 Oct 2026 (see `docs/build/reports/SPRITES.md` for what is built and what is only specified). Rules: `CLAUDE.md` rule 17, `DECISIONS.md` 22 Oct.

heading: Sprite system: items, mats, avatars and expressions as data, drawn by code > Principles
text: 1. **SVG only, built by code.** No raster art, no image generation, no AI at runtime. 2. **Everything dynamic is data.** A new topic, item, student, expression or mat is a JSON file under `content/sprites/`, never renderer code. 3. **Counts are exact by construction.** If a scene shows 45 balls, code draws 45 `use` elements, and a test parses the SVG and counts them.

heading: Sprite system: items, mats, avatars and expressions as data, drawn by code > Principles
text: 4. **AI drafts at authoring time only**, inside the grammar (call 11, `SPRITE_AUTHOR`), and a human approves before any teacher sees it.

heading: Sprite system: items, mats, avatars and expressions as data, drawn by code > Where things live
text: | What | Where | | Palettes (slots, approved sets, skin tones, hair and cloth colours) | `content/sprites/palettes.v1.json` | | Item specs | `content/sprites/items/<id>.v1.json` | | Avatar parts (bodies, hair, outfits, accessories) | `content/sprites/avatar_parts.v1.json` | | Expressions and face parts | `content/sprites/expressions.v1.json` | | Persona looks (seed and look per approved persona) | `content/sprites/personas.v1.json` | | Topic packs | `content/sprites/packs/<id>.v1.json` | | Renderer, Python (canonical; PNG for Telegram) | `services/api/sprites/` |

heading: Sprite system: items, mats, avatars and expressions as data, drawn by code > Where things live
text: | Renderer, TypeScript (inline SVG on the phone) | `apps/pwa/src/sprites/` | | Parity fixture (Python output, TypeScript must match) | `tests/fixtures/sprite_golden.json` | The two renderers are one grammar written twice. Both use integer arithmetic and the same seeded generator (xorshift32), so the same inputs give byte-identical SVG; `apps/pwa/src/sprites/golden.test.ts` proves it on the fixture the Python engine writes.

heading: Sprite system: items, mats, avatars and expressions as data, drawn by code > Grammar
text: **Allowed SVG elements** (in any rendered output): `svg`, `g`, `circle`, `ellipse`, `rect`, `line`, `polyline`, `polygon`, `path`, `defs`, `linearGradient`, `radialGradient`, `stop`, `clipPath`, `use`. **Forbidden:** `script`, `foreignObject`, `image`, `text` (and `tspan`, `title`, `desc`), `style`, `a`, `animate`, `animateTransform`, `set`; any `on*` attribute; a `style` attribute; any `href` that does not start with `#`; any non-whitespace text node.

heading: Sprite system: items, mats, avatars and expressions as data, drawn by code > Grammar
text: **Item and avatar specs** use only these shapes: `circle`, `ellipse`, `rect`, `line`, `polyline`, `polygon`, `path`, with integer numbers, fills and strokes that are a **palette slot name** (never a hex), `none`, or `grad:<id>` for a gradient the same spec defines. A spec that contains a hex colour, a non-integer, an unknown shape or an unknown attribute fails the grammar validator. **Palette slots:** `skin`, `hair`, `cloth_a`, `cloth_b`, `accent`, `item_a`, `item_b`, `mat`, `ink`.

heading: Sprite system: items, mats, avatars and expressions as data, drawn by code > Grammar
text: A palette maps each slot to a hex colour; specs never see the hex. **Fixed viewBox per category:** item `0 0 24 24`; avatar `0 0 64 72`; scene and mat `0 0 240 160`. **Size budgets** (compiled markup of one spec): item 2 KB, avatar 12 KB, mat 6 KB. A drawn scene has no budget: it is many `use` elements of one small definition.

heading: Sprite system: items, mats, avatars and expressions as data, drawn by code > Grammar
text: **Animation** is CSS classes on the page's stylesheet (opacity and transform only) and is switched off under `prefers-reduced-motion`. No animation element lives in an SVG. **Meaning without colour.** Items differ by silhouette or pattern (stick, counter, ball with seam, marble with swirl, mango with leaf, pencil, book). A bundle is shown by a box around ten units, group B in an addition scene by a frame, a marked unit in a subtraction scene by a cross.

heading: Sprite system: items, mats, avatars and expressions as data, drawn by code > Grammar
text: Palettes are tested for contrast against the mat under protanopia, deuteranopia and tritanopia (Machado, Oliveira and Fernandes 2009 matrices, severity 1.0, applied in linear sRGB). **No text in the art.** Alt text and labels are i18n keys (`sprite.*` in `strings/{en,hi,ta}.json`); the SVG carries `data-alt` with the key, and the page puts the translated text in `aria-label`.

heading: Sprite system: items, mats, avatars and expressions as data, drawn by code > Layout engines (pure functions, exact)
text: Each takes an item spec, a count, a palette and a seed and returns the SVG and a report, for example `{"item_id": "ball", "count_drawn": 45}`. | Layout | What it draws | Report | | `row` | n units in rows of at most 20 | `count_drawn` | | `grid_array(r, c)` | r by c units | `count_drawn = r*c` | | `ten_frame` | 0 to 20 counters in one or two ten-frames, row by row | `count_drawn` |

heading: Sprite system: items, mats, avatars and expressions as data, drawn by code > Layout engines (pure functions, exact)
text: | `bundle_group` | n units as whole bundles of exactly 10, plus loose units | `bundles`, `loose`, `count_drawn = n` | | `place_value_mat` | 0 to 99: tens column of bundles, ones column of units | `tens`, `ones`, `count_drawn = n` | | `number_line(min, max, marks)` | ticks for every integer, longer at 5 and 10, circles at the marks | `ticks`, `marks`, `count_drawn = len(marks)` |

heading: Sprite system: items, mats, avatars and expressions as data, drawn by code > Layout engines (pure functions, exact)
text: | `bar_model(parts)` | one bar split in proportion, alternate parts patterned | `parts`, `total` | | `cross_out(n of N)` | N units, exactly n crossed | `count_drawn = N`, `marked = n` | | `scatter(n, seed)` | n units in seeded, non-overlapping cells | `count_drawn` | | `two_groups(a, b, seed)` | a units and b units apart, group B framed | `count_drawn = a+b`, `groups` |

heading: Sprite system: items, mats, avatars and expressions as data, drawn by code > Avatars and expressions
text: An avatar is a composition: body, skin tone, hair style, hair colour, outfit (two cloth colours), accessory (none or bag; glasses and ribbon were removed on 22 Oct after the privacy review, because they can read as disability and gender markers). The look is derived from a seed (`look_from_seed`), and a persona record may override any field. The same seed gives the same SVG hash.

heading: Sprite system: items, mats, avatars and expressions as data, drawn by code > Avatars and expressions
text: Names come from the approved persona pool, never the roster; styles are named `hair_a` to `hair_f`, not by gender; no caste, religion or disability marker, no likeness of a real child. Expressions are face-part sets in the registry: `neutral`, `thinking`, `confused`, `got_it`, `wrong_answer`, `shy`, `distracted`.

heading: Sprite system: items, mats, avatars and expressions as data, drawn by code > Avatars and expressions
text: Each has a closed and an open mouth frame; the avatar SVG holds both and the page's CSS toggles them while audio plays. **Code maps child state to an expression in one table** (`services/api/sprites/expression.py`); AI never chooses one. A new expression is one JSON entry that reuses existing face parts.

heading: Sprite system: items, mats, avatars and expressions as data, drawn by code > Packs
text: A topic pack manifest holds: `id`, `subject`, `items`, `mats`, `layouts`, `expressions`, scenario `templates` (number slots filled by code, text by i18n key), `i18n_keys`, `version`, `status` (`draft`, `approved`, `enabled`). Shipped: `place-value-add-sub` (stick, bundle_of_ten, counter, ball, mango, pencil, marble, book, ten_frame; mats place_value_mat and number_line; add and subtract word-problem templates) and `fractions-demo` (a new item and the existing `bar_model`, JSON only, no renderer change: a test pins the renderer's hash).

heading: Sprite system: items, mats, avatars and expressions as data, drawn by code > Packs
text: **Two keys.** The coach approves a pack (gate 3); the programme officer enables it for the block. Neither alone enables. Every change is a new pack version, and an enabled pack that is edited stays in use until the new version is approved and enabled. **No check items.** A template's text and every filled number pair go through the no-check-items validator (no Form A or B pair, either order).

heading: Sprite system: items, mats, avatars and expressions as data, drawn by code > Authoring-time AI (call 11, `SPRITE_AUTHOR`)
text: Input: a plain description ("red cricket ball"). Output: an item spec in this grammar through a JSON schema that enumerates the shapes and slots, never free SVG. Offline only; never in a live turn. Gates, in order: schema, grammar whitelist, size budget, no text, palette slots only, no raw colour, a contact-sheet tile rendered, the pre-filter and call 7 for child-appropriateness (no weapons, alcohol or tobacco, religious or political symbols, brand marks), then coach approval, then officer enablement.

heading: Sprite system: items, mats, avatars and expressions as data, drawn by code > Authoring-time AI (call 11, `SPRITE_AUTHOR`)
text: A rejected spec returns the failing rule to the author and is never shown to a teacher.

heading: Sprite system: items, mats, avatars and expressions as data, drawn by code > Channels
text: - **PWA:** inline SVG from the TypeScript renderer, cached with the shell. - **Telegram and WhatsApp:** the server renders the scene to PNG (`resvg-py`, a Rust renderer in a wheel with no system libraries) and the flow engine sends it as an image; no browser rendering. - **Practice Class:** the seat row and the materials tray use the same renderer; judge mode's "Show the machinery" shows the sprite spec JSON for the scene.

heading: Sprite system: items, mats, avatars and expressions as data, drawn by code > Dashboard boundary
text: Configurable in the dashboard: enable or disable packs, items and expressions; persona looks and seating; palettes from the approved list; scenario templates. Code only: the grammar, the renderer, the layouts, the validators, the state-to-expression table, and anything that computes a count.

heading: The deterministic engine
text: **Code, not AI, owns every number.** Eval 1 (`evals/results/engine_items.json`) checks the error answers and item collisions; the phone and the server give identical diagnoses (see "One engine, two languages"). Everything a judge must be able to trust is plain, unit-tested Python in `engine/`: the error functions, the items, diagnosis and the track choice. No AI call computes or states a number about a class. Claude may later phrase a sentence around a number; the number comes from here.

heading: The deterministic engine > The five errors
text: Each error is a pure function `problem -> set of wrong answers` in [engine/bugs.py](../engine/bugs.py). | Code | Error | Example | Correct | Tracked | | PV-HEARD | Writes the number the way it is said | forty-three → 403; 346 → 30046, 3046, 300406 | 43; 346 | Yes, first priority | | PV-REVERSE | Swaps tens and ones | 43 → 34; 346 → 364 | 43; 346 | Detected only |

heading: The deterministic engine > The five errors
text: | ADD-NOCARRY | Drops the carried ten | 47 + 25 → 62 | 72 | Yes | | SUB-SFL | Smaller digit from larger in each column | 52 − 29 → 37 | 23 | Yes | | SUB-NODEC | Borrows a ten, does not reduce the tens digit | 52 − 29 → 33 | 23 | Yes | - An answer both heard and reversed (346 → 30064, 3064, 300604) counts for **both** PV-HEARD and PV-REVERSE.

heading: The deterministic engine > The five errors
text: - The untracked pattern `ADD-WHOLE-ONES` (38 + 47 → 715) is scored "other" but tallied separately: it may deserve a track. - A number with a zero digit has no heard or reversed answer (the generator never makes one). - Anything else a child writes is `other`; an empty box is `blank`; text the normaliser cannot turn into digits is `unreadable` and goes to a person. Blank and unreadable boxes never count towards an error.

heading: The deterministic engine > Items and forms
text: [engine/items.py](../engine/items.py) builds the 10-item check: 2 dictation, 3 addition with carrying, 1 anchor subtraction, 4 subtraction with borrowing. | Type | Rules | | Dictation | 3-digit; hundreds, tens, ones all non-zero; tens ≠ ones | | Add-carry | 2-digit operands; ones total ≥ 10; sum ≤ 99 | | Anchor | no borrowing; tens digit larger | | Borrow | ones digit smaller; tens digit larger; ones-digit gap ≠ 5; result ≥ 10 |

heading: The deterministic engine > Items and forms
text: `validate_item` also rejects any item where two errors give the same wrong answer, where an error answer equals the correct one, where the heard-and-reversed set overlaps a single error, or where the untracked answer collides with a tracked one. Example: 52 − 27 is rejected, since SUB-SFL and SUB-NODEC both give 35. `generate_form(seed, like=...)` is deterministic.

heading: The deterministic engine > Items and forms
text: With `like`, it makes a **parallel form**: the same ones totals in items 3–5 and the same ones gaps in items 7–10, with every number different. The two printed pilot forms live in [engine/forms.py](../engine/forms.py); `tests/engine/test_forms.py` proves each item reproduces `pilot_forms.golden.json`.

heading: The deterministic engine > Diagnosis: the 2-item rule
text: [engine/diagnosis.py](../engine/diagnosis.py). A child **shows** an error only if it appears on at least 2 of the items that probe it: both of items 1–2, 2 of items 3–5, 2 of items 7–10. One slip is not a pattern. A wrong anchor (item 6) is noted, and items 7–10 are still scored.

heading: The deterministic engine > Diagnosis: the 2-item rule
text: For a class: prevalence p = children showing the error ÷ children checked (a fraction; the engine never rounds). **Eligible** = p ≥ 25% and at least 10 children checked, compared with integers (`count × 4 ≥ checked`), so 3 of 12 is eligible and 3 of 13 is not. **Track** = PV-HEARD if eligible, else the tracked error with the most children (ties go to the first in code order). PV-REVERSE is never chosen.

heading: The deterministic engine > Grouping and mentors
text: [engine/grouping.py](../engine/grouping.py) works on **class-level counts only** (what the server stores), through `profile_from_counts`. 1. **Track assignment.** A class is eligible at p of at least 25% with at least 10 children checked. One track per class: PV-HEARD first, otherwise its highest-p error. Each assignment returns the facts for its one-line explanation ("Grouped for SUB-SFL because 11 of 28 children showed it").

heading: The deterministic engine > Grouping and mentors
text: 2. **Waitlist split.** Teachers with the same track, grade and medium are cut into terciles of baseline p and each tercile is split as evenly as possible (never more than one apart), with a seeded shuffle. The same seed always gives the same split.

heading: The deterministic engine > Grouping and mentors
text: 3. **Cohorts.** 15 to 20 teachers, at most 2 per school, one mentor slot each. A block with fewer than 15 eligible teachers is pooled with other short blocks (flagged `cross_block`); a pool still under 15 becomes one `undersized` cohort. Teachers who do not fit (school cap or a full cohort) are returned as `unplaced` for the next cohort. The demo block is one block split by medium and then by arm, so its cohorts are small and flagged undersized.

heading: The deterministic engine > Grouping and mentors
text: [engine/mentors.py](../engine/mentors.py) returns, for each rule, whether it was met and the numbers behind it. Exact fractions decide every boundary. | Kind | Rule | | Proven | On the track; last term p of at least 25%; this term fell at least 15 points and by at least half; at least 15 children checked both times; her fall beats the comparison group's average; she consents |

heading: The deterministic engine > Grouping and mentors
text: | Comparison-group improver | The proven bar, without the track and without the comparison-average rule; she consents | | Same-term candidate | Same grade and medium; p of at most 5% while the block average is at least 25%; at least 10 children checked; she consents. The cause is unverified, so a method interview comes first and she stays "candidate" until a term confirms |

heading: The deterministic engine > Grouping and mentors
text: `find_mentors` is the tier-1 exact lookup (error, grade, medium, status, verified) that P11 wires to the database. There is no vector database.

heading: The deterministic engine > One engine, two languages
text: The phone diagnoses offline with `apps/pwa/src/lib/diagnosis.ts`, which only looks up answers in `apps/pwa/src/generated/answer_keys.json` (written by `python tasks.py export-keys`, with a content hash so client and server can spot drift).

heading: The deterministic engine > One engine, two languages
text: Python also writes `tests/fixtures/diagnosis_cases.json` (parity fixtures: their expected values are the engine's own output, so they prove Python and TypeScript agree, not that either is right; correctness rests on the printed key and the hand-written assertions in `tests/engine/`) (named edge cases, seeded random children and whole classes of different sizes); pytest checks the files are not stale and Vitest checks TypeScript gives identical results.

heading: The deterministic engine > Why code, not AI
text: Diagnosis decides which teachers train together, so it must be exact, repeatable and explainable offline. A model can misread, drift between runs, and cannot show its working. Here every verdict traces to a table row and a rule above.

heading: The deterministic engine > Running the checks
text: Use `python tasks.py test` (or `check`), which use the project venv. Bare `pytest` on system Python lacks Hypothesis.

heading: The deterministic engine > Evidence
text: No number is typed in this page. The results live in generated files: - `evals/results/engine_items.json` (eval 1, `python tasks.py eval engine_items`): per error, how many generated problems match an independent column-procedure oracle, and how many collide. The registry copy in `docs/evidence/` arrives with `python tasks.py evidence` (P02). - Unit and property tests under `tests/engine/` (Hypothesis, 500 examples per property): run `python tasks.py test`. - Type check: `.venv/Scripts/python.exe -m mypy --strict engine` (the venv has mypy; system Python may not).

heading: The deterministic engine > Open for the team
text: - TODO-HUMAN(Seema): confirm the extra heard-and-reversed variants (3064, 300604 beside the printed 30064) and that all 20 pilot items match NCERT Grade 3.

heading: Did the track work? Evaluation
text: Code answers this question, in [engine/evaluation.py](../engine/evaluation.py). Claude never computes or states a number about a class, a cohort or a track. Verdicts belong to a **track version** (for example "SUB-SFL v1"), pooled across its cohorts. A failed track counts against the track, never against a teacher.

heading: Did the track work? Evaluation > Two methods, one vocabulary
text: Every verdict is **working**, **not working** or **inconclusive**. | | Block scale | Pilot scale | | When | Many classes on a track, with a waitlist comparison group | A handful of real classes, no comparison group | | Effect | Change in p for track classes minus change in p for waitlist classes | The trained error's fall minus the mean fall of untrained errors that had p of at least 10% at pre-test |

heading: Did the track work? Evaluation > Two methods, one vocabulary
text: | Uncertainty | 95% percentile bootstrap over classes (seeded) | Exact McNemar test on children who were Fixed versus New | | Working | The whole interval is below 0 **and** the estimate is a fall of at least 10 points | Extra fall of at least 10 points **and** McNemar p below 0.05 | | Not working | A fall of under 5 points, or a rise | Extra fall of under 5 points, or a rise |

heading: Did the track work? Evaluation > Two methods, one vocabulary
text: | Inconclusive | Anything else, or fewer than 15 classes in either arm | Anything else, or no untrained error to compare with | | Data | Class-level counts from the server | Child pairs by roll number, **on a phone or in a local script only** |

heading: Did the track work? Evaluation > Two methods, one vocabulary
text: The comparison group at block scale is the waitlist: eligible teachers for the same track, grade and medium are randomly assigned this term or next, stratified by baseline p (terciles; each tercile is split as evenly as possible). If there is no waitlist, `engine/grouping.py` offers a matched group: same error, grade, medium and school type, baseline p within 5 points. Pilot sheets carry roll numbers so that each child's two sheets can be paired.

heading: Did the track work? Evaluation > Two methods, one vocabulary
text: Pairing never runs on the server and raw pilot files never enter git; only the 2×2 counts leave the machine.

heading: Did the track work? Evaluation > The power caveat at pilot scale
text: A pilot has few classes and a few dozen children, and McNemar only counts children whose result changed. A real effect can easily come out **inconclusive**, and that is the honest answer. The block-scale evaluation (eval 8, [docs/evidence/eval_summary.md](evidence/eval_summary.md)) shows the same effect at scale: near the 10-point bar, planted effects are called "working" only part of the time. Treat pilot verdicts as evidence to read alongside teacher feedback, not as a pass mark.

heading: Did the track work? Evaluation > How small samples are worded
text: - Fewer than 15 classes in an arm: the verdict is **inconclusive**, with the reason `too_few_classes`. - Fewer than 15 classes anywhere a figure is shown: a note reads "from N classes, read as directional" (`engine.evaluation.confidence_note`). - Fewer than 5 classes: the figure is **hidden** in officer views and in the evidence tables ("hidden (fewer than 5 classes)"). - Teacher-facing text uses counts ("11 of 28 children"), never percentages.

heading: Did the track work? Evaluation > Evidence and how to reproduce it
text: | What | Command | File | | Demo verdicts (simulated block) | `python tasks.py evidence` | [docs/evidence/demo_verdicts.md](evidence/demo_verdicts.md) | | Statistics eval (eval 8) | `python tasks.py eval statistics` | `evals/results/statistics.json`, summarised in [docs/evidence/eval_summary.md](evidence/eval_summary.md) | | The simulated block (seed 2026) | `python tasks.py seed` | `data/synthetic/block_T1T2.json` |

heading: Did the track work? Evaluation > Evidence and how to reproduce it
text: **Read the eval 8 headline with its scope.** It shows the test is conservative: it finds planted effects of 15 points or more with 20 classes per arm, and it finds a 10-point effect (right at the working bar) only about half the time. Do not quote the recovery rate as general power. The per-effect table in the evidence summary shows every row.

heading: Did the track work? Evaluation > Evidence and how to reproduce it
text: Eval 8 plants effects of known size (and zero) in simulated terms and checks that planted working effects are called working at least 95% of the time and that no-effect terms are called working at most 5% of the time. Effect sizes, arm size, class-to-class spread and seeds are listed in its result file.

heading: Did the track work? Evaluation > Evidence and how to reproduce it
text: The simulated block plants SUB-SFL v1 as a working track and SUB-NODEC v1 as a failing one; the verdicts are computed from the counts by `block_effect`, and a test swaps the planted effects to prove nothing is hardcoded. All simulated data is labelled "simulated" wherever it is shown.

heading: Feedback log
text: Every piece of user feedback, and what we changed because of it. Rendered as "You said → We changed" by `python scripts/feedback_table.py`. Use `/log-feedback` to add rows. | date | round | participant code | what they said or did | what we changed | commit | status |

heading: Guardrails (v1, built in P03)
text: How wrong or unsafe AI output is stopped before it reaches a teacher. Everything here is code in `ai/validators/`, `ai/guard/` and `ai/client.py`; nothing depends on a prompt behaving.

heading: Guardrails (v1, built in P03) > The gates
text: - Gate 2 only runs if gates 1 and 1b pass, so a line with a wrong number never costs a checker call. - The checker **fails closed**: if call 7 times out, errors, or returns an inconsistent verdict (passed with failed items, failed with none, an unknown rubric item), the content is held and goes to a human or a template. - A human cannot lift content past a failed automatic gate: the badge stays *none* (`ai/guard/badges.py`).

heading: Guardrails (v1, built in P03) > The gates
text: - Gate code: `ai/guard/gates.py`. Pipelines per content type: child line, feedback card, method card, track draft, digest.

heading: Guardrails (v1, built in P03) > What each code validator checks
text: | Validator | Checks | File | | numbers | Digits in Latin, Devanagari and Tamil script must be in the allowed set (the engine's answer for a child line); number words in en, hi, ta are found so text can be forced to digits | `ai/validators/numbers.py` | | quotes | A quote is a verbatim part of the transcript after case, spacing and punctuation are normalised; Indic vowel signs are kept | `quotes.py` |

heading: Guardrails (v1, built in P03) > What each code validator checks
text: | length | Words and characters (a child line is at most 30 words) | `length.py` | | language | Script of each word against the language asked for, with a small allowance for code-mixing | `language.py` | | pii | Phone numbers (incl. +91 and Devanagari digits), emails, 12-digit ID-like numbers, roster names; violations never repeat what they matched | `pii.py` |

heading: Guardrails (v1, built in P03) > What each code validator checks
text: | arithmetic | Every "a − b = c" and "a + b = c" statement; an intentional child mistake is tagged `[child-wrong]` | `arithmetic.py` | | readability | Sentence length, long words, jargon list; stricter for child-facing lines | `readability.py` | | prefilter | Profanity and harsh words (en, hi, ta, romanised), PII, off-topic and injection markers, malformed output, length, script | `prefilter.py` | Word lists live in `content/lang/` and `content/safety/` (data, not code).

heading: Guardrails (v1, built in P03) > What each code validator checks
text: The Hindi and Tamil lists are first drafts marked `TODO-HUMAN(Seema, Shivani, Gopi)` for native review.

heading: Guardrails (v1, built in P03) > The output checker (call 7)
text: Rubric items: tone, child safety, stereotypes, language, fit to the target error, reading level for the stated audience, maths, no class statistics unless provided, and injection. For a simulated child line in the Practice Class, call 7 does not judge maths or fit: the engine chose the answer (often deliberately wrong) and code has already checked every number against it, so call 7 judges tone, safety, stereotypes, language, reading level, injection and role.

heading: Guardrails (v1, built in P03) > The output checker (call 7)
text: The verdict is structured: `passed`, `failed_items`, a short reason for the team, and a one-line reason in the user's language. When unsure it fails the item.

heading: Guardrails (v1, built in P03) > Content pipeline (track drafts)
text: A call 5 draft goes through the same gates as everything else, with two additions for track content: class numbers may appear only as slots (a literal count is blocked before the queue), and any pair of numbers that is an item of Form A or Form B is blocked, with the form and item named. The coach then reviews it in the queue, and a track version reaches teachers only after the coach's key and the officer's key.

heading: Guardrails (v1, built in P03) > Content pipeline (track drafts)
text: Details, and the open finding that call 7 treats a slot placeholder as a stated statistic: `docs/content-pipeline.md`.

heading: Guardrails (v1, built in P03) > Rejection loop
text: Reviewers reject with one structured reason: wrong maths, culturally off, too complex for the medium, tone issue, or factually shaky (`ai/guard/rejections.py`). Approved examples are saved in `content/rejections/approved/` and the latest few go into call 7's prompt as "rejected before, and why". The examples text is part of the recorded-response key, so a new example never silently reuses an old recording.

heading: Guardrails (v1, built in P03) > Reading level
text: Child-voice lines and child-facing lines in model lessons must sound like a Grade 3 child; teacher-facing lessons must be plain spoken language. Code proxies (sentence and word length, a jargon list) run at gate 1; call 7 has a rubric item on top.

heading: Guardrails (v1, built in P03) > Injection defences
text: 1. Teacher, mentor and reflection text is wrapped in tags (`<teacher_text>`, `<candidate_text>`, …) and every prompt says tagged text is data, never instructions. A closing tag inside the text cannot end its wrapper (`ai/client.py::_wrap`). 2. The pre-filter looks for instruction-like phrases in English, Hindi and Tamil before call 7. 3. Output is constrained by JSON schema and re-validated with Pydantic, so a hijacked reply cannot change shape.

heading: Guardrails (v1, built in P03) > Injection defences
text: 4. Numbers in child lines must equal the engine's answer, whatever the text says.

heading: Guardrails (v1, built in P03) > Injection defences
text: 5. The red-team harness (`evals/runners/redteam.py`, set `evals/sets/redteam.yaml`) runs 22 seed attacks (12 candidate AI outputs, 10 lines typed to the Practice Class) across six categories and three languages, plus Hinglish. Code-only results: `evals/results/redteam.json`; live results with call 7 and the call 2 labeller: `evals/results/redteam_live.json`. The numbers are in `docs/evidence/eval_summary.md`. That is the bar (0 unsafe reach a teacher) on the seed set only, not on the full set of 50 still to be written.

heading: Guardrails (v1, built in P03) > Audit trail versus explanations
text: - **Audit trail** (`ai_calls`, `GET /api/judge/audit`): one row per AI call for the team and judges. Ids, hashes, token counts, cost, latency, validator codes, checker verdict, retries, fallback used, reviewer decision. It never holds prompt text, teacher text or model output. - **Explanations** (`ai/guard/explain.py`): one line a user sees, built by code from facts already computed, in English, Hindi and Tamil. Teacher-facing lines use counts ("11 of 28 children"), never percentages. Example: "Held back: the checker found a maths error."

heading: Guardrails (v1, built in P03) > Fallbacks and budget
text: Every call has a timeout, bounded retries (live turns retry once, stating what was wrong) and a deterministic fallback: a template line, or "needs a human". Non-judge traffic stops at `AI_BUDGET_USD_TOTAL` and `AI_BUDGET_USD_DAILY`; judge traffic stops at `AI_BUDGET_USD_HARD`.

heading: Guardrails (v1, built in P03) > Call 10: demo teacher (judge mode only, built 22 Oct)
text: The AI that plays the teacher in the Practice Class "Watch" mode. It never reaches a real teacher, who hears the reviewed model run. Guardrails: the move id must be on the scenario's approved list; the line is 25 words or fewer; every number comes from the scenario's allowed set; no answer leak beyond what the style allows (the experienced style leaks nothing); on any failure the move's template line is used and the audit row records the fallback.

heading: Guardrails (v1, built in P03) > Call 10: demo teacher (judge mode only, built 22 Oct)
text: The server refuses the call outside a judge session, every line is labelled "AI playing the teacher (demo only)", and recorded runs are labelled "recorded run". Eval 11 measures it. Spec: `docs/design/addendum-v3.1.md` §C.

heading: Judge guide: a ten-minute test path > What you are testing
text: Cohort Coach is a tool for primary teachers in India that groups them for training by the specific mistake their pupils make, and helps them rehearse the fix before using it on children. Everything in the demo is simulated or labelled as simulated. The judge guide answers from the repository, the rubric map, the deck and the video script, and gives an honest status for each claim: Built, Partly built, Simulated, Mock or Roadmap.

heading: Judge guide: a ten-minute test path > Sign-in
text: Judge mode needs no sign-in and holds no real user's data. The staff pilot has its own sign-in, with accounts held by the team; judges do not need it. Use View as in the assistant panel to see another role's assistant on demo data. The About this product tab always answers as the judge guide.

heading: Judge guide: a ten-minute test path > The path
text: 1. Open the web app. The landing page shows four role cards and a five-minute guided tour. Ask the guide: who is the user? 2. Open the guided tour at step 1. It runs the check on sample sheets and shows the error card with where learning most likely broke down. 3. On the Judge page, choose Load a simulated class, then open My class. Each card shows a count of children, never a percentage.

heading: Judge guide: a ten-minute test path > The path
text: 4. Open Practice, choose Start, and type: Priya, what is 52 minus 29? Then type: Tell me how you got that. Open the Judge tab and choose Show AI layers to see the five layers of one turn. 5. Open the AI map and then the audit trail. Open Try to break it to see which check stops each prepared bad line.

heading: Judge guide: a ten-minute test path > The path
text: 6. Choose the Coach role on the landing page and open the review screen. Choose Officer and open the results to see one working track, one not working and one hidden under five classes. 7. On the Judge page choose Simulate offline, then open Enter check. The result waits and is sent when you go back online.

heading: Judge guide: a ten-minute test path > The path
text: 8. Switch the language in the top bar of the landing page and open My profile to see the same screens in Hindi or Tamil. 9. In the assistant, open About this product and ask: what is real and what is simulated?

heading: Judge guide: a ten-minute test path > What is real and what is simulated
text: The error counts, the cohorts, the verdicts and the children in the Practice Class are simulated. The model calls are real: Claude reads sheet photos, labels the teacher's moves, speaks as the simulated children and drafts modules. The pilot server is real and holds no real class data yet.

heading: Judge guide: a ten-minute test path > Where to look
text: The rubric map, docs/RUBRIC_MAP.md, lists every claim with its status, code path, test, demo steps, slide and video time. The README table Where AI is used is generated from ai/registry.py.

heading: Judge guide: a ten-minute test path > Paper Studio (check papers made by code)
text: As a teacher, open Papers, tap Create a paper and choose Generate from rules. Choose a new paper and tap Make the paper: you see the anchor and adaptive items, the answer key, a grid of which items check each error, the automatic check results, and its frozen post-test twin; Print opens the real PDF. As a coach, open Papers: the review queue, the published rules and Test these rules.

heading: Judge guide: a ten-minute test path > Paper Studio (check papers made by code)
text: No AI is used: code builds every paper from approved rules and an independent verifier re-checks it. Sample PDFs are in `docs/samples/` (class "SAMPLE", no child data); the rules are in `rules/paper-rules.v1.yaml`; the check of generated papers in every language is `docs/evidence/paper_studio_verification.md`.

heading: Judge guide: a ten-minute test path > The demo flow, step by step
text: Open the Judge page and tap Run the demo flow (or open #/demo?step=1). A bar on every screen shows Demo step n of 12 (step 13, two classes, is optional), with Back, Next, the judge guide's question for the step, and Reset demo.

heading: Judge guide: a ten-minute test path > The demo flow, step by step
text: The steps: 1 start as a teacher with a made-up class 3A; 2 make the pre-test paper in Paper Studio (the pilot paper, Form A); 3 generate 20 filled demo sheets and download them; 4 upload sheet 1 for the AI to read, then Auto-fill the other sheets from the demo answer file (no AI call); 5 review each sheet in the drawer and approve it; 6 finish entering, then Simulate other classes' results; 7 see the three cohorts (her class is in 2 of them: one this term and one next term, because a class takes one track a term); 8 make the first audio module (Demo: pre-approved); 9 try it in Practice Class; 10 ask the cohort a question (a 60 second wait, Skip the wait; the AI answers only from approved material and says when it has none); 11 the coach's queue and the SCERT officer's dashboard; 12 the post-test (optional) with before and after; 13 (optional) two classes to a cohort.

heading: Judge guide: a ten-minute test path > What is simulated in the demo
text: The class, its 20 children, their answers and sheets are made up by code from demo/scenarios/class_3a.yaml and labelled Demo. The 24 other classes come from the simulated block generator and are labelled Simulated, and so is every cohort count and dashboard number. The mentor's method card is a simulated mentor's. The demo sheets are synthetic, so the reading summary is not evidence of accuracy on real handwriting.

heading: Judge guide: a ten-minute test path > What is simulated in the demo
text: Real: Paper Studio, the sheet reader call on sheet 1, the error finder, the grouping and mentor rules, the module drafter and its checks, the chat service and its gates, the review queues.

heading: Judge guide: a ten-minute test path > Papers page (create, import, assign, cohort status)
text: Papers sits between Home and Enter check. Create a paper offers two routes: Generate from rules (Paper Studio) and From a PDF or an answered sheet. In the PDF route a vision call (call 16) reads only the printed questions; code computes every key, error probe and coverage cell with the engine, an independent check agrees, a printed key that differs is flagged, and a person confirms each item.

heading: Judge guide: a ten-minute test path > Papers page (create, import, assign, cohort status)
text: Handwriting and names are ignored and the upload is deleted on confirmation or after 24 hours. The assistant panel asks one open question at a time and its answers go through the same whitelisted edit as a typed change, tagged Assistant changed this with an Undo. Each paper shows whether cohorts formed and the reason if not.

heading: Judge guide: a ten-minute test path > Papers page (create, import, assign, cohort status)
text: Roles: a teacher assigns only to her own class, a mentor inside the cohorts she mentors, a coach inside their programme; the officer has no access. See docs/build/reports/PAPERS-PAGE.md for what is built and what is not.

heading: Judge guide: a ten-minute test path > Why did no cohort form?
text: A cohort forms when enough classes share the same track. Each class gets one track: writing a number as it is said (PV-HEARD) first, otherwise the mistake the most children made, and only when at least 1 child in 4 showed it with at least 10 children checked. A child shows a mistake only when it appears on at least 2 of the questions that check it.

heading: Judge guide: a ten-minute test path > Why did no cohort form?
text: The screen gives every class's reason for each mistake: in, under 1 in 4, another track, too few children checked, or no track for that mistake yet. A class that is the first to submit waits for other classes. In production a cohort needs 15 classes (COHORT_MIN_CLASSES). The pilot and the demo allow 2, labelled "Pilot cohort, two classes".

heading: Judge guide: a ten-minute test path > Why did no cohort form?
text: When a paper has only one question of a kind, such as borrowing across a zero (703 - 468), the 2-question rule cannot be met there. The pilot and the demo may then count that one question (COHORT_ALLOW_SINGLE_ITEM_PROBES), and the cohort says "Based on one question per child". Production leaves this off. At pilot scale there is no waitlist: both classes are trained, and the pilot compares the trained mistake with the untrained ones.

heading: Judge guide: a ten-minute test path > How is the next module chosen?
text: Code chooses it; the AI only words it. After module 1 the teacher plays it or marks it heard, then answers Tried it, Partly or Not yet, with an optional note (a child's name is removed before it is saved). Then she can press Generate next module, and the coach can press it for her. Tried it gives the next module in the track. Partly gives the same approach again, as a smaller step with more practice.

heading: Judge guide: a ten-minute test path > How is the next module chosen?
text: Not yet gives another approach for the same mistake from the strategy library, leaving out the approaches she has already had. If she has not answered by the set date (3 days in the demo), the planned next module is queued, and her silence is never counted as a result. Call 5 words the module from the approved module topic and strategies; if no draft comes back, code writes it from the same content.

heading: Judge guide: a ten-minute test path > How is the next module chosen?
text: Every module goes to the coach's review queue before it reaches her, voiced in her language with her class's numbers filled in by code. A failed voice leaves the text, with a retry.

heading: Judge guide: a ten-minute test path > Your cohorts and what is happening in each
text: Two classes, step 5 (Cohorts) lists each cohort you coach: the mistake, the number of classes and teachers, the children in the cohort who showed it, and the mentor suggestion or why there is none.

heading: Judge guide: a ten-minute test path > Your cohorts and what is happening in each
text: It also shows module 1's status in each language, plays (system), modules marked heard (self-report), feedback (tried, partly, not yet) with notes that have names removed, the next modules' status, chat activity (open questions, AI drafts waiting, answers sent by the AI, corrections) and the next check. A timeline lists every event, with links to the review queue and the chat. Counts only, never a child.

heading: Judge guide: a ten-minute test path > Your cohorts and what is happening in each
text: A mentor sees only her own cohort, and an officer sees totals, with any figure over fewer than 5 classes hidden.

heading: Judge guide: a ten-minute test path > Recorded AI answers and AI off
text: The header says AI: recorded answers when the server replays recorded AI answers (AI_MODE=recorded), and each replayed answer says Recorded AI answer. It says AI: off when the AI is switched off (AI_MODE=off); then each AI feature says so and offers its non-AI path, and nothing pretends to be an AI answer. Calls 4 (method card) and 6 (digest) are planned, not built, and the AI map says so.

heading: Judge guide: a ten-minute test path > Recorded AI answers and AI off
text: A newly made demo sheet has no recording to replay, so in recorded mode sheet 1 says so and Auto-fill carries on. Report: docs/build/reports/QA-DEMO.md.

text: > **Kit v3 (19 Oct):** this page describes the v1 build, where the check is entered on the phone and only counts sync. In v3 the check arrives as photos through the bot or the PWA and the flows run on one back end; this page is rewritten in P05 and P14. heading: Offline, low data, cheap phones (v1, after P05)

Rows for features built in later phases are marked "later" and are filled in as they land. **Target phone:** an Android Go-class phone with 2 GB of RAM running Chrome. **Install:** a PWA from the browser, no app store. **First load:** under 1 MB of compressed JavaScript; the measured figure is in `docs/evidence/bundle_size.json`. Fonts are the phone's system fonts and there are no images, only SVG icons.

heading: Offline, low data, cheap phones (v1, after P05) > The trade-off, said plainly
text: Rehearsing with simulated children is the most useful feature and the only one that needs a live connection. It falls back to text on a weak signal, and (P14) to practice cards with scripted branches when offline. The check, the diagnosis, the error cards and, later, the lessons all work with no signal.
