heading: Practice Class (v1, built in P04)
text: > **A hypothesis, not a result.** That rehearsing with simulated children improves what a teacher does in class has not been tested by any source we have; it is the hypothesis the pilot tests, and we report the verdict whatever it is (CLAUDE.md rule 13). Nothing on this page claims it works.

heading: Practice Class (v1, built in P04)
text: A teacher rehearses a technique with five simulated children who make her own class's mistakes. **Code decides every number; Claude only supplies the children's words.** Text mode is built; voice (P07) and the screens (P06) come next.

heading: Practice Class (v1, built in P04) > The screen (T5)
text: Five original SVG children with their names and a highlight on whoever spoke (plain shapes, no gender, religion or caste markers; the one who speaks only when named is marked "shy"). A materials tray with bundles of ten, loose sticks and a place-value chart: a tap is a move. A text box, a turn counter ("Turn 2 of 40"), and "End and see feedback".

heading: Practice Class (v1, built in P04) > The screen (T5)
text: The feedback card shows two strengths and one thing to try with her own words highlighted, a "Checked ✓" badge, a thumbs up or down per point, a "this is wrong" flag and "Try again with the same children" (same seed, same seats). The transcript is saved on the phone only. "Share this session to improve the simulator" is off by default and, for now, only records her choice.

heading: Practice Class (v1, built in P04) > The screen (T5)
text: Tests: `apps/pwa/e2e/practice.spec.ts` ("a rehearsal of 7 turns with a material tap…", "retry uses the same children", "feedback thumbs and the flag are kept on the phone; sharing is off by default and remembered"); application logs hold none of what she types: `tests/practice/test_api.py::test_no_log_record_at_any_level_holds_what_she_typed`.

heading: Practice Class (v1, built in P04) > The screen (T5)
text: Judge mode adds **Show AI layers**: under each reply, the turn's five layers straight from the API's `layers` trace (the label and its confidence, the engine's decision and strength change, the validators, the checker's verdict, latency, tokens and cost, the output and its badge). Pages for the **AI map** (the registry as 8 calls by 5 layers) and the **Audit trail** (the last 50 AI calls as metadata) are linked from the judge script. Teachers never see the overlay.

heading: Practice Class (v1, built in P04) > The screen (T5)
text: Seats follow the class: from Home the app sends the class's counts (never a child's answers) and, in judge mode with no class on the phone, the scenario's default mix. Degraded states are shown, not hidden: a template reply says "the connection is slow, so a simple reply was used"; when the day's budget is spent, "Practice is paused for today" with a recorded sample rehearsal to watch; offline, "Practice needs a connection" with everything else still working.

heading: Practice Class (v1, built in P04) > The screen (T5)
text: The screenshots in `docs/evidence/screenshots/` (`en-5` to `en-9`) were taken against the API in **recorded mode**, replaying a rehearsal recorded live, so their latencies are replay times, not real ones; real latencies are in `docs/evidence/` (`practice_latency.json`). Live-mode screenshots follow once staging exists.

heading: Practice Class (v1, built in P04) > How one turn works
text: Two Claude calls and one checker call per turn (calls 2, 1 and 7), plus call 3 at the end. A material tap (bundles, sticks, chart) is a move without a labeller call. Every turn returns a `layers` trace (input, processing, guardrails, evaluation, output) that judge mode renders in P06.

heading: Practice Class (v1, built in P04) > One live turn, in the five layers
text: From a live rehearsal (2026-10-17, scripted synthetic lines, `evals/sets/practice_scripts/sub-sfl-en.txt`; the whole session, every turn's `layers`, the feedback card with its two verbatim quotes, and the cost are in `docs/evidence/practice_session_live.json`: 7 turns, median 5344 ms per turn, cost USD 0.0288 including the feedback). Turn 2, an excerpt of that file:

heading: Practice Class (v1, built in P04) > The rules the engine follows
text: From `CLAUDE.md` section 5; the values are tuning parameters in `content/movelists/` and `content/scenarios/`, owned by Seema. - Five fictional children. Seat 0 is always correct; seats are filled to match her class's error mix (if 40% of the class shows SUB-SFL, 2 of the 5 children do); one child is shy and speaks only when named.

heading: Practice Class (v1, built in P04) > The rules the engine follows
text: - Each child with an error has a strength from 0 to 1, starting at 0.9, and an engagement level. A child answers wrong with probability equal to her strength, and the wrong number is always the bug function's answer. - Moves: show with bundles −0.3, ask to explain −0.2, check by adding back −0.2, just tell the rule −0.05, praise raises engagement, scolding lowers it and the child goes quiet for two turns.

heading: Practice Class (v1, built in P04) > The rules the engine follows
text: - When asked to explain, the engine produces the faulty working as data ("2 minus 9 can't be done, 9 minus 2 is 7, 5 minus 2 is 3"); the model only rephrases it. When she checks by adding back, the engine makes the check ("37 plus 29 is 66, not 52"). - A session ends when every child with the error has been right twice in a row, or at 40 turns (also the judge-mode cap).

heading: Practice Class (v1, built in P04) > The rules the engine follows
text: - If she names no child, the child she was talking to continues; if she speaks to the class, the engine picks a speaker by engagement.

heading: Practice Class (v1, built in P04) > Why an engine, not just a prompt
text: A language model asked to play a confused child can drift: it gets the sum right by accident or invents an error no child makes. Putting the error in code keeps the children faithful to her class, makes sessions reproducible (a seeded generator per turn: the same seed and script replay exactly) and makes the simulator testable. The simulator fidelity eval checks that every number a child says is the engine's, against an independent oracle: `docs/evidence/eval_summary.md` (Eval 2).

heading: Practice Class (v1, built in P04) > The three calls
text: | Call | Does | Guards (code) | | 2 labeller | Labels her line with one move from the lesson's list, who she addressed, and a problem she posed | Move list enforced as a JSON-schema enum; low confidence → `other`; injection markers → `off_task` by code; a posed problem must use numbers she said and be a valid two-digit problem; line cut at 600 characters |

heading: Practice Class (v1, built in P04) > The three calls
text: | 1 child voice | Puts the plan into 1–2 short sentences in the child's voice | Numbers ⊆ the plan's allowed set; digits only (no number words); at most 30 words; script matches the language; pre-filter; an `answer` line must contain the planned answer; one retry, then a template line; then call 7 |

heading: Practice Class (v1, built in P04) > The three calls
text: | 3 feedback | Two strengths and one thing to try, each quoting her words | Each quote verbatim in the turn it cites and in her words, not a child's; points only from the rubric; a strength's turn must carry one of that point's moves; no scores; numbers only from the transcript and the engine; then call 7. If it fails, a card built by code from the rubric and her own lines |

heading: Practice Class (v1, built in P04) > The three calls
text: Scolding is named gently by a note the app writes itself (`content/templates/feedback_notes.yaml`), not by the model. The AI never scores a teacher.

heading: Practice Class (v1, built in P04) > Privacy
text: - Nothing about a rehearsal is stored on the server. Session state is in memory with a two-hour limit, and the full transcript goes back to her phone. - The audit trail keeps metadata only (call, model, tokens, cost, latency, validator codes). Practice Class calls are marked `metadata_only`. Her words never reach the audit rows, the judge endpoints or the logs.

heading: Practice Class (v1, built in P04) > Privacy
text: - Children are fictional, named from a reviewed list (`content/personas/children.v1.yaml`): first names only, balanced by gender, temperament only, no caste, religion, region or disability markers. - A real child's voice is never used.

heading: Practice Class (v1, built in P04) > Modes
text: | Mode | What it is | Use | | `recorded` | Replays `ai/fixtures/recorded/` (a real session recorded on 2026-10-17 from synthetic lines) | Tests, CI, demos; no network | | `live` | The Claude API | Real rehearsals; prints and logs cost | | `record` | Live, and saves each answer as a fixture | Re-recording after a prompt change |

heading: Practice Class (v1, built in P04) > Modes
text: | `stub` | `services/practice/stub_client.py`: rule-based, not a model | Offline demos and API tests; makes no claim about model quality | Rehearse in the terminal: `python tasks.py practice --scenario sub-sfl --lang en --stub` (or `--live`, `--recorded --script evals/sets/practice_scripts/sub-sfl-en.txt --seed 5`).

heading: Practice Class (v1, built in P04) > API
text: `POST /api/practice/sessions` (scenario, language, optional class counts) → session id, the five children (names and which one is shy; not who has which error), materials, move labels. `POST /api/practice/sessions/{id}/turns` (text or material tap) → child, line, numbers, label, badge, explanation, `layers`, latency. `POST /api/practice/sessions/{id}/end` → the feedback card and the transcript.

heading: Practice Class (v1, built in P04) > What the live runs found
text: Recorded here because they changed the build; numbers are in `docs/evidence/eval_summary.md`. - The checker (call 7) first rejected valid child lines: it read the engine's deliberate wrong answers as maths errors and a bare "37, Miss!" as not fitting a lesson. Prompt v2 to v4 tell it the line is a simulated child, that code has already checked every number, and that it judges tone, safety, stereotypes, language, reading level, injection and role.

heading: Practice Class (v1, built in P04) > What the live runs found
text: - With thinking on, the checker sometimes ran out of tokens and returned nothing, so it failed closed. Short rule-bound calls now run with thinking off where the API allows it, with larger token limits. - The red team found a Hinglish role-reversal line labelled `other` instead of `off_task`. The child stayed in role and nothing changed, but the labeller prompt (v3) now lists off-task examples in four languages.

heading: Practice Class (v1, built in P04) > What the live runs found
text: - Latency: three serial calls (label, child line, check) put the median text turn above the 3 s target. The plan: in voice mode the checker runs while the speech is synthesised (P07), so its time is hidden; the API server will sit near the Claude endpoint (P15); an A/B with Haiku for call 1 was slower and is not adopted. Text mode stays over target until then, and the Practice Class degrades to templates when a call times out.

heading: Practice Class (v1, built in P04) > One to three children speak, and the room overhears (31 Oct 2026)
text: - **Who speaks.** The engine picks one to three children each turn: the child she named first, then others chosen by engagement. The shy child speaks only when named and a child who went quiet stays out. The first speaker is made exactly as before; the others answer the problem on the board in their own words from the engine's templates (their answer is right or wrong by the same bug function) or agree, thank or say they are lost. They never use the AI.

heading: Practice Class (v1, built in P04) > One to three children speak, and the room overhears (31 Oct 2026)
text: - **Who hears.** Every child in the class hears what the teacher says to one child. The named child gets the full effect of the move on her error strength and engagement; the others get `overhear` (0.5 in the scenario files) of it. Scolding makes only the child it was aimed at go quiet.

heading: Practice Class (v1, built in P04) > One to three children speak, and the room overhears (31 Oct 2026)
text: - **Speed switches (.env).** `PRACTICE_SKIP_CHECKER=1` skips call 7 on a child's line; the validators and pre-filter still run. `PRACTICE_AI_INTENTS=explain,work_aloud` sends only explanations to call 1; any other line is a template. Both are off by default. Decision: `docs/build/DECISIONS.md` (2026-10-31).

heading: Practice Class (v1, built in P04) > Voice through the speech layer (1 Nov 2026, branch `speech-bodhan`)
text: Speech goes through the provider chain (`services/speech/chain.py`): Bodhan AI first, Sarvam as the fallback (Prompt 3 of `docs/build/bodhan-speech-prompts.md`; report `docs/build/reports/SPEECH-PRACTICE.md`).

heading: Practice Class (v1, built in P04) > Voice through the speech layer (1 Nov 2026, branch `speech-bodhan`)
text: - **In.** The phone records in the format it supports (`MediaRecorder.isTypeSupported`) and sends the file as recorded. A timer counts to 25 s and the recording stops by itself at 25 s, with a message. The server converts to 16 kHz mono WAV, trims silence, never sends more than 28 s in one request, passes the session language, and drops the audio once the text exists. Silence or a very short clip is never sent or scored.

heading: Practice Class (v1, built in P04) > Voice through the speech layer (1 Nov 2026, branch `speech-bodhan`)
text: - **Masking.** The transcript and typed lines are masked before calls 1 to 3 (`mask_personal`, keeping the five pretend children's names); this was already in place and is tested by `tests/practice/test_session.py::test_a_real_childs_name_is_masked_before_any_model_call_but_the_pretend_children_keep_theirs`.

heading: Practice Class (v1, built in P04) > Voice through the speech layer (1 Nov 2026, branch `speech-bodhan`)
text: - **Out.** Each child keeps one Bodhan voice for the session, chosen by seat and the persona's gender from `content/voices.yaml` (distinct from the lesson narrator), with her Sarvam voice as the fallback. The engine's mood sets the style by code: bright to happy, small to sad, the others to the voice's neutral reading. A child's line is at most 120 characters (a gate check). Speech is still started in parallel with call 7 and released only on pass; chorus lines are voiced in parallel; a failure leaves that child's line as text.

heading: Practice Class (v1, built in P04) > Voice through the speech layer (1 Nov 2026, branch `speech-bodhan`)
text: - **Failures and caps.** A failed line is text only and the next turn tries again; after two failures in a row (no audio, or the first provider failing so a fallback answered) the session moves to the next provider for the rest of it. Each session has a speech allowance (`SPEECH_SESSION_MAX_STT_SECONDS`, `SPEECH_SESSION_MAX_TTS_CHARS`); when it is used, "Voice is off for the rest of this practice. The text continues."

heading: Practice Class (v1, built in P04) > Voice through the speech layer (1 Nov 2026, branch `speech-bodhan`)
text: - **Rate limit.** Bodhan's default allowance is about 8 requests a minute per model, so a live turn waits at most `BODHAN_LIVE_PACE_MAX_WAIT_S` (2 s) for it before Sarvam speaks instead. - **Cache.** Lines are cached in memory and in the private audio store (`line-cache/`); `python tasks.py practice-pregen` voices the engine's template lines ahead of time. `scripts/voice_audition.py` makes a listening page to choose the voices.

heading: Practice Class (v1, built in P04) > Voice through the speech layer (1 Nov 2026, branch `speech-bodhan`)
text: - **Timing.** Every voice turn records each stage and the provider in `layers.evaluation.timing`; `scripts/practice_voice_latency.py` reports medians and 95th percentiles (mock, or `--live --yes`).

text: - **What to practise.** The screen starts with the goal (the error in plain words) and the rubric's "try next" lines in her language. Both come from content files, not from AI.

heading: Practice Class (v1, built in P04) > Review, impact tags, cues and language (added 2026-10-19)
text: - **What can I say?** A button opens a cue card: for every move on the list, example lines in her language (`content/movelists/*.yaml`, `examples`), with the example child's name replaced by one of her five children. Tapping a line puts it in the box to change. A move that makes children go quiet is never cued. Four delivery tips (speak slowly, ask then wait, say the name first, praise the trying) are drafts for Seema.

heading: Practice Class (v1, built in P04) > Review, impact tags, cues and language (added 2026-10-19)
text: - **Recorded on the phone.** Each rehearsal is saved in IndexedDB as it goes: turns, the move she used (labelled by call 2), language, seed, and the feedback card. Nothing is sent. She can delete one recording or all of them.

heading: Practice Class (v1, built in P04) > Review, impact tags, cues and language (added 2026-10-19)
text: - **Review tab.** Lists rehearsals newest first with date, the error practised, number of turns and her tag. Opening one replays it turn by turn (Previous and Next), shows the moves she used with counts, her feedback card and an impact picker, and "Practise again with the same children". The summary is counts ("Rehearsals: 4. Helped: 2. No difference: 1. Did not help: 1."), never percentages.

heading: Practice Class (v1, built in P04) > Review, impact tags, cues and language (added 2026-10-19)
text: - **Impact tag.** "Did this rehearsal help?": It helped, No difference, It did not help. It is her own view, kept on the phone, labelled as hers; it is not a score and nothing else reads it (`CLAUDE.md` rules 3 and 11). It does not say anything about whether children improved: only the next check shows that.

heading: Practice Class (v1, built in P04) > Review, impact tags, cues and language (added 2026-10-19)
text: - **Language.** The session is created in the language selected in the app; goal, tips, cues, child names, materials, feedback and explanation lines arrive in it. If she switches language mid-rehearsal, a banner offers "Restart in <language>" (same children). A Playwright test checks that the home, check and practice screens (with the cue card open) show no English words in Hindi or Tamil. - Tested by `apps/pwa/e2e/review.spec.ts`, `apps/pwa/src/lib/review.test.ts` and `tests/practice/test_api.py`.

The in-app notice (`/#/privacy`, three languages) says the same things in plain words.

heading: Privacy and DPDP (draft, 2026-10-20) > 3. What is not done
text: - The grievance contact and the nominee and breach processes are placeholders. - No server-side access request (a teacher can only export from her phone), and no server-side deletion for feedback (it is anonymous by design). - `ADMIN_KEY` is a shared key, not named admin accounts. With no key the admin endpoints are closed (503); `ADMIN_OPEN=1` opens them for local dev and the judge demo only, and must never be set on a public server.

heading: Privacy and DPDP (draft, 2026-10-20) > 3. What is not done
text: - Withdrawing consent stops sending and drops queued feedback, but counts already sent stay on the server until she erases them. Consent records on the server are kept as proof and are not erased by "Erase everything"; the phone's own consent record, device id and settings are. - If "Erase everything" runs offline the server's class counts are not erased (the class ids are gone from the phone); a pending-erase queue is not built.

heading: Privacy and DPDP (draft, 2026-10-20) > 3. What is not done
text: - A teacher can still type a child's name into feedback text: the server only refuses phone numbers, emails and ID numbers. That is why the admin page must stay closed to the public. - No named data fiduciary, no cross-border statement, no breach statement and no rate limit on feedback and consent posts yet. - The fetch meter clones each API response that lacks a content-length to count it; on very low-end phones this doubles a reply's memory briefly.

heading: Privacy and DPDP (draft, 2026-10-20) > 3. What is not done
text: - Consent for a teacher who is a minor, and the age gate, are not needed (teachers are adults) and are not built. - Retention periods for server data are stated as "while the programme runs"; a number of days should be agreed. - Data localisation and cross-border transfer (Claude and Sarvam endpoints) have not been reviewed. - The pilot's roll-number pairing is covered in `CLAUDE.md` section 4 (local script, nothing leaves the machine).

heading: Privacy and DPDP (draft, 2026-10-20) > 4. Practical notes
text: - **Backup files hold children's answers.** The app says so next to the export button; sealing with a passphrase is optional, not forced. - **Persistent storage** is requested so the browser does not clear the phone's data; a browser may decline, and the profile page says which it did. - **Data used** is counted on the phone from the app's own calls and never sent.

heading: Privacy and DPDP (draft, 2026-10-20) > 4. Practical notes
text: - Uploads from the Practice Class voice turn may be spooled to a temporary file by the framework above 1 MB; the audio is the teacher's own and is deleted on close (see `docs/speech.md`).

heading: Privacy and DPDP (draft, 2026-10-20) > Stage of breakdown (22 Oct)
text: The stages (input, core, output) are worked out on the phone from the answers she typed or confirmed, with signature answers the engine writes into the answer keys; a parity test checks the phone's result against the Python engine on 136 synthetic children (`tests/fixtures/stage_cases.json`). The per-child rows never leave the phone. What stays on the phone with the check is her tag "missed the teaching on this" per child position.

heading: Privacy and DPDP (draft, 2026-10-20) > Stage of breakdown (22 Oct)
text: What reaches the server is nothing new: the class counts per error, as before. A stage is always "most likely", never shown to a child, and never a judgement of a child or a teacher. `POST /api/stages` (stateless, nothing stored or logged, a 300-child cap) exists for the bot's check flow in a later phase and is not called by the web app.

heading: Privacy and DPDP (draft, 2026-10-20) > Abuse and cost limits (27 Oct)
text: The endpoints that start a paid call (Practice Class sessions, turns, voice turns, the demo teacher's run, and sheet reading) accept a limited number of requests per minute from one connection (`services/api/ratelimit.py`; the limits and their environment names are in `.env.example`). Over the limit the answer is 429 with a Retry-After. The limit is kept in memory per server process and holds no personal data; the spend hard-stops in `ai/client.py` remain the backstop.

heading: Privacy and DPDP (draft, 2026-10-20) > Abuse and cost limits (27 Oct)
text: The audit-trail and AI-map endpoints answer only in the judge-mode deployment (a test locks this). When `AUDIT_HASH_SALT` is set the audit log's input hashes are keyed, so a short or guessable input cannot be confirmed from the log. **Assistant embeddings (optional, off by default).** With `RETRIEVAL=vector`, the assistant sends the *masked* question text (names, roll numbers, phones and emails already removed) to the Gemini embeddings API to find matching help pages.

heading: Privacy and DPDP (draft, 2026-10-20) > Abuse and cost limits (27 Oct)
text: The pages are repository and help text, embedded offline; no child, teacher or class data is embedded or sent. Source: `services/assistant/vector.py`. **Sheet pictures on the Check screen.** The picture of each sheet (taken with the camera or chosen from a folder or the gallery) is shrunk on the phone, read once, and kept in the browser's memory only, per roll number, so the drawer can show it beside the boxes.

heading: Privacy and DPDP (draft, 2026-10-20) > Abuse and cost limits (27 Oct)
text: It is never written to the phone's storage (not IndexedDB, not the cache, not local storage) and is dropped when she finishes entering, reloads, or leaves the screen. The exception is the opt-in above: if she agreed, the picture of a sheet she approves is sent once more, to her private bucket, and kept for 60 days (see the table).

heading: Privacy and DPDP (draft, 2026-10-20) > Abuse and cost limits (27 Oct)
text: The file's SHA-256 is sent with the picture so a recorded answer can be replayed; it identifies a file, not a child. If a sheet has a class code and roll number in its header, the reader returns them to the phone only; the reading call keeps no photo and its audit row holds metadata only (`apps/pwa/src/screens/Check.tsx`, `e2e/enter-check.spec.ts`, `e2e/photo.spec.ts`). **Check labels and before-and-after (30 Oct).** A check's label (kind, paper, date, term) is stored with it on the phone.

heading: Privacy and DPDP (draft, 2026-10-20) > Abuse and cost limits (27 Oct)
text: Pairing a pre-test with a post-test runs on the phone, by roll order, and the screen shows counts per competency only. Nothing new is sent to the server: the class counts sent at the end of a check are unchanged. `scripts/pilot_results.py` reads an unsealed backup on the coordinator's own machine and writes counts only (`tests/test_pilot_results.py`).

heading: Browser QA rubric
text: How every page of the web app is judged in a real browser. Results are generated into [docs/evidence/browser_qa.md](evidence/browser_qa.md); nothing is scored by hand.

heading: Browser QA rubric > How it is run
text: 1. Build the web app and start the API in recorded and stub mode (no paid calls): see `apps/pwa/playwright.config.ts` for the settings. 2. `node apps/pwa/qa/crawl.mjs docs/evidence/browser_qa` opens every route in Chromium in English, Hindi and Tamil, at a 360 px phone width and a 1280 px desktop width (132 page views), and writes `report.json`. 3. `npx playwright test --reporter=list > docs/evidence/browser_qa/e2e_list.txt` runs the feature tests (taps, forms, offline, voice, review, cohort). 4. `python scripts/browser_qa_report.py` scores each route.

heading: Browser QA rubric > The five criteria (0 to 2 each, 10 in all)
text: | Criterion | 2 | 1 | 0 | | Loads clean | No blank page, console error, failed API call or "undefined" in all 6 views | 1 view fails | 2 or more fail | | Languages | No raw string key or blank page in Hindi or Tamil | 1 view fails | 2 or more fail |

heading: Browser QA rubric > The five criteria (0 to 2 each, 10 in all)
text: | Layout and touch | No horizontal scroll at either width; every tap target at least 40 px high on the phone (the design asks for 44) | 1 view fails | 2 or more fail | | Browser feature test | At least 2 passing feature tests drive the page | 1 test | None |

heading: Browser QA rubric > The five criteria (0 to 2 each, 10 in all)
text: | Rules | No percentage, "percent" or its Hindi or Tamil word on a teacher screen | 1 view fails | 2 or more fail | Bands: Pass 9 to 10, Partial 6 to 8, Gap 5 or less.

heading: Browser QA rubric > What this does not cover
text: - A real low-end phone and Slow 3G (the checklist item Gate 2): the crawl uses Chromium with a phone viewport. - Telegram (roadmap, not in the demo): the same flows are covered by the golden-transcript tests through each adapter, not in a browser. - Live AI and live speech: the run uses recorded fixtures and stub speech, so it tests the screens, not the models. - Whether a page is easy to understand. That needs the user-testing rounds (`docs/feedback-log.md`).

heading: Browser QA rubric > What this does not cover
text: - The crawl opens each page in its first state, as an officer, so a page that needs a longer journey to reach its main content is judged by its feature tests, not by the crawl.

heading: Speech: voice in the Practice Class (v1, after P07)
text: A teacher can hold a button and speak to the five pretend children, and hear each child answer in a different voice. Speech is the second AI layer on top of the text pipeline, not a separate path: speech-to-text produces her words, the same pipeline (label, engine, child line, gates) produces the child's line, and text-to-speech reads it. If any speech step fails, she is moved to typing and nothing is lost.

heading: Speech: voice in the Practice Class (v1, after P07)
text: **Status, stated plainly.** Built and tested against mocked HTTP, real ffmpeg and a stub speech service, and since the key was replaced (2026-10-17) run live once: all 36 clips (twelve children in en, hi, ta) synthesised, so the twelve speaker names are accepted by Sarvam (`evals/results/voice_check.json`), and 24 live voice turns were timed (`evals/results/voice_latency.json`). The voice median is **over** the 5 s target (below).

heading: Speech: voice in the Practice Class (v1, after P07)
text: Whether the five children sound distinct is still for a person to confirm: `scripts/check_voices.py` saves the clips for listening.

heading: Speech: voice in the Practice Class (v1, after P07) > The path of one voice turn
text: The audio is never stored by us: it exists only in process memory (and the framework's transient upload buffer while the request is read); the recording is decoded, transcribed and dropped; the reply audio is returned inline and cached in memory only by a hash of the line. A real child's voice is never recorded or used. What she said comes back to her phone as text, like a typed turn, and the transcript stays on the phone.

heading: Speech: voice in the Practice Class (v1, after P07) > Which voice is which child
text: `content/voices/children.v1.yaml` gives each of the twelve fictional children one stock Bulbul v3 speaker and a pitch ratio (configured, between 1.18 and 1.40). Raising the pitch is done by ffmpeg (`asetrate`, `aresample`, `atempo`), which raises the pitch and keeps the speed; a test measures the shift with an FFT and checks the duration is kept.

heading: Speech: voice in the Practice Class (v1, after P07) > Which voice is which child
text: A child therefore sounds the same in every session, and the five seats of a session are configured with different speakers (a test checks the twelve speaker names differ; that they sound different is not yet verified). - Bulbul v3 has no pitch control (`pitch` and `loudness` are v2 only), so the shift is ours.

heading: Speech: voice in the Practice Class (v1, after P07) > Which voice is which child
text: - Cloned voices are built behind `SARVAM_CLONES=1`, off by default and not tested live: Sarvam's docs do not list the clone request fields and publish no licence terms. Policy if switched on: licence-cleared AI-designed voices or a consenting adult, never a real child. - Speaker names were taken from Sarvam's documentation and are unverified. `check_voices.py` reports any speaker the service refuses.

text: | Situation | What happens | | The server has speech, this phone can record, the link is not 2g, and she has not chosen typing before | Hold-to-speak is the main action | | `effectiveType` is `2g` or `slow-2g` | Starts in typing mode; "Use voice" is one tap away | | One voice request fails | A notice; she can try again |

text: | Two in a row fail | Typing takes over by itself with a plain notice; "Use voice" brings it back | | Server circuit breaker: 3 speech failures in a row | Speech is skipped for 30 s (503 with `text_mode`), then one trial request is let through | | Microphone blocked | Notice that says how to allow it, and typing |

heading: Speech: voice in the Practice Class (v1, after P07) > When voice is on, and when it turns itself off
text: | She taps for under 0.4 s, or nothing is heard | Nothing is sent or she is asked to hold and speak again; not counted as a failure | | She chooses "Type instead" | Remembered on this phone | Only the Practice Class needs a connection, and voice is its heaviest form. This is the stated trade-off: voice needs a good signal, typing needs less, and the offline practice cards are the last resort (P14).

heading: Speech: voice in the Practice Class (v1, after P07) > Check-then-release
text: Text-to-speech starts as soon as the candidate line passes the code validators, in parallel with call 7 (the checker), so the checker's time is hidden behind synthesis. The audio is released only if the line passes the checker. If the checker holds the line back, or the model call falls back, the line that is voiced is the safe template line, never the held candidate.

heading: Speech: voice in the Practice Class (v1, after P07) > Check-then-release
text: The held candidate was already sent to Sarvam for synthesis (that is what running in parallel means); it is a fictional child's line, the result is discarded, and an unstarted job is cancelled. `tests/speech/test_voice_turn.py::test_audio_is_released_only_when_the_line_passes_the_checker` checks that the audio sent back is the template line's and not the AI candidate's.

heading: Speech: voice in the Practice Class (v1, after P07) > What is logged
text: One row per speech request in `speech_calls`: stage (stt or tts), mode, language, latency, byte counts, characters, seconds, cost in INR (prices in `services/speech/pricing.yaml`, copied from Sarvam's pricing page on 2026-10-17), cache hit, and the error kind. Never the audio and never the text (a test checks the row against the turn's words). `python scripts/budget.py` shows it. The per-turn trace in judge mode gains `layers.evaluation.stages` (`stt_ms`, `tts_wait_ms`), shown in the AI-layers overlay.

heading: Speech: voice in the Practice Class (v1, after P07) > Limits on the public endpoint
text: A recording is refused above 2 MB (and by `Content-Length` before it is read) or above 30 s of audio after decoding (the phone stops at 25 s); a finished rehearsal is refused (409) before any paid speech call, so the 40-turn judge cap also caps speech spend. Speech has its own daily budget, `SPEECH_BUDGET_INR_DAILY` (default 200, counted in memory per server process from the same cost estimate as `speech_calls`); when it is spent, voice reports `text_mode` and everyone types.

heading: Speech: voice in the Practice Class (v1, after P07) > Limits on the public endpoint
text: Any unexpected error in the speech path becomes `text_mode`, never a 500. A per-IP rate limit is still parked (`docs/build/PARKING.md`) and is needed before the public staging URL. Sending a teacher's voice to Sarvam is the one place audio leaves our server: the hold-to-speak screen should carry a one-line notice and the consent text to be written with Seema (TODO-HUMAN).

heading: Speech: voice in the Practice Class (v1, after P07) > Pronunciation
text: `content/pronunciation/{hi,ta}.yaml` list the maths words to check. Every `say` is empty: nobody has listened yet, and the build does not guess. Words that are filled in become the dictionary file (`services/speech/pronunciation.py`); the id Sarvam returns goes in `SARVAM_DICT_HI` and `SARVAM_DICT_TA`. TODO-HUMAN(Shivani for Hindi, Gopi for Tamil).

heading: Speech: voice in the Practice Class (v1, after P07) > Stub speech (tests and demos)
text: `SPEECH_MODE=stub` (the screen shows "Simulated voice" when it is on) returns scripted teacher lines (the same four lines in each language, in turn) as the "transcript" and a generated tone as the voice. It is not speech recognition, and `speech_mode` in the response says `stub`. The Playwright tests use it with Chromium's fake microphone; they prove the hold-to-speak flow and the fallback, not recognition.

heading: UI guidelines: fewer words, clearer screens (2026-10-20)
text: Teachers using a low-end phone, often in a second language, should be able to use the app without reading paragraphs. These rules came from reviewing every screen on 20 Oct. They sit on top of `docs/design-system.md` (tokens, contrast, tap targets), which still governs.

heading: UI guidelines: fewer words, clearer screens (2026-10-20) > 1. What changed in this pass
text: | Before | Now | Why | | Text-only buttons ("Listen", "This is wrong") and a paragraph under them | Icon buttons (speaker, flag) with an accessible name; the "arrives later" or "thank you" message is a toast that goes by itself | Less text on the card; the message is still announced to screen readers |

heading: UI guidelines: fewer words, clearer screens (2026-10-20) > 1. What changed in this pass
text: | Bottom menu of words | Icon above a short label, scrolls sideways when it does not fit | Faster to find; works from 320 px | | Home with four stacked buttons | One primary action plus a grid of tiles (icon and label) | One obvious next step, the rest one tap away |

heading: UI guidelines: fewer words, clearer screens (2026-10-20) > 1. What changed in this pass
text: | Settings spread across screens | One **My profile**: classes, storage and backup, data used, privacy, feedback, each a titled panel | One place to look | | Raw `<button>` styles per screen | `IconButton`, panels, tiles, chips, switches, stars from one set | Consistent look |

heading: UI guidelines: fewer words, clearer screens (2026-10-20) > 2. Rules
text: 1. **Icon plus label by default; icon alone only for a familiar action** (listen, flag, rename, delete, use). Icon-only controls always carry `aria-label` and `title`. Never an icon as the only carrier of a status: add a word or a shape. 2. **One icon set** (`apps/pwa/src/components/icons.tsx`): inline SVG, 24 px grid, 2 px stroke, `currentColor`. No icon fonts, no images, no extra requests (budget in `CLAUDE.md` section 9).

heading: UI guidelines: fewer words, clearer screens (2026-10-20) > 2. Rules
text: 3. **A sentence on the page only if it is needed to act.** Reassurance, "not yet" and "done" messages go to a toast (`useToast`): short, 4.5 s, tap to close, never the only place a decision is explained. 4. **One primary action per screen**, filled; everything else secondary (outlined). Destructive actions use the danger style and always confirm.

heading: UI guidelines: fewer words, clearer screens (2026-10-20) > 2. Rules
text: 5. **Panels group related controls** (rounded, 1 px line, a title with an icon). At most three levels: screen title, panel title, label. 6. **Counts, never percentages, for teachers** (rule 5); simulated data keeps its banner (rule 6). 7. **Tap targets at least 48 px, text at least 16 px** (tested in `tests/test_design_tokens.py`); icon buttons are 56 px wide.

heading: UI guidelines: fewer words, clearer screens (2026-10-20) > 2. Rules
text: 8. **Language first.** Every string has `en`, `hi`, `ta`. A test scans the home, check, practice, programme and history screens in Hindi and Tamil for stray English words. 9. **Responsive.** Fluid from 320 px; a centred column up to 1000 px; no horizontal scrolling except tables and the menu (tested at 320, 360, 768 and 1280 px). 10. **Colour carries meaning only with a second cue**: green (done), amber (check), red (danger), blue (action); always with an icon or word.

heading: UI guidelines: fewer words, clearer screens (2026-10-20) > 3. How to check a new screen
text: - Open it at 320 px and at 1280 px. Is there any sideways scroll? Is the primary action visible without scrolling on 360 x 640? - Count the sentences above the first action. More than two: move the rest to a toast, a panel behind a tap, or delete it. - Tab through it with a keyboard: every icon control has a name and a visible focus ring. - Switch to Hindi and Tamil: no English, no clipped text.

heading: UI guidelines: fewer words, clearer screens (2026-10-20) > 4. Still to do (listed, not built)
text: - Replace the remaining text-only buttons on the Check keypad and the Practice Class with icons where the meaning is universal. - Audio on every text card (the speaker icon currently answers "arrives in a later step"). - Skeleton loading states, and a first-run walkthrough of three screens. - A dark theme and a larger-text setting. - Review with real teachers (round 3) before tuning further: these rules are the team's judgement, not a test result.

heading: Slide 1: Title
text: Cohort Coach. Grouping primary teachers for training by the mistake their pupils make. Team A-Z 0-9 · Hack2skill × Anthropic "AI for Foundational Learning" · Challenge 3 (Teacher Support and Training).

heading: Slide 2: The problem (five figures)
text: Training is generic, rarely practised, and not followed up; monitoring counts inputs. | Figure | Source (digest row, page) | Scope note to say aloud | | --- | --- | --- | | 3 of 4 States skip a needs analysis before training | FLN 54 | A five-State study | | 75% say training rarely demonstrates or practises | FLN 56; NITI 147 | One State | | 80% of monitoring indicators track inputs | FLN 72, 73 | A five-State study | | Under a third of teachers trained yearly | FLN 54 | A five-State study | | 1,04,125 single-teacher schools | NITI 130 | National | BaSE figures cover EdTech-using teachers only. IDR and APU are opinion and are not used as evidence that anything works.

heading: Slide 3: The idea and the loop
text: A termly 10-item check shows which mistake each class makes. Teachers whose classes share a mistake form a cohort across schools and get a 3-week track on that one mistake. A mentor is a teacher whose class fixed it. The next check says whether children improved, against a comparison group. Loop diagram: check, cohort, track, practice, next check, mentor, next cohort.

heading: Slide 4: The assumption we have not proved
text: Rehearsing a move with simulated children before using it on real ones is a hypothesis. No source we have tests it. The pilot tests it, and we will report the verdict whatever it is. Children are shown to improve only by the next check, never by lessons delivered or sessions held.

heading: Slide 5: AI in layers (the call table)
text: The README's "Where AI is used" table, generated from `ai/registry.py`; each call's input, processing, guardrails, evaluation and output. Show the Practice Class turn as a diagram: teacher's words, move label (call 2), engine chooses the wrong answer, child's line (call 1), checker (call 7), voice. Say which calls are built (1, 2, 3, 5, 7, 8, 10, 11) and which were cut (4, 6, 9): `AI_USAGE.md` is the source.

heading: Slide 6: Guardrails
text: Code computes every number; the model only speaks around it. Four gates: code validators, rule-based pre-filter, the output checker (call 7), a person (the coach, then the officer's key). Every AI card has "this is wrong". Rejections feed the checker. Evidence: red team 52 cases, 0 unsafe reach a teacher (`evals/results.md`); the held-draft finding and its fix (`docs/content-pipeline.md`).

heading: Slide 7: Real scenarios
text: Low connectivity, low data, low-cost phones. A text fallback for every voice step; the check and the lessons queue offline; only the Practice Class needs a live connection, and the deck says so. Computed worst-case data per track: `docs/evidence/data_budget.json` (met with text practice, missed if every session uses voice). Web app first load: `docs/evidence/bundle_size.json`. Not yet measured: Slow 3G and a real low-end phone (`docs/build/PROGRESS.md`).

heading: Slide 8: User inputs and testing (A)
text: how input was collected (the round 3 and 4 plan, `docs/user-testing/`).

heading: Slide 9: User inputs and testing (B)
text: "You said, we changed" from `docs/feedback-log.md` with commit links, with confidence notes. If a round has not happened, the slide says so; it shows no invented quotes.

heading: Slide 10: The pilot, built and live
text: Pilot mode (`PILOT_MODE=1`) on Google Cloud: a coordinator uploads pre-test sheets (private bucket, consent reference, retention), the system reads them, drafts three lessons from the class counts, a coach approves, and the audio is shared on WhatsApp. `docs/build/reports/PILOT-MODE.md`, `docs/deploy.md`.

heading: Slide 11: Honest statistics
text: Officer view: track results with an interval, groups under 5 hidden, a failed track counts against the track, not the teacher. Evidence: `evals/results.md` row 8 (statistics), `docs/evidence/demo_verdicts.md`. Cost per teacher per track: `docs/evidence/cost_per_teacher.md` (a range; assumptions stated).

heading: Slide 12: Roadmap (A)
text: a one-block pilot with a DIET from January 2027, then a district; WhatsApp; IVR; literacy tracks.

heading: Slide 13: Roadmap (B)
text: "Beyond Grade 3 maths", the topic-pack anatomy (`docs/roadmap.md`). Integration with state assessment data, UDISE+ identifiers, existing training records.

heading: Slide 14: What we cut, and what we need
text: The cuts, each logged (`docs/build/PARKING.md`). Needed from partners: a block, a DIET, schools that agree to the pre-test, a coach and an officer.

heading: Video 00:00 Problem
text: In most blocks, training is the same for every teacher, rarely practised, and nobody checks what changed. (FLN 54, 56: five-State study; the 75% figure is one State.) On screen: Title card, then two figures from the evidence slide

heading: Video 00:15 The idea
text: Cohort Coach groups teachers by the specific mistake their pupils make. On screen: The check: a teacher photographs ten children's sheets

heading: Video 00:35 Counts from code
text: The class counts come from code. Claude reads handwriting; it never computes a number. On screen: The error card: "11 of 28 children take the smaller digit from the larger"

heading: Video 00:55 Cohorts and mentors
text: Teachers who share a mistake form a cohort, with a mentor whose class fixed it. On screen: The coach's cohort list; the thread with a made-up child name refused

heading: Video 01:15 Gates and review
text: Each lesson is drafted, then checked by code, by a second model, and by a person. Neither key alone publishes. On screen: The review queue: checks, return with a reason, coach key then officer key

heading: Video 01:40 The lesson
text: The lesson reaches her in the app as a voice lesson, with the badge and two taps; Telegram is on the roadmap. On screen: The lesson page: lesson 1, "Tried it in class?"

heading: Video 02:00 Practice Class
text: Before she tries it on children, she rehearses with five simulated children who make her class's mistakes. This is a hypothesis; the pilot tests it. On screen: The Practice Class, one turn, with the AI-layers overlay

heading: Video 02:25 Results
text: The next check says whether children improved, against a comparison group. A failed track counts against the track, not the teacher. On screen: The officer's results: one working, one not, one hidden under 5 classes

heading: Video 02:45 Close
text: Open source. Everything shown is simulated or labelled. Thank you. On screen: Repo and README, "Where AI is used"
